apollo.title: How to Counter Apollo in Deadlock | Items & Strategy

apollo.sub: Learn how to counter Apollo in Deadlock. Compare items for his mobility and spirit burst, bait Riposte, and plan your response to his ultimate.
lane: Test Riposte with gunfire or a low-risk attack instead of opening with your strongest ability.
Trade after the defensive cooldown is spent, and keep stamina for his return engage.

An early Slowing Hex is useful when mobility is denying your lane’s kill attempts.
fight: **Land movement denial when allies can immediately follow up.** If he cleanses the first application, hold a second control source for the escape.
When he commits his ultimate in open space, move toward your team or your side of the map so the commitment leaves him exposed.

Situational response
Consider Slowing Hex when fighting Apollo if Flawless Advance lets him escape your damage. Buy it when denying that movement would create a kill window your team can use.

Choose it when a large spirit-damage hit is the reason you die before responding. Its conditional protection has a cooldown and does not negate every part of the combo.

Time the spell parry for the actual damage, rather than the first setup cue. Apollo can delay his commitment until your protection ends.

Consider Spirit Sap when Apollo’s Spirit-scaling damage is deciding trades and your team can return spirit damage.

faq: What is Apollo’s biggest weakness?

Apollo becomes easier to punish after Riposte or his movement is spent. Test the defensive response with a low-risk attack, then commit when he cannot freely answer or escape. Slowing Hex is valuable when denying Flawless Advance gives your team an immediate finish window.
What should you buy first against Apollo in lane?

Slowing Hex is the lane option when Apollo’s movement keeps denying kill attempts. Apply it before his movement sequence and have damage ready. Test Riposte with gunfire or a small commitment first; spending your strongest ability into his defensive response can waste the opening before the hex matters.
Which counter items matter against Apollo later in the game?

Choose Spirit Resilience for repeated spirit damage or Spellbreaker when Apollo’s opening burst decides the exchange. Add coordinated cast denial if he cleanses your movement lock and escapes. Silence Wave or Cursed Relic needs allied damage ready; buying more control without follow-up may only delay the reset.
Should you buy bullet or spirit resistance against Apollo?

Spirit protection is the more relevant defense when Apollo’s front-loaded combo is taking your health. Spirit Resilience works across repeated exchanges, while Spellbreaker addresses a large conditional burst hit. These purchases help you survive; movement denial and coordinated damage are still needed to stop Flawless Advance from rescuing him.
How do you respond to Apollo’s ultimate?

Counterspell answers the damaging part of Apollo’s ultimate when you can read the timing. Save it for the actual hit rather than the earliest setup cue. Apollo can delay his commitment, so an early activation may end before the damage arrives. Spirit defense is steadier when that reaction is unreliable.
Do anti-heal items work against Apollo?

Anti-heal is only a priority against Apollo when healing or lifesteal is actually preventing your team’s finish. Use Slowing Hex before Apollo starts Flawless Advance, then focus him while that escape is unavailable.
What can you cleanse or remove in the Apollo matchup?

The Apollo plan uses timed protection and movement denial rather than treating Dispel Magic as an ultimate cleanse. Save Counterspell for the damage window. If Apollo cleanses your Slowing Hex, layer another control source or Silence Wave during a commitment your team can punish.
What positioning mistakes should you avoid against Apollo?

Test Riposte with gunfire or a low-risk attack instead of opening with your strongest ability. Trade after the defensive cooldown is spent, and keep stamina for his return engage. Land movement denial when allies can immediately follow up.

What should you buy first against Baba in lane?

Rebuttal fits Baba’s repeated kicks and ground slams when you can read the parry. Dispel Magic is relevant when Threadsap or Brew debuffs prevent a useful return trade. Take cover after Threadsap instead of forcing a weakened spell combo into empowered gunfire; the item should support that reset.

Plan an interrupt or timed protection for Feed the Birds instead of expecting one cleanse to answer both threats.

Take cover after Threadsap lands rather than forcing a weakened spell combo into her empowered shots. Parry Granny Long Legs when you can read the attack. The kick stuns Baba when parried; the ground slam can be blocked without stunning her.

deadman-danny.title: How to Counter Deadman Danny in Deadlock | Items & Strategy
deadman-danny.meta: Counter Deadman Danny in Deadlock with anti-air, spirit defense and safer positioning. Find items for Strix Salvo, Jettison Fuel and Close The Deal.
deadman-danny.sub: Counter Deadman Danny in Deadlock with anti-air, spirit defense and safer positioning. Find items for Strix Salvo, Jettison Fuel and Close The Deal.
lane: Move out of Strix Salvo’s missile line before its delayed explosions. A mark makes the next charged shot more dangerous, so break the firing angle rather than extending the same trade.
Use bridges, doorways and overhead cover to limit his aerial shots. Keep stamina for leaving the missile line or a visible landing, rather than spending every dash on poke.
Leave Jettison Fuel’s spray instead of standing through weapon damage and Bullet Resist reduction. Its finishing backblast deals spirit damage, so bullet protection is not the whole answer.

Avoid Chimera Mk1’s landing blast. If he overheats and hits no hero, his self-stun creates a punish window while the jetpack cools. Jettison Fuel vents heat when it deals damage, so watch the actual landing and follow-up before chasing.
fight: Track his aerial approach without bunching up beneath it. Use overhead cover and reserve movement for the landing or close-range grab.
Use Knockdown on an exposed airborne Danny early enough for its delayed stun to land. Coordinate damage during the catch; do not treat the delay as an instant rescue after Close The Deal has started.
Land Silence Wave or Cursed Relic before his next cast when your team is ready to focus him. Denying the next engage is a different job from trying to cancel an ultimate that already grabbed someone.
Retreat earlier when low: Close The Deal deals extra damage to enemies below half health. Keep a teammate close enough to respond, while giving each other room to avoid the same landing explosion.
Respect his death explosion. After finishing him, move away from the body rather than standing over it at low health.

Prepare Unstoppable before the grab or landing control, or keep Indomitable’s automatic response available for the catch. Reactive Barrier protects follow-up after control; Dispel Magic is for eligible non-ultimate debuffs such as fuel resistance shred.
glance: Deadman Danny combines aerial angles with marked-target burst and a close-range grab. Keep cover above you, leave missile lines early, and make him commit his landing away from your team. Spirit defense answers much of his ability damage; fuel spray and bullet-resistance reduction create a separate weapon threat.
Deny the aerial angle and punish a missed landing while his movement is unavailable.
Start with the damage or catch costing you fights, then add a coordinated anti-air or cast-denial response.
roleText: Pressure from an aerial angle, mark a target, then commit a dive or grab when the finish is available.

Buy Spirit Shielding when repeated spirit follow-up leaves you too low to keep farming. It is a smaller lane investment before committing to sustained spirit resistance.
Its triggered barrier helps absorb follow-up spirit pressure after a qualifying hit. It does not remove a mark or replace stepping out of the missile line.
His landing stun leads to lethal follow-up

Lane
Choose Reactive Barrier when a landing stun repeatedly turns into a losing lane trade. Buy for the damage after the catch rather than expecting it to prevent the engage.
An automatic barrier can cushion follow-up after qualifying control. It does not stop Close The Deal from grabbing you or move you away from the landing.
You run out of movement before his missiles or landing arrive
Extra Stamina
Lane
Buy Extra Stamina when you regularly spend your movement before Danny commits his missile line, fuel spray or landing. Keep the extra dash available for that threat.
Another movement option helps you leave a delayed missile line or change angle before a dive connects. It is useful before you lose your actions, not an escape button during the grab.
He keeps shooting safely from the air
Knockdown
Mid Game
Buy Knockdown when Danny’s exposed aerial position lets him deal damage without a team response. Your allies should be close enough to use the delayed catch.

The delayed stun gives your team a control window against an exposed airborne target. Cast before the dangerous commit and check his protection; it is not an instant answer once you have already been grabbed.
Missile burst and the ultimate take too much of your health
Spirit Resilience
Mid Game
Build Spirit Resilience when Strix Salvo, landing explosions or Close The Deal repeatedly force you out of fights. Choose it for recurring spirit damage across several exchanges.

Passive spirit protection reduces the damage side of his ability pressure, including the spirit-damage ultimate. It does not prevent the grab, shorten the flight sequence or protect against the weapon-damage fuel spray.
He gets another dive or grab off before you can finish him
Silence Wave
Mid Game
Buy Silence Wave when your team can focus Danny but his next ability keeps extending the fight. Use the denial window with allied damage ready.
Land it before the cast you want to deny. It helps create a finish window; do not assume silence cancels Close The Deal after a target has already been grabbed.
Jettison Fuel and weapon fire are winning the trade

Mid Game
Consider Metal Skin when fuel spray and weapon pressure are the part actually killing you. Activate for the committed bullet-damage window and move toward cover.

Bullet immunity addresses weapon-damage pressure, but the fuel backblast, missile spirit damage and Close The Deal still need another response. It does not remove Bullet Resist reduction already applied.

Late Game

Choose around the response you need. Debuff Reducer shortens eligible effects across exchanges, Indomitable responds automatically to qualifying control, and Unstoppable protects a planned commitment when activated in time. None of them answers every part of her kit.

Knockdown offers a delayed catch, while Silence Wave can deny her next cast. Neither is a reliable way to stop an active Still Life, and neither removes ink already placed.

Do not expect Dispel Magic to remove Wraith’s ultimate control. The plan uses prepared Unstoppable or a timed response to the incoming Telekinesis application. Plated Armor and gun defense address repeated weapon pressure, but neither means a controlled target can freely activate any item after the catch.

Avoid long exposed peeks that give Wraith easy weapon hits and card value. Keep moving and use elevation to make card angles less predictable. Prepare Unstoppable before control removes your activation window, or use a timed response you can execute reliably.

counterspell.name: Counterspell
counterspell.title: Counterspell in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
counterspell.meta: Learn how to use Counterspell in Deadlock to block ability damage and effects with parry. Explore defensive timing, hero matchups and alternatives.
counterspell.sub: Counterspell rewards reading an enemy's commitment. By upgrading your parry to block ability damage and effects during its protection window, it lets you turn a predictable burst or control attempt into a missed opportunity for the opponent.
counterspell.who: Players comfortable responding to a readable ability commitment with a prepared parry.
counterspell.when: Prepare the parry for the dangerous ability or damage window. The strongest use is blocking the part of the sequence that would otherwise decide the exchange.
counterspell.example: Against Apollo: Time Counterspell for the actual damage window of the ultimate. Correct timing can negate the ability damage and effects even after the sequence has started.
counterspell.watch: Using the response too early can waste the window. Sudden catches and repeated control may require a different defensive plan.
counterspell.buy: Buy it when a readable ability repeatedly decides your fights and you can react with parry. If the catch happens before you can respond, compare automatic control protection instead.
counterspell.bestIntro: Telegraphed burst or control sequences where you can read and react to the commitment.
best: apollo#problem-3
His ultimate is finishing you after the slow-motion setup
Time Counterspell for the actual damage window of the ultimate.
Correct timing can negate the ability damage and effects even after the sequence has started.
billy#problem-2
His ultimate grab keeps converting into a kill
Counterspell the pull or use Unstoppable/Ethereal Shift.
The ultimate is telegraphed enough to answer if you keep the defensive tool available.
drifter#problem-3
His ultimate is about to land on you
Preemptively Counterspell the obvious ultimate timing.
The animation is readable enough to protect yourself before the burst and effects connect.
infernus#problem-2
His ultimate stun is deciding teamfights
Counterspell the telegraphed explosion or Warp Stone out of range.
The wind-up gives you a real reaction window if you preserve the defensive tool.
ivy#problem-1
Stone Form is stunning you for easy follow-up
Counterspell the Stone Form impact.
The ability is telegraphed enough to parry, removing both the damage and the control that normally sets up the next hit.
lady-geist#problem-1
She is low health but threatens a fight-winning health swap
Counterspell the swap or silence her before she can cast it.
Chasing a low Geist is dangerous specifically because Soul Exchange can reverse the health bars instantly.
alts: Indomitable

Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.
Unstoppable

Unstoppable protects a planned commitment from crowd control. Activate it before the dangerous control sequence begins, especially when repeated disables would stop you from completing an engage or dealing damage. You still need a position that survives the incoming damage.
Ethereal Shift

Ethereal Shift lets you sit out a dangerous moment through brief invulnerability and untargetability. Against a committed burst or a short ultimate window, the goal is to waste the enemy's investment and return with a plan for your next position.
counterspell.short: Upgrades parry to block ability damage and effects.

divine-barrier.name: Divine Barrier
divine-barrier.title: Divine Barrier in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
divine-barrier.meta: Use Divine Barrier in Deadlock to shield an ally and clear removable debuffs. Learn when to buy it, how to time a save and which defensive items to compare.
divine-barrier.sub: Divine Barrier turns a defensive purchase into a teammate save. Its shield and debuff purge can protect an ally during a dangerous sequence, including removable bomb pressure, when you keep a clear view and a usable save angle.
divine-barrier.who: Players who need to protect an ally through burst or a removable debuff sequence.
divine-barrier.when: Keep an ally-save angle available and use the shield or cleanse when the threatened teammate can still benefit from the response.
divine-barrier.example: Against Bebop: Use Divine Barrier on the bombed teammate. It can cleanse removable non-stun debuffs from an ally, making it one of the best team-save answers when the bomb is on someone other than you.
divine-barrier.watch: An ally-save purchase needs attention to the teammate and their position. It does not remove the need to prevent the next catch or follow-up.
divine-barrier.buy: Consider it when a teammate is repeatedly targeted and an ally shield or cleanse would change the outcome. Choose a buyer who can watch that teammate and remain in position to use it.
divine-barrier.bestIntro: Burst and debuff setups where a teammate needs immediate protection.
best: bebop#problem-4
A teammate is stuck with Bebop Sticky Bomb
Use Divine Barrier on the bombed teammate.
It can cleanse removable non-stun debuffs from an ally, making it one of the best team-save answers when the bomb is on someone other than you.
pocket#problem-4
Pocket Affliction is on a teammate and they need an immediate save
Use Divine Barrier on the afflicted ally.
It can cleanse eligible negative effects from a teammate and is the team-oriented answer when Counterspell only protects the person who bought it.
alts: Rescue Beam

Rescue Beam combines healing with a positional teammate save. The pull can remove an ally from the enemy's ongoing damage angle, so a good rescue depends as much on where you bring them as on how much health they recover.
Dispel Magic

Dispel Magic resets a fight weighed down by removable non-ultimate debuffs. Use it to clear effects such as Bebop's Sticky Bomb before detonation, then reposition or recommit with the debuff gone. Its activation restrictions are part of the decision.
Reactive Barrier

Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.
divine-barrier.short: Shields an ally and purges removable debuffs.

return-fire.name: Return Fire
return-fire.title: Return Fire in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
return-fire.meta: Learn when to buy Return Fire in Deadlock to reflect damage during trades you can survive. Compare defensive synergy, matchups and alternatives to reflection.
return-fire.sub: Return Fire punishes enemies for damaging you during an exchange you can survive. It suits durable brawlers facing sustained pressure: combine the reflection with appropriate defense so the opponent pays for continuing to shoot instead of simply winning the damage race.
return-fire.who: Durable brawlers who can survive incoming pressure and punish the opponent for continuing to hit them.
return-fire.when: Use it during a damage exchange you can survive, especially when sustained gun pressure makes reflection valuable.
return-fire.example: Against Silver: Use Return Fire during the sustained human-form weapon trade. Her rapid gun pattern can reflect meaningful damage back into her, especially on heroes that already have enough durability to stay in the exchange.
return-fire.watch: Reflected damage does not remove the incoming threat. Pair it with suitable defense and do not rely on it to win a damage race you cannot live through.
return-fire.buy: Buy it when you already have the durability to stay alive through incoming damage and reflection would punish sustained attacks. It is a follow-through purchase, not a replacement for the defense you need to survive.
return-fire.bestIntro: Sustained damage trades where opponents keep attacking into your defensive window.
best: silver#problem-4
Silver human-form gun pressure is punishing you before wolf form even starts
Use Return Fire during the sustained human-form weapon trade.
Her rapid gun pattern can reflect meaningful damage back into her, especially on heroes that already have enough durability to stay in the exchange.
vyper#problem-1
Her rapid-fire weapon pressure is melting you
Use Return Fire if you are already durable, or Metal Skin if survival is the only goal.
Vyper fires enough shots to punish herself heavily into Return Fire, while Metal Skin simply blanks the bullets.
alts: Metal Skin

Metal Skin gives you a temporary bullet-immunity window against decisive weapon pressure. Against a gun carry, activate it for the dangerous commitment and use that time to reach cover or let allies respond; it does not remove debuffs already on you.
Plated Armor

Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.
Disarming Hex

Disarming Hex stops a target from firing their weapon, creating breathing room against gun-focused carries. It is particularly useful when your team wants to keep fighting through the enemy's damage window rather than only protect one player.
return-fire.short: Reflects incoming damage during exchanges you can survive.

weapon-shielding.name: Weapon Shielding
weapon-shielding.title: Weapon Shielding in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
weapon-shielding.meta: Learn when to buy Weapon Shielding in Deadlock for a barrier after weapon burst. Compare gun-pressure matchups, defensive timing and alternative items.
weapon-shielding.sub: Weapon Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of weapon damage, helping absorb follow-up pressure. Use that shield window to reach cover or return a manageable trade instead of staying exposed until the next burst overwhelms you.
weapon-shielding.who: Laning players who need a shield response to repeated gun poke and want room to stabilize.
weapon-shielding.when: Use the shield window to take cover, improve spacing, or return a manageable trade before the next weapon exchange.
weapon-shielding.example: Against Drifter: Use a weapon-triggered barrier to stabilize the gun follow-up. A cleanse is a separate answer to the mark that enables the teleport.
weapon-shielding.watch: Weapon damage is the trigger; the resulting barrier can absorb other incoming damage too. If that trigger is unreliable in the matchup, compare a different defensive tool rather than assuming the barrier will always be available.
weapon-shielding.buy: Consider it when weapon poke repeatedly starts the enemy's winning trade and reliably triggers the barrier. If the lane is ability-led, compare Spirit Shielding or another defense suited to that damage.
weapon-shielding.bestIntro: Early weapon poke and gun-led lane pressure.
best: drifter
His catch is followed by heavy weapon pressure
Use a weapon-triggered barrier to stabilize the gun follow-up. A cleanse is a separate answer to the mark that enables the teleport.
alts: Plated Armor

Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.
Reactive Barrier

Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.
Escalating Resilience

Escalating Resilience rewards weapon users who can keep shooting through a longer exchange. Its bullet resistance builds as you attack, helping you hold your ground against sustained gun pressure while continuing to contribute damage.

spirit-sap.name: Spirit Sap
spirit-sap.title: Spirit Sap in Deadlock: Counters, Uses & When to Buy
spirit-sap.meta: Learn when to buy Spirit Sap in Deadlock, which hero matchups suit it, and how to weaken Spirit-scaling damage while setting up allied spell pressure.
spirit-sap.sub: Spirit Sap reduces one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist. Apply it before a spell trade to weaken their Spirit-scaling output and help allied spirit damage land harder.
spirit-sap.who: Players who can safely target a threatening caster before the exchange, especially when their own hero or a teammate can follow up with spirit damage.
spirit-sap.when: Apply before the enemy’s next spell exchange, then use the affected target’s lower Spirit Resist. Keep a safe position; crossing an exposed firing lane just to apply the active can cost more than it gains.
spirit-sap.example: Against Baba: use Spirit Sap before a spell trade when her Spirit-scaling pressure is deciding the exchange. Coordinate allied spirit damage while she is affected, and keep a separate response for Threadsap, melee pressure or control.
spirit-sap.watch: Spirit Power reduction is not a flat reduction to all incoming damage. It does not silence, disarm, cleanse an effect on you or apply anti-heal. Do not assume it changes damage already applied, damage stored by a previous cast or existing summons without verifying the interaction.
spirit-sap.buy: Consider it early when a specific enemy’s Spirit-scaling damage is winning trades and your side can use the resistance reduction. Keep it useful in mid-game skirmishes by applying it immediately before coordinated pressure. It is less compelling when the decisive problem is weapon damage, an unavoidable catch, or a target your team cannot reach.
spirit-sap.bestIntro: These illustrate the targeted trade Spirit Sap can support. They are editorial examples, not a win-rate ranking or a claim that every build needs the item.

Consider Spirit Sap when Threadsap-enhanced pressure or another Spirit-scaling part of Baba’s build is deciding the exchange.

Apply before his next shot window when you can target him safely, then return damage from cover. It does not block the shot, ground him or stop his ultimate; do not cross an exposed lane just to cast it.
kelvin
His Spirit-scaling beam pressure is winning exchanges
Consider Spirit Sap when Kelvin’s own spell damage is keeping you out of the fight and allied spirit damage can punish him.

Apply before the next connected exchange, then break the beam angle if it remains unsafe. Spirit Sap does not cancel the beam, remove the slow or replace anti-heal when recovery inside Frozen Shelter prevents a finish.

Her repeated Spirit-scaling pressure is costing you trades
Consider Spirit Sap when Mina’s Spirit-scaling ability pressure is deciding the exchange and your team can return spirit damage.

Apply before the next trade while she is targetable. Keep a separate response for movement that denies your finish; Spirit Sap does not silence her escape or automatically answer weapon-focused damage.

Consider Spirit Sap when Violet’s Spirit-scaling damage is deciding trades and your side can follow up with spirit damage.

Apply before the next exchange and attack from a covered angle. It does not cancel Still Life, remove drawn strokes or prevent Abstract Landscape’s exit effects. Keep a separate response when control rather than damage is deciding the fight.
alts: Spirit Shielding
Grants a barrier after a burst of spirit damage.
Spirit Resilience
Passive resistance against recurring spirit damage.
Spellbreaker
Adds spirit defense and periodic protection against a large spirit hit.
Silence Wave

spirit-sap.short: Reduce one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist.
why: Weaken a target’s Spirit-scaling output before the next exchange
Help allied spirit damage against the same target
faq: What does Spirit Sap do in Deadlock?

Spirit Sap is a targeted active that reduces one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist. It combines a way to weaken Spirit-scaling output with a way to improve allied spirit damage against the same target.
When should you buy Spirit Sap?

Consider it early when a specific enemy’s Spirit-scaling damage is winning trades and you or a teammate can follow up with spirit damage. It can remain useful in mid-game skirmishes, but does not replace the response to weapon pressure, hard control or healing.
Does Spirit Sap reduce all spirit damage?

It reduces the target’s Spirit Power; that is not the same as reducing all spirit damage by a fixed percentage. The benefit depends on how the relevant effect scales. Do not assume it changes previously applied damage or existing summons without checking the interaction.
Is Spirit Sap better than Spirit Resilience?

They do different jobs. Spirit Sap requires you to target one enemy and use the debuff window; Spirit Resilience provides passive personal spirit protection. Compare whether your next fight needs a coordinated trade tool or more dependable protection through repeated damage.
Does Spirit Sap stop abilities or remove debuffs?

Spirit Sap is not silence, an interrupt or a cleanse. Reducing Spirit Power does not mean the target cannot cast. Keep a separate response when preventing a cast or removing an eligible effect is the important job.
Which heroes does Spirit Sap counter?

It is a situational trade option into Spirit-scaling threats such as Baba, Grey Talon, Mina and Violet when your side can follow up with spirit damage. The enemy’s build and the timing of the trade matter more than treating every ability user as the same matchup.
Is Spirit Sap an anti-heal item?

No. Do not treat Spirit Power reduction as a healing-reduction debuff. Choose a reliable anti-heal source when recovery is preventing the finish; any effect on a particular Spirit-scaling heal is a separate interaction to verify.
What does Spirit Sap upgrade into?
Spirit Sap builds into Focus Lens. Choose that larger investment for the job its current active needs to do in your match, rather than upgrading automatically because you bought the component.

slowing-hex.name: Slowing Hex
slowing-hex.title: Slowing Hex in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
slowing-hex.meta: Learn when to buy Slowing Hex in Deadlock to slow enemies and disable affected movement abilities. Compare escape-denial timing, matchups and alternatives.
slowing-hex.sub: Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.
slowing-hex.who: Players whose team can finish a target once a specific movement option is denied.
slowing-hex.when: Use it before the relevant movement skill and while allies can follow up. Against Kelvin, apply it before Ice Path; against Mina or Mirage, be ready to follow up after a cleanse.
slowing-hex.example: Against Apollo: Use Slowing Hex before he starts the movement sequence. It shuts off a large portion of Apollo's mobility and makes his commit much easier to punish.
slowing-hex.watch: It does not disable every movement tool, including The Doorman's Doorway. Movement that has already started may require a different response.
slowing-hex.buy: Buy it when a particular movement ability repeatedly lets an enemy dive and leave safely. Check that the ability is affected and prioritize the purchase before another uncontested escape.
slowing-hex.bestIntro: Mobile targets whose escape depends on a movement skill affected by Slowing Hex.
best: apollo#problem-1
Apollo mobility and Flawless Advance keep letting him escape
Use Slowing Hex before he starts the movement sequence.
It shuts off a large portion of Apollo's mobility and makes his commit much easier to punish.
billy#problem-4
Billy keeps using Rising Ram to disengage after every trade
Apply Slowing Hex before or as Billy commits.
Denying the movement ability turns his normal hit-and-run pattern into a much riskier all-in and gives your team time to punish him.
calico#problem-1
She keeps diving and escaping before your team can finish her
Apply Slowing Hex before the mobility chain.
Calico loses most of the movement tools that let her commit and leave safely.
holliday#problem-2
She keeps chaining jump pads to escape or find barrel angles
Apply Slowing Hex before she uses the jump pad.
It prevents the movement ability and removes the mobility that makes her so difficult to pin down.
kelvin#problem-4
Kelvin keeps starting Ice Path before your team can stop him
Apply Slowing Hex before Ice Path is active.
The timing matters—using the anti-mobility item before he establishes the path is much more effective than trying to shut it down after he is already airborne.
lash#problem-2
He keeps escaping after starting fights
Apply Slowing Hex after he commits.
Removing his movement options turns the dive from a safe hit-and-run into a punishable overextension.
alts: Knockdown

Knockdown gives your team a delayed stun to punish airborne targets and interrupt vulnerable channels. The delay is the key detail: cast while there is still time for the stun to land, and have damage ready when the target is controlled.
Capacitor

Capacitor combines weapon-build value with a targeted catch. Its projectile slows an enemy, prevents stamina usage, and restricts movement abilities and items, giving your team a window to punish a target that normally escapes.
Silence Wave

Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.
slowing-hex.short: Slows the target and disables affected movement abilities.
why: Stop recasts of move tools like Apollo's 2

plated-armor.who: Players facing repeated weapon hits and on-hit buildup who want passive protection rather than relying only on an active immunity window.
plated-armor.when: Choose it when repeated weapon on-hit buildup is deciding the exchange. Its chances to prevent on-hit application can slow the pressure from Haze, Infernus, or Mina before you reach the next dangerous trade.

silence-wave.name: Silence Wave
silence-wave.title: Silence Wave in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
silence-wave.meta: Learn how to use Silence Wave in Deadlock before an enemy’s escape or defensive cast. Compare timing, hero matchups and other cast-denial options.
silence-wave.sub: Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.
silence-wave.who: Players creating a team window before an enemy escape or defensive ability is cast.
silence-wave.when: Land the silence before the important ability starts, then commit while the target's cast options are restricted.
silence-wave.example: Against Apollo: Layer Silence Wave after his cleanse or when he commits. If Apollo removes the first movement lock, a silence creates a second shutdown window and prevents him from immediately chaining the abilities that let him escape.
silence-wave.watch: Silence alone does not cancel a channel that has already started unless the source also interrupts. Use a interrupt when that is the required job.
silence-wave.buy: Buy it when an escape or defensive ability keeps denying a kill and a direct silence would let your team finish. For a channel that has already begun, check whether you need an interrupt instead.
silence-wave.bestIntro: Ability-dependent targets whose next defensive or movement cast will decide the exchange.
best: apollo#problem-4
Apollo cleanses Slowing Hex and escapes anyway

alts: Cursed Relic

Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.
Silencer

Silencer turns sustained weapon hits into pressure against ability-reliant enemies, reducing outgoing spirit damage and building toward silence. It fits gun users who can stay on a target long enough to restrict the cast that would otherwise turn the fight.
Slowing Hex

Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.

scourge.name: Scourge
scourge.title: Scourge in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
scourge.meta: Explore Scourge in Deadlock for resistance and close-range maximum-health damage. Learn when to buy it against high-health targets and compare alternatives.
scourge.sub: Scourge pairs defensive resistance with a close-range aura that damages enemies based on maximum health. It suits heroes who can stay near a large-health target without losing the fight simply to maintain aura uptime.
scourge.who: Close-range players who can remain near a high-health enemy long enough to use the aura.
scourge.when: Use its durability and aura during a close fight you can safely maintain. The percentage-health damage has a clear purpose against a large health pool.
scourge.watch: The aura needs proximity. Chasing into an unsafe area for uptime can cost more than the purchase contributes.
scourge.buyNotes: Consider the slot and the core item you would delay. This purchase should solve a repeated, important threat while still fitting your hero’s damage or team role.
scourge.buy: Consider it when a high-health enemy is difficult to finish and your hero naturally fights nearby. Make sure your build can hold that distance safely before investing in an aura that needs proximity.
scourge.bestIntro: High-health targets you can pressure at close range; Rat King is the direct recommendation.
alts: Siphon Bullets

Siphon Bullets creates a temporary health swing through repeated weapon hits, stealing a percentage of the enemy's maximum health. Against a large-health target, sustained contact and a coordinated finish help convert that temporary advantage before the stolen health returns.
Tank Buster

Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.
Decay

Decay gives you a direct way to put healing reduction on a sustain target, alongside current-health damage over time. It suits fights where you need anti-heal applied deliberately before the enemy starts winning the health trade.
scourge.short: Adds resistance and a close-range maximum-health damage aura.
why: Percentage-health damage punishes huge health pools
Adds durability while you stay close enough to pressure

healing-rite.name: Healing Rite
healing-rite.title: Healing Rite in Deadlock: Uses & When to Buy
healing-rite.meta: Use Healing Rite in Deadlock to recover health during safe windows between fights. Learn when to buy it and compare lane sustain and recovery options.
healing-rite.sub: Healing Rite helps you recover between fights and return to lane with enough health to contest farm. It works best when you can step out of the enemy's pressure, complete the recovery safely, and avoid returning to the same exposed angle.
healing-rite.who: Laning players who have a safe recovery opportunity and need health back before returning to farm.
healing-rite.when: Find a safe window for the channel, recover, then return from a position that reduces the next poke exchange.
healing-rite.watch: A channelled recovery tool needs a usable window. It is not an immediate answer to the burst that is already killing you.
healing-rite.buy: Buy it during a difficult lane when you have safe recovery windows but cannot afford to keep leaving farm. It will not solve a burst that kills you before you can get out.
healing-rite.bestIntro: Lane attrition where a safe reset can restore useful farming time.
alts: Extra Regen

Extra Regen is a lane-stabilizing purchase for health lost between trades. The value comes from staying available to last-hit and contest souls: recover behind cover, adjust your angle, and avoid giving back the same health to free poke.
Restorative Locket

Restorative Locket turns accumulated stacks into a self-heal, helping you stay present through repeated exchanges. The reset is most useful when it gives you enough health to keep farming or rejoin a fight from a better angle.

alts: Spirit Resilience

Spirit Resilience provides consistent passive protection against spirit damage. It helps when abilities keep wearing you down across multiple exchanges, giving you a baseline defense while you focus on positioning, cooldowns, and your own contribution to the fight.
Spellbreaker

Solomon.summary: Solomon wants you to fight on ground he has already prepared. Change angle, bait a piece move and attack during the gap before he can reposition it again. Your defensive buy should address either the spirit damage or the control that keeps you on his squares.
lane: Poke from outside activated Bishop squares and change your firing angle so he has to move pieces to reach you.
Use another elevation when it gives a cleaner shot. Do not assume nearby trucks block Bishop pressure.
Trade after Bishop movement is spent, watching the piece indicators before committing.
Clear the wave before challenging tower pressure, then approach Solomon from a safe angle. Early spirit protection helps if you cannot keep enough health to farm.
gameplay: Leave activated squares instead of continuing the same trade. Bishop's final upgrade adds stacking spirit-resistance reduction, making repeated exposure more costly.
Watch Rook's reflection and perpendicular split before choosing a retreat path. Keep movement for the follow-up rather than dodging only the first line.
Hold important damage through Kingside Knight's invulnerable movement, then pressure after the protection is spent. Its upgraded self-move can also clear debuffs.
sits: Rook’s immobilization or Queen’s stun sets up my death
Reactive Barrier

If Solomon’s Rook immobilizes you or Queen stuns you into lethal follow-up, Reactive Barrier gives you protection after the catch. Use that breathing room to leave his prepared squares; the barrier does not remove the control.
I survive the opening spell hit but die to the follow-up
Spirit Shielding
Choose Spirit Shielding when you survive Solomon’s first spirit hit but die to the damage that follows. Its triggered barrier buys time to leave his piece setup; it cannot undo the opening hit.
Repeated slows and control leave me exposed too long
Debuff Reducer

If Solomon’s slows, Rook immobilization or Queen stun keep you on dangerous squares too long, Debuff Reducer shortens those effects. Move off the prepared ground as soon as you regain movement; it does not absorb the damage.
Repeated spirit damage keeps forcing me out of fights
Spirit Resilience

Choose Spirit Resilience when repeated damage from Solomon’s pieces keeps forcing you out of fights. Passive spirit resistance helps you stay healthy between exchanges, but you still need to leave dangerous Bishop squares and avoid the control setup.
An opening disable stops my response in important fights
Indomitable

Consider Indomitable when Solomon’s opening Rook or Queen disable prevents you from reacting. Its automatic response can give you a chance to act, but another qualifying disable can consume it first; it does not protect through every follow-up.
Bishop or Rook debuffs stop me escaping or trading back
Dispel Magic

Use Dispel Magic when eligible Bishop or Rook debuffs stop you escaping Solomon’s prepared ground. Clear the effect, then change angle or elevation. It does not remove his deployed pieces or cleanse an already applied Queen stun.

Reactive Barrier: Rook’s immobilization or Queen’s stun sets up my death

If Solomon’s Rook immobilizes you or Queen stuns you into lethal follow-up, Reactive Barrier gives you protection after the catch. Use that breathing room to leave his prepared squares; the barrier does not remove the control.
Spirit Shielding: I survive the opening spell hit but die to the follow-up
Choose Spirit Shielding when you survive Solomon’s first spirit hit but die to the damage that follows. Its triggered barrier buys time to leave his piece setup; it cannot undo the opening hit.
Debuff Reducer: Repeated slows and control leave me exposed too long

If Solomon’s slows, Rook immobilization or Queen stun keep you on dangerous squares too long, Debuff Reducer shortens those effects. Move off the prepared ground as soon as you regain movement; it does not absorb the damage.
Spirit Resilience: Repeated spirit damage keeps forcing me out of fights

Choose Spirit Resilience when repeated damage from Solomon’s pieces keeps forcing you out of fights. Passive spirit resistance helps you stay healthy between exchanges, but you still need to leave dangerous Bishop squares and avoid the control setup.
Spellbreaker: Solomon’s spirit damage is forcing you out of fights

Choose Spellbreaker when a large spirit hit from Solomon’s piece setup takes too much health and shorter debuffs would help you escape. Its burst protection has a cooldown, so keep moving off his squares between activations.
Indomitable: An opening disable stops my response in important fights

Consider Indomitable when Solomon’s opening Rook or Queen disable prevents you from reacting. Its automatic response can give you a chance to act, but another qualifying disable can consume it first; it does not protect through every follow-up.
Unstoppable: Solomon’s control setup leaves you unable to respond

Activate Unstoppable before entering Solomon’s control setup when a Rook root or Queen stun would stop your response. It keeps your actions available during the commitment; it does not make his damaging squares safe to stand on.
Dispel Magic: Bishop or Rook debuffs stop me escaping or trading back

Use Dispel Magic when eligible Bishop or Rook debuffs stop you escaping Solomon’s prepared ground. Clear the effect, then change angle or elevation. It does not remove his deployed pieces or cleanse an already applied Queen stun.

Solomon.extra: Use elevation and unconventional firing angles so Solomon’s prepared squares do not dictate the entire fight. Watch piece movement and cooldown windows, then commit when he cannot immediately rebuild the same bishop or rook pressure.

Violet.summary: Violet uses slows and ink walls to keep you exposed for Still Life’s damage and stun. Stay near cover, leave the brush path early and keep a clear retreat route. Successful empowered shots reduce her cooldowns, so avoid extended trades.
lane: Farm beside solid cover with a route back. Still Life deals damage while Violet looks at its target; completing the sketch adds damage and a stun. Move toward cover when she starts, rather than standing exposed to finish a trade.
Move out of the brush path instead of retreating along it. Flow State slows and damages enemies, and Violet can finish it with a larger-area flick. Leave space between yourself and your lane partner.

Keep movement for her next setup. Living Ink hero hits reduce her ability and item cooldowns, so repeated hits let her keep pressure going. A missed shot is a better time for a short return trade than chasing through her ink.

Choose a lane item for the problem you actually have. Reactive Barrier helps after qualifying control; Spirit Shielding helps with concentrated spirit damage. Extra Stamina is an alternative when reaching cover is the issue. Drawn strokes block movement and projectiles; heavy melee breaks one but damages the attacker.
gameplay: Check your exit before approaching an objective. Avoid letting drawn walls or Abstract Landscape leave your team fighting from one cramped route.

Do not give her team a free fight inside the ultimate. It blocks vision, reveals enemies inside and grants allies Spirit Power. Leaving triggers spirit damage, silence and slow; plan the exit with your team instead of assuming you can cross and immediately cast an escape.
Use separate angles and nearby cover. Make it harder to keep Still Life on an exposed target while splash damage and the brush reach several teammates.
sits: Control is setting up lethal follow-up damage
Reactive Barrier

Consider it when a qualifying control effect leaves you taking more damage before you can reach cover. Its barrier helps you survive the damage that follows Still Life’s stun or the ultimate’s exit effect. It does not prevent the control or remove her ink.
Spirit bursts are costing you lane farm
Spirit Shielding

Consider it when brush hits or spirit splash repeatedly leave you too weak to farm or survive the next attack. Its barrier activates after enough spirit damage arrives in a short window. Use that protection to reach cover or take a safer return trade; it does not prevent a stun or silence.
Repeated status effects keep disrupting your response
Debuff Reducer

Consider it when shorter eligible effects would let you recover your movement or actions sooner across repeated exchanges. Shortens eligible slows, stuns and silences from her abilities. It does not remove the ink area or reduce the damage you take.
A removable effect is preventing your escape or return trade
Dispel Magic

Consider it when an eligible Flow State or Still Life effect repeatedly costs you a useful response. Activate while you can still use items to clear eligible Flow State or Still Life effects. It does not remove the ultimate’s silence, so do not count on it to cancel a whole sketch.
Recurring spirit damage keeps forcing you out of fights
Spirit Resilience

Consider it when several casts, rather than one opening burst, repeatedly drive you out of fights. Passive spirit resistance provides steadier protection through recurring ability pressure. Compare it with Spirit Shielding for concentrated bursts; neither stops control or replaces a safe position.
Control keeps stopping a planned commitment
Unstoppable

Consider it when you need to keep acting through the expected control window during an important fight. Activate before her control lands to keep acting through Flow State, Still Life and Abstract Landscape. It protects against control, not damage, and does not remove existing ink.
A sudden control effect catches you before you can respond
Indomitable

Consider it when a qualifying catch happens too quickly for a dependable active response. Automatically responds to qualifying control from Still Life or Abstract Landscape. It has a cooldown, so another control effect can use it up first.
Slows keep extending a chase
Enduring Speed

Consider it when slowing pressure prevents you reaching cover and lets the enemy keep attacking. Movement speed and slow resistance help repositioning. They do not remove silence or stun and do not bypass the ultimate’s exit effect.
You have no movement left when her setup arrives
Extra Stamina

Consider it when spending stamina on farming or trading leaves no movement for reaching cover or dodging the brush path. Preserve the extra movement for the threat. It does not let you pass through a drawn wall or remove a control effect.
One quick reposition would put you behind cover
Warp Stone

Consider it when you can choose a safer position before control lands. Use a deliberate destination while you can act. Do not assume it bypasses a drawn wall or the ultimate exit trigger. Its bullet resistance does not answer her spirit damage.
You need to deny her next cast during a team attack
Silence Wave

Consider it when your team can reach Violet but her next spell keeps turning the commitment against you. Land the silence before the cast you want to deny and follow up together. Silence will not cancel a Still Life that is already running or remove ink already placed.
Your team needs a stronger action-denial window to finish her
Cursed Relic

Consider it for a coordinated late-game focus when denying her abilities, weapon attacks and item usage would let allies finish the target. Its curse creates a powerful control window but reduces your own damage, so arrange allied follow-up. It does not remove an ultimate area she has already placed or its exit effects.
Her healing is undoing your damage and you can apply spirit damage
Healbane

Consider it only when visible regeneration or lifesteal is preventing a finish and your normal damage can reliably apply anti-heal. Apply spirit damage before the important recovery window. Her regeneration and allied Spirit Lifesteal upgrades can make anti-heal relevant, but this is not an automatic purchase against every Violet build.
Her recovery is extending fights and you can maintain weapon hits
Toxic Bullets

Consider it when healing is deciding the fight and your weapon can reliably build and maintain the effect on the target. Repeated weapon hits apply the healing reduction. Only buy it when her healing is deciding fights, not just because Violet is on the enemy team.
Your team needs a delayed catch to focus her
Knockdown

Consider it when Violet remains in reach but your team lacks a dependable catch and can follow up when the delayed control lands. Cast it with time for the delayed stun to land and have allied damage ready. Treat it as a catch, not a guaranteed way to cancel Still Life.
Her spirit burst is still lethal through your defenses
Spellbreaker

Consider it when Violet’s spirit burst remains lethal despite your existing defenses, especially when shorter status effects would also help. Adds spirit and debuff resistance, plus protection against a qualifying large spirit hit. Check that protection is available before committing; another qualifying hit can consume it first. It does not cancel Still Life or remove her ink.
Her Spirit-scaling pressure is winning your spell trades
Spirit Sap

Consider Spirit Sap when Violet’s Spirit-scaling damage is deciding trades and your side can follow up with spirit damage. Apply before the next exchange and attack from a covered angle. It does not cancel Still Life, remove drawn strokes or prevent Abstract Landscape’s exit effects. Keep a separate response when control rather than damage is deciding the fight.
