Violet.extra: Choose Reactive Barrier for damage after control or Spirit Shielding for spirit bursts. Plan your ultimate exit carefully—crossing its boundary triggers damage, silence and slow.

Siphon Bullets.short: Repeated hits temporarily steal a percentage of enemy maximum health.
Siphon Bullets.desc: Siphon Bullets creates a temporary health swing through repeated weapon hits, stealing a percentage of the enemy's maximum health. Against a large-health target, sustained contact and a coordinated finish help convert that temporary advantage before the stolen health returns.
Siphon Bullets.when: Buy it when you can maintain weapon hits on a high-health opponent during longer fights. If their healing is the larger obstacle, make sure your team also has reliable anti-heal.

Scourge.short: Adds resistance and a close-range maximum-health damage aura.
Scourge.desc: Scourge pairs defensive resistance with a close-range aura that damages enemies based on maximum health. It suits heroes who can stay near a large-health target without losing the fight simply to maintain aura uptime.
Scourge.when: Consider it when a high-health enemy is difficult to finish and your hero naturally fights nearby. Make sure your build can hold that distance safely before investing in an aura that needs proximity.

Cursed Relic.short: Locks enemy actions and strips non-ultimate buffs, but lowers your damage.
Cursed Relic.desc: Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.
Cursed Relic.when: Buy it when an enemy's escape, defensive items, or non-ultimate buffs keep denying your team's finish. Agree on the follow-up first, especially if you would be sacrificing an important carry damage slot.

Indomitable.short: Automatically breaks the next qualifying control effect and grants a barrier.
Indomitable.desc: Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.
Indomitable.when: Consider it when sudden hard control repeatedly starts a lethal follow-up and manual reactions are unreliable. Check which effect will trigger it: a lesser catch can spend the protection before the decisive engage.

Healbane.short: Spirit damage applies anti-heal; affected enemy deaths restore health.
Healbane.desc: Healbane turns your spirit damage into healing reduction, making it a natural counter-buy for ability users facing sustain. Apply it before the enemy gets full value from healing, then use the reduced recovery to help your team secure the kill.
Healbane.when: Buy it when healing starts deciding trades and your normal abilities can reliably reach the target. It is a practical early anti-heal option without needing to build around repeated weapon hits.

Toxic Bullets.short: Repeated weapon hits apply anti-heal and maximum-health bleed.
Toxic Bullets.desc: Toxic Bullets gives weapon users anti-heal and percentage-health bleed after repeated shooting. It fits carries who can keep landing shots on a sustain target, with the application built before the enemy's important healing window.
Toxic Bullets.when: Buy it when you have reliable weapon uptime and enemy healing keeps undoing your damage. If you cannot maintain hits on the target, compare an anti-heal option that fits your actual damage pattern.

Spirit Burn.short: Spirit-damage buildup triggers an explosion, burn, and healing reduction.
Spirit Burn.desc: Spirit Burn rewards builds that can reach its spirit-damage trigger, adding an explosion, damage over time, and healing reduction. It combines damage scaling with anti-sustain pressure, but you must trigger the effect before the enemy's recovery decides the fight.
Spirit Burn.when: Buy it when your spirit build can reliably trigger the burn and you need damage alongside anti-heal. If sustain needs an immediate answer before that investment, compare Healbane or Decay.

Reactive Barrier.short: Automatically grants a shield after a hard-control catch.
Reactive Barrier.desc: Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.
Reactive Barrier.when: Consider it when you survive the catch itself but die to the damage that follows. Its shield helps you endure the combo; choose control prevention if losing your actions is the main problem.

Slowing Hex.short: Slows the target and disables affected movement abilities.
Slowing Hex.desc: Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.
Slowing Hex.when: Buy it when a particular movement ability repeatedly lets an enemy dive and leave safely. Check that the ability is affected and prioritize the purchase before another uncontested escape.

Ethereal Shift.short: Brief invulnerability and untargetability to avoid committed damage.
Ethereal Shift.desc: Ethereal Shift lets you sit out a dangerous moment through brief invulnerability and untargetability. Against a committed burst or a short ultimate window, the goal is to waste the enemy's investment and return with a plan for your next position.
Ethereal Shift.when: Buy it when a specific burst or ultimate window is the reason you die, even after improving your positioning. You need time to activate it and a safe plan for when the protection ends.

Dispel Magic.short: Clears non-ultimate debuffs; unavailable while stunned or slept.
Dispel Magic.desc: Dispel Magic resets a fight weighed down by removable non-ultimate debuffs. Use it to clear effects such as Bebop's Sticky Bomb before detonation, then reposition or recommit with the debuff gone. Its activation restrictions are part of the decision.
Dispel Magic.when: Buy it as soon as a removable debuff repeatedly costs you a trade or a death. Do not wait for a typical purchase minute when a cleanse would let you survive the next bomb or damage-over-time sequence.

Knockdown.short: Delayed stun for grounding flyers or interrupting vulnerable channels.
Knockdown.desc: Knockdown gives your team a delayed stun to punish airborne targets and interrupt vulnerable channels. The delay is the key detail: cast while there is still time for the stun to land, and have damage ready when the target is controlled.
Knockdown.when: Buy it when a flying enemy or interruptible channel is repeatedly taking over fights. Confirm your team can follow up and that immunity will not protect the target when the delayed stun arrives.

Counterspell.short: Upgrades parry to block ability damage and effects.
Counterspell.desc: Counterspell rewards reading an enemy's commitment. By upgrading your parry to block ability damage and effects during its protection window, it lets you turn a predictable burst or control attempt into a missed opportunity for the opponent.
Counterspell.when: Buy it when a readable ability repeatedly decides your fights and you can react with parry. If the catch happens before you can respond, compare automatic control protection instead.

Unstoppable.short: Proactive crowd-control immunity for an important commitment.
Unstoppable.desc: Unstoppable protects a planned commitment from crowd control. Activate it before the dangerous control sequence begins, especially when repeated disables would stop you from completing an engage or dealing damage. You still need a position that survives the incoming damage.
Unstoppable.when: Buy it when your engage or damage window repeatedly fails because of control. It is especially useful when you can anticipate the fight and activate protection before losing the ability to act.

Warp Stone.short: Teleports you forward and grants bullet resistance.
Warp Stone.desc: Warp Stone gives you an immediate position change and bullet resistance, helping escape a close threat or committed damage angle. Pick a destination that removes follow-up pressure; teleporting within the same danger wastes much of the opportunity.
Warp Stone.when: Buy it when one decisive reposition would let you survive or keep dealing damage. It fits repeated problems with close-range pressure, walls, or ultimate angles better than effects that need a cleanse.

Metal Skin.short: Temporary bullet immunity for the enemy's decisive weapon commitment.
Metal Skin.desc: Metal Skin gives you a temporary bullet-immunity window against decisive weapon pressure. Against a gun carry, activate it for the dangerous commitment and use that time to reach cover or let allies respond; it does not remove debuffs already on you.
Metal Skin.when: Buy it when enemy bullet damage kills you before you can play the fight. You can move it ahead of a damage upgrade if surviving the next weapon commitment is what lets your build contribute.

Spellbreaker.short: Adds spirit defense and periodic protection against a large spirit hit.
Spellbreaker.desc: Spellbreaker helps against spirit-heavy burst through spirit and debuff resistance plus periodic mitigation of a large spirit hit. Its protection is most valuable when available for the ability that matters, rather than spent on an earlier qualifying hit.
Spellbreaker.when: Consider it when repeated spirit burst remains lethal despite your existing defenses. Choose it for the current damage source and watch the protection's availability before committing to a fight.

Rebuttal.short: Rewards successful parries and reduces parry cooldown.
Rebuttal.desc: Rebuttal strengthens your response to melee pressure through a successful parry. Healing, returned damage, and a shorter parry cooldown help disrupt repeated melee trades, making it a useful lane counter when you can recognize the actual melee attack.
Rebuttal.when: Buy it when repeated melee trades are costing health or farm and you can land the parry. It can be worth prioritizing in lane against melee pressure rather than waiting for later fights.

Spirit Shielding.short: Grants a barrier after a burst of spirit damage.
Spirit Shielding.desc: Spirit Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of spirit damage, helping absorb what follows. It is useful when the opening ability hit starts a dangerous trade and a shield gives you time to reach cover or return manageable damage.
Spirit Shielding.when: Consider it when ability poke or burst repeatedly opens the enemy's winning trade. The trigger must be relevant to your matchup; compare other protection when weapon damage is the main opener.

Rusted Barrel.short: Reduces enemy fire rate for more manageable gun trades.
Rusted Barrel.desc: Rusted Barrel reduces an enemy's fire rate, making sustained gun trades easier to manage. Apply it during the exchange you want to change, then use the reduced weapon pressure to contest the wave, reposition, or return damage.
Rusted Barrel.when: Buy it when an opponent's repeated gunfire is winning lane trades and you need a focused response. Reassess if that opponent shifts toward ability burst or a control combo.

Suppressor.short: Spirit damage reduces enemy fire rate.
Suppressor.desc: Suppressor lets spirit-damage users reduce an enemy's fire rate through their damage pressure. It is useful when your spirit damage can reach a gun carry consistently, helping your team trade with less sustained weapon pressure.
Suppressor.when: Buy it when weapon-heavy enemies are winning trades and your abilities can reliably apply the effect. Consider it before the next sustained fight rather than relying on it against damage that already landed.

Capacitor.short: Pins targets by restricting stamina and movement tools.
Capacitor.desc: Capacitor combines weapon-build value with a targeted catch. Its projectile slows an enemy, prevents stamina usage, and restricts movement abilities and items, giving your team a window to punish a target that normally escapes.
Capacitor.when: Consider it when your weapon build benefits from the shock effects and your team also needs a stronger catch. If you only need movement denial, compare Slowing Hex before committing to the larger purchase.

Juggernaut.short: Reduces enemy fire rate when you take hits.
Juggernaut.desc: Juggernaut slows enemy fire rate when you take hits, helping frontline players manage sustained weapon pressure. It is most useful when you can survive the exchange and keep holding space, rather than absorbing damage from an unwinnable position.
Juggernaut.when: Buy it when repeated gunfire is wearing down your frontline and fire-rate reduction fits the way you fight. If you need to survive one short weapon burst, compare an immediate defensive active.

Extra Regen.short: Restores health between lane trades to preserve farming time.
Extra Regen.desc: Extra Regen is a lane-stabilizing purchase for health lost between trades. The value comes from staying available to last-hit and contest souls: recover behind cover, adjust your angle, and avoid giving back the same health to free poke.
Extra Regen.when: Buy it early when repeated poke forces you away from farm. If the enemy kills you in one combo, recovery between trades should give way to an answer that helps you survive the combo itself.

Alchemical Fire.short: Area damage that clears clustered summons and pressures enemy positions.
Alchemical Fire.desc: Alchemical Fire helps dismantle the space an enemy team wants to fight from. Its area damage is especially useful against clustered summons: clear the setup first, then take the fight on ground that favors you.
Alchemical Fire.when: Buy it when grouped turrets or summons keep blocking your team's approach. Prioritize it before the next push into that setup, rather than after you have already committed inside it.

Stamina Mastery.short: Improves stamina for repeated dodges and escapes.
Stamina Mastery.desc: Stamina Mastery supports matchups that demand repeated movement, including successive dodges and vertical escapes. The extra flexibility helps only if you keep a reserve for the next threat instead of spending every movement option on the first exchange.
Stamina Mastery.when: Upgrade when basic stamina no longer covers the repeated movement your fights require. Buy for a clear pattern of dodges or escapes, and keep enough capacity for the enemy's decisive ability.

Debuff Reducer.short: Shortens status effects without needing an active button.
Debuff Reducer.desc: Debuff Reducer helps you spend less of each fight under status effects. It is a passive answer to repeated disruption, useful when shorter debuffs give you room to move or trade without relying on another active button.
Debuff Reducer.when: Consider it when repeated status effects disrupt several exchanges. If one particular catch is instantly lethal, prioritize a tool that directly answers that catch instead of only shortening its duration.

Return Fire.short: Reflects incoming damage during exchanges you can survive.
Return Fire.desc: Return Fire punishes enemies for damaging you during an exchange you can survive. It suits durable brawlers facing sustained pressure: combine the reflection with appropriate defense so the opponent pays for continuing to shoot instead of simply winning the damage race.
Return Fire.when: Buy it when you already have the durability to stay alive through incoming damage and reflection would punish sustained attacks. It is a follow-through purchase, not a replacement for the defense you need to survive.

Monster Rounds.short: Improves damage against minions and summons.
Monster Rounds.desc: Monster Rounds helps you clear minions and summons before they take control of your lane or a fight. Against enemy setup, removing the extra targets first can be more effective than trying to damage the hero while every summon is still active.
Monster Rounds.when: Buy it early when summon or minion pressure makes farming and clearing unsafe. Upgrade only when you need more than the basic clear, and keep using cover while dismantling the setup.

Restorative Locket.short: Consumes accumulated stacks for a self-heal.
Restorative Locket.desc: Restorative Locket turns accumulated stacks into a self-heal, helping you stay present through repeated exchanges. The reset is most useful when it gives you enough health to keep farming or rejoin a fight from a better angle.
Restorative Locket.when: Consider it when recoverable chip damage keeps forcing you out of lane or skirmishes. If every catch is lethal before you can heal, spend on immediate survival first.

Veil Walker.short: Uses veils for speed, stealth, and safer approaches.
Veil Walker.desc: Veil Walker uses veil routes to give you speed and stealth for a safer approach or rotation. Its counter value comes from changing the angle an enemy can pressure, rather than expecting movement benefits while staying exposed in a direct duel.
Veil Walker.when: Consider it when useful veil routes let you avoid ranged pressure or approach a fight from a better angle. Check the routes you actually use before buying for a situation where no veil is available.

Tank Buster.short: Percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance.
Tank Buster.desc: Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.
Tank Buster.when: Consider it when raw health is the reason your target takes too long to finish. Confirm whether the real obstacle is health, healing, or a defensive cooldown before choosing the purchase.

Armor Piercer.short: Bullet procs bypass barriers and bullet resistance.
Armor Piercer.desc: Armor Piercer gives weapon carries a way to pressure enemies protected by bullet resistance or barriers. Its bullet procs bypass those defenses, making sustained shooting more useful against a target that ordinary weapon damage struggles to finish.
Armor Piercer.when: Consider it once bullet defense or barriers are the main reason your weapon damage falls short. You still need reliable shooting access; a late damage investment cannot fix being unable to reach the target.

Enduring Speed.short: Adds speed and slow resistance for easier repositioning.
Enduring Speed.desc: Enduring Speed helps you reclaim distance against slows and persistent chases. The speed and slow resistance matter most when they let you leave an enemy's preferred range, break an exposed angle, or arrive at cover before another trade.
Enduring Speed.when: Buy it when slows keep turning manageable poke into extended damage, or rotations leave you vulnerable to a chase. It fits best when better movement solves the problem before hard control lands.

Mystic Slow.short: Ability damage slows targets for easier follow-up or kiting.
Mystic Slow.desc: Mystic Slow adds movement pressure to ability damage, helping spirit builds keep enemies within reach or create distance from a pursuer. It works through the damage you can actually land, so reliable ability contact matters more than simply owning the item.
Mystic Slow.when: Buy it when your spirit damage connects but targets keep walking out of follow-up range. If a movement ability is the escape you must stop, compare Slowing Hex instead of relying on a slow alone.

Spirit Resilience.short: Passive resistance against recurring spirit damage.
Spirit Resilience.desc: Spirit Resilience provides consistent passive protection against spirit damage. It helps when abilities keep wearing you down across multiple exchanges, giving you a baseline defense while you focus on positioning, cooldowns, and your own contribution to the fight.
Spirit Resilience.when: Buy it when recurring ability damage is the main reason you cannot stay in fights. Check the opponent's actual build so you do not spend on spirit defense against a weapon-led damage pattern.

Plated Armor.short: Chance to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects.
Plated Armor.desc: Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.
Plated Armor.when: Buy it when recurring weapon hits and on-hit buildup are the problem across several fights. Compare Metal Skin for a deliberate immunity window and Dispel Magic for removable effects already applied.

Escalating Resilience.short: Builds bullet resistance while you keep shooting.
Escalating Resilience.desc: Escalating Resilience rewards weapon users who can keep shooting through a longer exchange. Its bullet resistance builds as you attack, helping you hold your ground against sustained gun pressure while continuing to contribute damage.
Escalating Resilience.when: Consider it when your fights are extended weapon trades and you have enough uptime to build the resistance. Against sudden burst or a disable that prevents shooting, compare a more immediate defense.

Weapon Shielding.short: Grants a barrier after a burst of weapon damage.
Weapon Shielding.desc: Weapon Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of weapon damage, helping absorb follow-up pressure. Use that shield window to reach cover or return a manageable trade instead of staying exposed until the next burst overwhelms you.
Weapon Shielding.when: Consider it when weapon poke repeatedly starts the enemy's winning trade and reliably triggers the barrier. If the lane is ability-led, compare Spirit Shielding or another defense suited to that damage.

Disarming Hex.short: Stops an enemy from firing during their weapon-damage window.
Disarming Hex.desc: Disarming Hex stops a target from firing their weapon, creating breathing room against gun-focused carries. It is particularly useful when your team wants to keep fighting through the enemy's damage window rather than only protect one player.
Disarming Hex.when: Buy it when weapon damage is deciding fights and you can safely target the carry. Check their build first: a disarm offers much less relief against damage coming primarily from abilities.

Decay.short: Targeted healing reduction with current-health damage over time.
Decay.desc: Decay gives you a direct way to put healing reduction on a sustain target, alongside current-health damage over time. It suits fights where you need anti-heal applied deliberately before the enemy starts winning the health trade.
Decay.when: Buy it when healing is extending fights and your build cannot reliably apply another anti-heal option. Make the purchase before the next sustain-heavy engagement and use it as your team commits.

Silence Wave.short: Silences enemies before an important escape or defensive cast.
Silence Wave.desc: Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.
Silence Wave.when: Buy it when an escape or defensive ability keeps denying a kill and a direct silence would let your team finish. For a channel that has already begun, check whether you need an interrupt instead.

Divine Barrier.short: Shields an ally and purges removable debuffs.
Divine Barrier.desc: Divine Barrier turns a defensive purchase into a teammate save. Its shield and debuff purge can protect an ally during a dangerous sequence, including removable bomb pressure, when you keep a clear view and a usable save angle.
Divine Barrier.when: Consider it when a teammate is repeatedly targeted and an ally shield or cleanse would change the outcome. Choose a buyer who can watch that teammate and remain in position to use it.

Healing Rite.short: Recovers health during a safe window between fights.
Healing Rite.desc: Healing Rite helps you recover between fights and return to lane with enough health to contest farm. It works best when you can step out of the enemy's pressure, complete the recovery safely, and avoid returning to the same exposed angle.
Healing Rite.when: Buy it during a difficult lane when you have safe recovery windows but cannot afford to keep leaving farm. It will not solve a burst that kills you before you can get out.

Rescue Beam.short: Heals a teammate and pulls them out of danger.
Rescue Beam.desc: Rescue Beam combines healing with a positional teammate save. The pull can remove an ally from the enemy's ongoing damage angle, so a good rescue depends as much on where you bring them as on how much health they recover.
Rescue Beam.when: Buy it when allies repeatedly get caught in positions you can pull them out of. Choose it before important team fights and make sure your own position offers a safer destination.

Bullet Resist Shredder.short: Reduces enemy bullet resistance for stronger weapon follow-up.
Bullet Resist Shredder.desc: Bullet Resist Shredder makes a focused target more vulnerable to weapon damage. It shines when your own gun pressure and your teammates' bullets land together, turning a resistance reduction into a practical opening to finish the fight.
Bullet Resist Shredder.when: Buy it when your team has meaningful weapon follow-up but targets survive that pressure. It is most useful before coordinated fights where several allies can shoot the same enemy.

Silencer.short: Weapon hits weaken spirit damage and build toward silence.
Silencer.desc: Silencer turns sustained weapon hits into pressure against ability-reliant enemies, reducing outgoing spirit damage and building toward silence. It fits gun users who can stay on a target long enough to restrict the cast that would otherwise turn the fight.
Silencer.when: Consider it when your weapon build has reliable target access and needs ongoing cast pressure. If the next ability must be stopped immediately, compare a direct active instead of waiting for weapon buildup.

Fleetfoot.short: Active speed boost for kiting and repositioning.
Fleetfoot.desc: Fleetfoot helps you manage fighting distance with an active speed boost. It suits heroes who want to keep pressure on a target while kiting away from close-range threats, or quickly change position before the next damaging exchange.
Fleetfoot.when: Consider it when keeping the right distance would let your build deal damage safely. Buy for a repeatable kiting problem; a movement active has less value if the real issue is a debuff or hard-control catch.

Extra Stamina.short: Adds movement capacity for another dodge or escape.
Extra Stamina.desc: Extra Stamina gives you more movement decisions in a fight. An additional dash or air movement option can be the difference between dodging a readable threat and having nothing left after spending stamina to farm or trade.
Extra Stamina.when: Buy it when you regularly run out of movement before the enemy's important ability arrives. Preserve the added capacity for that threat rather than spending it all on your approach.

Ricochet.short: Spreads weapon damage to nearby enemies and summons.
Ricochet.desc: Ricochet spreads weapon pressure to nearby targets, helping gun builds handle clustered enemies and summons. Its counter value grows when an enemy setup gives you several useful targets to hit from one safe angle, rather than a single isolated opponent.
Ricochet.when: Consider it when your weapon build also needs clear against grouped summons or nearby enemies. If the immediate problem is one lane summon, compare a smaller clear purchase before delaying core damage.

Cultist Sacrifice.short: Improves NPC clear and consumes eligible summons for rewards.
Cultist Sacrifice.desc: Cultist Sacrifice turns enemy setup into an opportunity. Building on Monster Rounds, it improves NPC pressure and can consume eligible summons for souls and a lasting buff, making it particularly useful when McGinnis keeps building turret positions.
Cultist Sacrifice.when: Upgrade when summon pressure is recurring and there are safe opportunities to consume eligible targets. Start with Monster Rounds if affordable clear is all you need right now.

Phantom Strike.short: Teleports to an enemy, then grounds, slows, and disarms them.
Phantom Strike.desc: Phantom Strike lets you commit directly to an enemy, ground them, and create a slowed, disarmed window. It can help punish an aerial carry, but the arrival point matters: your hero must survive where the target is standing.
Phantom Strike.when: Consider it when your hero can safely reach and finish an otherwise inaccessible target. Buy for a planned engage with follow-up, rather than using an expensive commitment to chase into an enemy team.

Spirit Sap.short: Reduce one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist.
Spirit Sap.desc: Spirit Sap reduces one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist. Apply it before a spell trade to weaken their Spirit-scaling output and help allied spirit damage land harder.
Spirit Sap.when: Consider it early when a specific enemy’s Spirit-scaling damage is winning trades and your side can use the resistance reduction. Keep it useful in mid-game skirmishes by applying it immediately before coordinated pressure. It is less compelling when the decisive problem is weapon damage, an unavoidable catch, or a target your team cannot reach.

blocks: Deadlock Counter Itemization: What to Buy and When
By Deadlock Item Builder · Practical matchup guide

The best Deadlock counter item solves the threat that is stopping you from contributing. Use this guide to compare answers, protect your core build and decide when a situational purchase is worth the detour.
Identify the threat, compare answers that fit your hero, and buy for the next fight.
Which Deadlock counter item solves your problem?
Start with the problem you need to solve. These are situational choices, not a list to buy in full.
The enemy heals back the damage your team deals.
Your hero can repeatedly deal spirit damage to the enemy who is healing.
Apply it before or during the healing window; it does little if your spirit damage never reaches that target.
Enemy gun damage kills you before you can escape or finish the fight.
You need a short window to survive weapon damage and reach cover or finish a committed fight.
Ability damage and control can still threaten you. Have a plan for when the active expires.
The target uses a movement ability to escape your team’s damage.
The target relies on an affected movement ability and your team can attack before the control ends.
Check the hero’s ability interaction. A cleanse or an escape used before your cast can spoil the catch.
A flying target stays out of reach, or a channeled ability is deciding the fight.
You need delayed control against an airborne target or an interruptible channel, with follow-up ready.
The stun is delayed. Check for a cleanse, immunity or another defensive response before relying on it.
Name the problem before opening the shop

A hero name is only the beginning of a counter-buy decision. Holliday might be winning fights because her barrels hurt, because her lasso catches your carry, or because her bounce pads let her escape. Those are different problems. Describe what actually lost the last fight: you could not move, could not reach a target, could not finish a kill, or could not survive the damage. That description gives your purchase a job.

Check the enemy build as well. A recommendation for a gun-focused opponent may be a poor use of souls when that player is investing in abilities. Start with the helper’s Most Common Problems, then compare the individual item explanations.
Choose an answer your hero can deliver

A counter has to work through your own play pattern. A spirit-damage hero that can repeatedly touch a target can apply Healbane naturally. A weapon user with reliable time on target may prefer Toxic Bullets. An active item is only useful if you can reach its target and use it before the dangerous moment.

Think about your role in the next fight. A frontliner may need to stay present long enough to protect a carry. A backline damage dealer may get more value from changing position. Both can be facing the same enemy and still need different purchases.
Look for overlap across the enemy team

Select multiple opponents in the helper to look for shared answers. An item that helps against several relevant threats is often easier to justify than a narrow answer to someone you rarely encounter. This is a shortlist, though: a shared recommendation does not measure who is fed, where you are fighting, or which cooldown is ending your fights.

Ask your team who already has utility. Two players can deliberately layer control, but buying the same answer without a plan may leave healing or another threat untouched. Decide who applies the first effect and who holds the follow-up.
Buy before the fight you need to change

There is no universal minute at which a counter becomes mandatory. If one affordable purchase lets you contest the next objective, delaying a luxury damage upgrade can make sense. If you are struggling simply because your core build is incomplete, stacking defensive purchases can leave you unable to punish an enemy mistake.

Protect the part of your build that lets your hero contribute. Buy the smallest useful answer, then review the next fight: did it keep you alive, create a kill window, or help your carry? If the enemy adds a cleanse or immunity, change your timing or coordinate a second layer instead of assuming the original plan still works.
How to use these counters in real matchups

Lasso catches you? Investigate control prevention. Barrels are the problem? Compare spirit defense. Bounce pads save her? Look at movement control. Buying from the hero name alone skips the decision that matters.
Your carry already has enough damage
If your Haze is carrying fights, utility that keeps her active may help more than another selfish upgrade. Agree who handles healing, who holds control and who protects the carry.
Buying every item recommended for one hero.
Delaying your essential damage without a clear benefit.
Choosing utility your hero cannot apply to the target.
When should you buy counter items in Deadlock?
Buy when a specific threat is likely to decide the next fight and the purchase changes that outcome. Lane, mid-game and late-game labels are useful context, not mandatory purchase times.
Should you finish your build before buying counters?
Not always. An urgent answer can justify a detour, but preserve the core items that let your hero deal damage, engage or support the team.

blocks: Deadlock Laning Guide: Counter Poke, Melee and Sustain
By Deadlock Item Builder · Practical matchup guide

A good lane counter helps you keep farming and avoid repeated deaths. Start with the trading pattern—poke, close-range pressure, summons or sustain—then buy a small answer that supports better positioning.
Use cover, sustain and cooldown windows first; buy a small answer to the recurring trade.
Early lane counters by pressure type
Start with the problem you need to solve. These are situational choices, not a list to buy in full.
Repeated lane poke leaves you too low to farm safely.
You lose health across repeated trades but can take cover and recover between them.
It will not save you from burst that kills you before you can disengage and regenerate.
You have lost too much health to stay in lane and need a recovery window.
You can step out of enemy pressure and complete a safe recovery before returning to farm.
You need a safe recovery window. It is not an emergency answer to damage that is already killing you.
Enemy melee attacks keep winning close-range lane trades.
Parryable melee attacks are deciding your trades and you can reliably time your parry.
The parry benefits require a successful parry. Do not treat every dash or ability hit as a melee attack.
Enemy summons or turrets create too much pressure for you to farm safely.
You need faster weapon-based clearing of minions, turrets or summons to protect your farm.
Better NPC clear does not make you safe from the hero behind the summons; use cover while clearing.
Work out how the lane is taking your health

The supplied lane guide groups pressure by how it reaches you: direct line of sight, close-range threat, poke, summons and sustain. A hero can occupy several categories. Identify the ability or trading pattern causing trouble rather than trying to memorize one fixed answer per hero.

If ordinary gunfire is winning the exchange, shorten exposure and use cover. If an area spell reaches around cover, choose a different position instead of repeating the same trade. Preserve stamina for the next meaningful threat.

Extra Regen or Healing Rite can help keep a difficult poke lane playable. Sustain works best when you also reduce the amount of damage you take. Repeatedly stepping into the same cast while relying on regeneration can still leave you too low to contest souls.

Bait a spell with a brief exposure, move before it connects, then use its cooldown to farm or pressure. Against abilities that bounce or cover an area, avoid cramped positions that give the enemy easy value. You do not need to win every exchange to leave lane with a usable build.
Respect melee and protect your parry

Against close-range pressure, keep an escape route and avoid spending all your movement on a harmless exchange. Parry is an important tool against melee attacks. Rebuttal is worth comparing when parry opportunities are a recurring part of the matchup, especially into melee-focused Abrams or Billy.

Baba’s Granny Longlegs attacks are also discussed as parry opportunities in the supplied guide. Do not assume every successful parry produces an identical punish window: its heavy attack is described differently from the light attack. Use the dedicated Baba page for that matchup.
Turn summons and sustain into a farming plan

Against summons, prioritize clearing pressure safely and collecting the resources available rather than fighting into a prepared wave. Monster Rounds is a candidate to compare in the McGinnis matchup. Clearing the lane can create the room you need for a better trade.

Against healers, repeated damage that fully recovers may gain little. Against a shield, consider baiting it with a small commitment and trading after it expires. Buy a small lane answer when it preserves farm or prevents a recurring death, then return to the core items that let your hero contribute after lane.
How to use these counters in real matchups
Keep stamina for the meaningful approach and protect your parry timing. Compare Rebuttal when melee is the recurring issue rather than buying it because Billy is simply in the lane.
McGinnis prepares pressure before the trade
Clear safely, compare Monster Rounds and collect the available farm. Fighting through her prepared pressure can give her the exchange she wants.
Using all your stamina before the enemy commits.
Taking trades a healer can recover from at no meaningful cost.
Buying several lane answers and losing your first core spike.
Should you buy anti-heal during the laning phase?
Consider it when healing is the specific problem and your hero can apply the effect. If you cannot threaten a kill, safer farming and a core purchase may be a better use of limited souls.
How do you counter melee heroes in lane?
Preserve spacing, stamina and a route out of the trade. Use parries against applicable melee attacks, and compare Rebuttal when those opportunities repeatedly decide the lane.

Rewards successful parries and reduces parry cooldown. Full item guide →
Improves damage against minions and summons. Full item guide →

comp-poke.title: How to Counter Poke Comps in Deadlock | Deadlock Item Builder
comp-poke.meta: Break the sight line, protect your resources, and approach from an angle that does not cost half your health before the fight starts.
blocks: How to Counter Poke Comps in Deadlock
Break the sight line, protect your resources, and approach from an angle that does not cost half your health before the fight starts.

Move between cover, clear the wave or setup safely, and avoid repeated trades into the same firing lane. Buy defense for the damage that actually lands, then coordinate a catch or a different approach.
Best counter items against poke teams
Choose it early when chip damage forces you away from the wave but you can find a safe recovery window.
Retreat to a protected position instead of trying to recover while the same poke keeps connecting.
Choose it when ability damage repeatedly chips you down before you can contribute.
Use the protection to hold a useful angle; it does not make every exposed crossing safe.
Choose it when sustained gun hits, rather than spell burst, are denying a useful approach.
Check the item’s protection window and keep cover available for the damage it does not cover.
Choose it when an airborne damage dealer keeps using an unreachable firing position.
Coordinate the delayed stun with teammates who can reach the landing; check enemy protection before committing.
Choose it when one short reposition can get you behind cover or into a useful angle.
Choose the destination first. Reaching the enemy alone may only give them an easier kill.
Choose the item that answers the recurring threat and fits your hero. These are situational options, not a five-item shopping list.
Use cover and leave predictable peeks.
Keep waves and summons from pinning you down.
Catch or flank with follow-up in reach.
How to recognise this team style
Poke teams win the approach before a full fight starts. Ranged shots, repeated spells, turrets or prepared zones make your team lose health while trying to reach a useful position.

Inspect the damage pattern. A flying hero can deal sustained weapon damage, while another ranged build relies on spirit burst. The same “poke” label does not justify one resistance purchase for everyone.

Cross open space in short, planned movements. Break line of sight when a charged shot or dangerous ability is ready instead of repeatedly returning to the same corner. Overhead cover matters against aerial firing angles.

Clear waves and summons from safety where possible. If you let the setup accumulate, the enemy can hold an approach while objectives take damage. Arrive before the area is fully prepared rather than walking into a finished siege at low health.

Look for an approach that makes the ranged threat reposition. A coordinated catch or second angle is stronger than a solo chase through their team. Make sure someone can finish the target once it loses its safe perch.
If the enemy spends a major poke spell without gaining a catch, use the gap to move or clear pressure. Do not wait for every cooldown to return before trying the exact same route again.
Heroes that can contribute to this style
Violet adds steerable empowered shots and brush pressure. Approach through cover, avoid lining up along the brush path, and deny her sustained view before Still Life completes.

These are examples of the threat, not a fixed draft recipe. Builds and team decisions change the way these heroes contribute. For split-push especially, look at the map behaviour rather than treating the tag as a permanent hero role.
Peeking the same sight line repeatedly while a charged attack is available.
Buying only spirit defense without checking a ranged hero’s weapon build.
Diving the backline alone while teammates remain trapped behind the setup.

Should you buy bullet or spirit defense against poke?
Match the purchase to the actual damage. Ranged gun pressure and ability poke need different protection, even when they come from the same hero.
Does Knockdown counter every poke team?
No. It is particularly useful when an airborne target gives your team a reachable landing window. It does not replace cover or wave control against ground-based siege.
How do you approach a poke comp?
Clear immediate pressure from cover, then use a cooldown gap or another angle with teammates who can follow. Avoid crossing the whole firing lane alone at low health.
Compare counter buys against the actual enemy heroes.

comp-dive.title: How to Counter Dive Comps in Deadlock | Deadlock Item Builder
comp-dive.meta: Keep your backline within reach, make the first engage expensive, and punish divers after they spend their movement.
blocks: How to Counter Dive Comps in Deadlock
Keep your backline within reach, make the first engage expensive, and punish divers after they spend their movement.

Stay close enough to help each other without stacking into the same engage. Keep an escape or defensive active for the first commitment, then use control and focused damage after the diver spends movement.
Best counter items against dive teams
Choose it when affected movement abilities let the diver reach your backline or leave for free.
Apply before the movement you need to prevent. A delayed response after the dive has landed may not save the target.
Choose it when changing your angle can avoid the engage and keep your damage available.
Plan a safe destination near cover or teammates; do not blink into another enemy’s follow-up.
Choose it when a predictable damage sequence is deciding the catch.
Time the invulnerability for the payoff. Your team still needs to cover the position where you will return.
Choose it when you can safely reach an ally caught by the engage.
Hold a useful angle and time the pull so the ally leaves the danger instead of returning straight into it.
Choose it when a diver’s healing keeps them alive through focused damage and you apply spirit damage reliably.
Apply before committing the damage; anti-heal does not stop the initial engage.
Choose the item that answers the recurring threat and fits your hero. These are situational options, not a five-item shopping list.
Play around cover and a teammate who can peel.
Save movement for the engage you need to avoid.
Focus a diver once escape or protection is spent.
How to recognise this team style
Watch how the fight starts: do enemies bypass the frontline and reach a vulnerable damage dealer? Repeated short-range commitments are a clearer signal than simply counting mobile heroes.
A team with one diver may still play around poke or picks. Prepare for the actual engage you are seeing, and check whether the diver’s damage is mainly weapon, spirit or melee.

Use a position where another teammate can respond without both of you being caught by the same area control. Cover, changes in elevation and a planned route out make the diver spend more to reach a clean target.

Keep a defensive cooldown for the important commitment. If you spend it on small poke, the dive can arrive during the gap. A support should be close enough to save or interrupt while holding a different angle from the threatened carry.

Call which movement or defensive spell the diver has spent. That is the point where a catch becomes easier to finish. Avoid splitting your damage across several enemies if one committed diver is now exposed.

Do not chase a retreating frontline so far that the next diver reaches your backline unopposed. A successful defense can be enough to reclaim space and pressure an objective while the enemy’s engage tools are unavailable.
Heroes that can contribute to this style

These are examples of the threat, not a fixed draft recipe. Builds and team decisions change the way these heroes contribute. For split-push especially, look at the map behaviour rather than treating the tag as a permanent hero role.
Standing alone beyond the range of your team’s saves.
Using your escape for minor poke before the main engage.
Buying anti-heal when the immediate problem is dying before you can act.
How to Counter Poke Comps in Deadlock
Poke teams Enemies wear you down from range and control open approaches. See items & game plan →
How to Counter CC-Heavy Teams in Deadlock
Heavy CC teams Enemies chain stuns, roots, silence or displacement to deny your response. See items & game plan →
How to Counter Healing and Sustain Comps in Deadlock
Sustain teams Enemies extend fights through healing, recovery, barriers and saves. See items & game plan →
How to Counter Burst Comps in Deadlock
Burst teams Enemies concentrate damage into a short combo or catch-and-finish window. See items & game plan →
How to Counter Split-Push Teams in Deadlock
Split-Push teams Enemies pressure side lanes while your team is occupied elsewhere. See items & game plan →
What items counter dive teams in Deadlock?

Choose the answer to the actual engage: Slowing Hex for affected movement, Warp Stone for a safe reposition, Ethereal Shift for a committed damage window, or Rescue Beam for an ally save. Add anti-heal if recovery prevents the punish.
Stay close enough to help without sharing one area catch. Use separate angles around the same cover and keep a safe route for the threatened player.
Does one mobile hero make a dive comp?
No. Judge how several enemies combine their approach and follow-up. A mobile hero can also play for isolated picks or pressure from another angle.

role-carry.meta: Learn how to play gun carry in Deadlock: efficient farming, item spikes, safe teamfight positioning, target selection and build-aware counter purchases.
blocks: How to Play Gun Carry in Deadlock
Build a lead you can actually use. A gun carry needs efficient souls, a useful item spike, and enough room to keep firing when the fight starts.
Efficient waves and useful item spikes
Cover, exits and room to keep firing

Your job is to turn sustained weapon damage into won fights and objectives. You usually benefit from a strong share of farm, but that investment only pays off if you can keep shooting without being caught.

M1 carry means a build centred on primary fire. Some heroes add spirit damage or damage-over-time effects to those hits. Judge the build by how it delivers pressure, not by assuming every shot deals only bullet damage.
Heroes that can play this role
These are common playstyles, not exclusive classes. Your build and team needs decide which job to emphasise.
See how builds change these heroes’ jobs

Secure the wave before forcing a long chase. Trade from cover, manage ammunition, and make the opponent pay for approaching souls without putting your own collection at risk. A small sustain or defensive purchase can be worth more than another damage component if it lets you remain in lane.

Use your spells to help secure resources or create a favourable trade. Do not spend your escape on a small amount of poke when the enemy can immediately punish you. With a utility partner, coordinate their control with a damage window you can actually follow.
For the shared fundamentals, read the [Deadlock laning guide](/guides/laning-counterplay).

Build a route around an available wave and nearby resources. Clear the wave, check what enemies are visible, then use the gap for a camp, safe pressure or a useful rotation. Repeatedly walking past waves to farm distant camps can waste both time and map control.

Take more dangerous farm only when visibility, nearby teammates or your escape makes it reasonable. If enemies disappear, shorten the route. Farming efficiently includes staying alive and preserving the resources your team can safely reach.

Join around a real item spike or a nearby objective you can influence. “I am a carry” is not a reason to ignore a winnable fight beside your lane. Equally, crossing the map for a fight that is already lost can cost the farm and objective your team could still defend.

Start behind the space your frontline has made, with cover or an exit nearby. Move laterally to find a firing angle rather than simply walking closer. If a pick hero disappears from view, consider where their catch would come from before committing to open ground.

Damage an exposed priority target when you can do so safely. If reaching that target would get you killed, hit the reachable threat while changing your angle. Avoid chasing a low-health enemy so far that you lose the fight happening around your team.

Save the escape or defensive active for the threat that would stop you firing. A short survival window is valuable when it creates time to reposition and resume damage; standing still through it can leave you caught as soon as it ends.
How to choose items for your role

Keep your next damage spike in mind, but answer a recurring lethal threat before it makes the spike unusable. [Toxic Bullets](/counter-items/toxic-bullets) suits weapon application when enemy recovery is extending fights; choose it because you can maintain hits on the relevant target.

For survival, compare [gun-defense options](/guides/gun-damage), [spirit-defense options](/guides/spirit-damage) and [control protection](/guides/crowd-control) against what is actually stopping you. Ask whether a teammate can cover targeted utility, while you handle your personal need to survive the engage.
Use the [Counter Item Helper](/counter-item-helper) to compare answers to the enemy heroes, then choose the purchase that fits your job.
Farming without checking the next objective or your current power spike.
Using movement for poke and having no answer to the enemy engage.
Chasing a support through dangerous space instead of dealing reachable damage.
Stacking damage when one recurring catch prevents you from using any of it.

On Wraith, a nearby catch with Telekinesis available can justify joining a teammate rather than taking one more camp. If the catch is too far away or no one can follow, collect safe resources and keep the next item timing moving.
[Back to the full hero roles chart →](/roles)
Is Haze always a gun carry?
No. A weapon-focused Haze can play as a carry, while a sleep-and-isolation approach can emphasise picks. Match your farming and fight decisions to the build and job your team needs.
When should a carry stop farming and fight?

Look for an item spike, an objective that matters and a position where you can contribute safely. You do not need to finish the entire build, but arriving without damage or a safe angle is rarely useful.
Should gun carries buy counter items?

Yes, when the threat would otherwise prevent them from dealing damage. Choose effects you can apply naturally, and coordinate team utility so several players do not delay their core items for the same job.
Find the counter buys that fit your next fight.

role-pick.title: How to Play Pick Heroes in Deadlock | Deadlock Item Builder
role-pick.meta: Learn Deadlock pick fundamentals: find exposed targets, coordinate catches, control rotations, protect carries and turn successful picks into objectives.
blocks: How to Play Pick Heroes in Deadlock
Make one exposed enemy easy to finish. A good catch connects your control, a reachable target and teammates who are ready to supply the damage.
A catch is only the beginning.
Look for a target outside protection
Make the catch reachable for allies
Take space or pressure an objective

Pick heroes use control, displacement or isolation to create a focused kill opportunity. A hook, swap or targeted lockdown can force an enemy out of safety, but the spell is only the start of the play.

Your job is to make the follow-up reliable. That means reading who is exposed, where your teammates are and whether protection or a save will undo the catch. A support who is reachable can be a better target than a carry you cannot safely hold.
Heroes that can play this role
These are common playstyles, not exclusive classes. Your build and team needs decide which job to emphasise.
See how builds change these heroes’ jobs

Use pressure to secure the wave while threatening the enemy’s predictable peeks. When possible, let an area ability damage both the wave and a nearby opponent. Make your partner aware of the setup before committing to a catch.

Do not chase a lane kill at the cost of an easy return kill or missed resources. If your important control is unavailable, play around cover and collection until the next useful window. A target forced away from the wave can already be a successful trade.
For the shared fundamentals, read the [Deadlock laning guide](/guides/laning-counterplay).

Move with a teammate whose damage can finish your catch. Look for enemies crossing between lanes, collecting a dangerous wave or returning along a predictable route. Check what is visible before entering contested space; the isolated target may have help just outside sight.

Keep your own resource collection moving between attempts. Repeatedly waiting for a target who never appears wastes the time you could use to clear an available wave or cover an objective. Choose routes that combine resources with a realistic opportunity.

When a pick succeeds, convert the missing enemy into something concrete: safer pressure on an objective, access to resources or a better position for the next fight. Reset if your team is low or key tools are spent instead of automatically chasing another enemy.

Before using control, check whether the destination and duration let teammates follow. Pulling a durable enemy into your backline may give that enemy the fight they wanted. Displace a target into usable damage, not just toward the nearest ally.

Track defensive movement and saves. If a target can deny your catch, force the response with a smaller commitment or switch to another exposed enemy. Coordinate your control so the team does not spend every disable into the same protection window.

Your control can also peel. If a diver reaches your carry, stopping or moving that diver may win more than starting a new chase. Decide whether the team needs an offensive catch or protection before the fight begins.
How to choose items for your role

Choose utility that makes your actual catch work: access to the target, reliable control or enough survival to remain useful after the setup. Do not add a delayed disable without considering the movement or protection that can defeat it.

Use the [mobility counter guide](/guides/mobility) when escape is denying a finish, and the [control guide](/guides/crowd-control) when enemy protection changes your timing. Coordinate targeted counter purchases with teammates; one dependable application can be more valuable than several poorly timed duplicates.
Use the [Counter Item Helper](/counter-item-helper) to compare answers to the enemy heroes, then choose the purchase that fits your job.
Landing control when no teammate can reach the target.
Pulling a strong frontline into the middle of your vulnerable allies.
Spending every disable before checking enemy saves or immunity.
Roaming for too long without collecting resources or covering an objective.

On Holliday, decide where the Lasso target should end up before committing. If your carry is being dived, using the displacement to separate the diver from that ally can be more useful than hunting another target.
[Back to the full hero roles chart →](/roles)
What is a pick hero in Deadlock?
A pick hero uses control, displacement or isolation to create a focused kill opportunity. The important part is making the target reachable for teammates who can finish it.
Yes. The same control used to catch an enemy can interrupt a dive or protect a teammate. Your team’s immediate need determines whether you use the tool offensively or defensively.
Should you always target the enemy carry?
No. Prioritise an exposed enemy you can actually catch and finish. A protected carry beyond your team’s reach may be a worse target than a reachable support who can otherwise save them.
Find the counter buys that fit your next fight.

comp-burst.title: How to Counter Burst Comps in Deadlock | Deadlock Item Builder
comp-burst.meta: Survive the damage window that decides the fight, then punish the cooldowns they spent. Match your defense to the actual combo and keep a safe reset available.
blocks: How to Counter Burst Comps in Deadlock
Survive the damage window that decides the fight, then punish the cooldowns they spent. Match your defense to the actual combo and keep a safe reset available.

Identify the damage type and the setup that makes the combo reliable. Use timed invulnerability or spell protection when you can react; choose passive defense or a barrier when the window is too sudden.
Best counter items against burst teams
Choose it when a predictable short combo is the lethal part of the fight.
Time the protection for the actual damage and make sure your return position is covered.
Choose it when the spell threat has a timing you can respond to reliably.
Practice the specific sequence. It is a timing answer rather than permanent protection against all damage.
Choose it when passive protection is more dependable than a reactive active against repeated spell damage.
Pair resistance with cover and an escape route; the attacker’s follow-up may still matter.
Choose it when a qualifying disable starts the burst and you need to survive the follow-up.
The protection gives you time to respond or receive a save; it does not remove the setup itself.
Choose it when gun damage, rather than spirit or melee, is the main payoff.
Use the bullet-immunity window to reposition or fight from safety. Do not expect it to cover every damage type in a mixed combo.
Choose the item that answers the recurring threat and fits your hero. These are situational options, not a five-item shopping list.
Find the setup and lethal damage source.
Keep a response for the real damage window.
Re-enter when their commitment has failed.
How to recognise this team style
Burst describes the timing of damage, not a single damage type. A short spell combo, concentrated gun pressure after control, or a close-range sequence can all feel like a sudden kill.
Check whether the burst arrives directly or after a predictable mark, hook or other catch. Preventing that setup may be more efficient than stacking defense against every part of the follow-up.

Do not stand where the enemy can begin the combo without spending anything. Use cover and keep a teammate able to respond. When a setup is applied, change your route toward help instead of moving farther into isolation.

Choose an escape destination before the catch. If a reactive item is your plan, confirm that the setup leaves you an activation window. Passive defense may be the more reliable answer when the first control removes your actions.
Hold your response for the payoff rather than spending it on the first small hit. The attacker may be waiting for that defensive tool to expire before using the real damage.

After surviving, track what the enemy spent to deliver the combo. Reset behind cover or coordinate a punish while their damage or escape is unavailable. Do not chase immediately if you are still low and their teammates can finish the exchange.
Heroes that can contribute to this style

Violet can contribute follow-up damage when a teammate creates a clear target, but the strength of that burst depends on her build and the exchange. Her main classification remains ranged pressure and control.

These are examples of the threat, not a fixed draft recipe. Builds and team decisions change the way these heroes contribute. For split-push especially, look at the map behaviour rather than treating the tag as a permanent hero role.
Buying bullet immunity for a mainly spirit combo.
Spending invulnerability on minor poke just before the payoff.
Surviving the first combo, then chasing into the next source of damage.

Heavy CC teams Enemies chain stuns, roots, silence or displacement to deny your response. See items & game plan →
How to Counter Healing and Sustain Comps in Deadlock
Sustain teams Enemies extend fights through healing, recovery, barriers and saves. See items & game plan →
How to Counter Split-Push Teams in Deadlock
Split-Push teams Enemies pressure side lanes while your team is occupied elsewhere. See items & game plan →
Should you buy resistance or an active against burst?
Use a timed active when the payoff is predictable and you can act reliably. Passive defense is more dependable when the catch is sudden or prevents activation.
Does Metal Skin counter all burst damage?
No. It provides a bullet-defense window. Check whether spirit damage, melee or another part of the combo is what actually kills you.
What should you do after surviving a burst combo?
Move to safety or punish the spent cooldowns with teammates. A failed enemy combo is an opening, but a low-health solo chase can throw it away.
Compare counter buys against the actual enemy heroes.

guide-crowd-control.title: Deadlock CC Counters: Cleanse, Block and Survive
guide-crowd-control.meta: Compare Deadlock crowd control counters: Dispel Magic, Indomitable, Unstoppable and Reactive Barrier. Choose prevention, cleansing or survival for your matchup.
blocks: Deadlock CC Counters: Cleanse, Block and Survive
By Deadlock Item Builder · Practical matchup guide
A cleanse, a control block and a barrier are different answers. Identify the effect that catches you, whether it can be removed, and how much follow-up damage you still need to survive.
Separate prevention from cleansing and survival; one item does not cover every disable.
Start with the problem you need to solve. These are situational choices, not a list to buy in full.
A removable debuff sets up damage or control that forces you out of the fight.
The threatening effect is removable and you can use the item before its follow-up decides the fight.
Check which effects it removes. Do not rely on pressing it while a disable prevents you from using items.
One opening disable catches you and lets the enemy start their combo.
A sudden qualifying control effect starts the enemy combo and is difficult to react to manually.
An earlier control effect can spend its protection. Further disables may still catch you afterward.
Crowd control interrupts your engage or stops you dealing damage.
You can anticipate the enemy’s control and activate protection before you engage or commit damage.
Activate before the disable lands. Control immunity does not protect you from the enemy’s damage.
You survive the initial disable but die to the damage that follows.
A hard-control catch triggers the barrier and its shield can help you survive the immediate follow-up.
The shield does not remove the disable. Repeated control or enough follow-up damage can still kill you.
Separate the setup from the damage

A death after crowd control contains two problems: the effect that stopped you and the damage that followed. More resistance may help with the second without fixing the first. Identify whether you are caught by one opening effect, several chained disables, or a debuff that gives you time to react.

Bebop’s hook, Seven’s delayed stun and Dynamo’s ultimate should not be treated as interchangeable. Use the dedicated hero guide to understand the specific sequence before trusting a general control-defense recommendation.
Use a cleanse only for effects it removes

Dispel Magic is a candidate when a removable debuff is the problem. Infernus burn and Seven’s delayed stun are examples discussed in the supplied guides. The useful moment is when removing that effect changes the fight, rather than after the follow-up has already forced you out.

Do not assume a cleanse removes every ultimate or works while you are unable to use items. Check the effect’s current interaction. Timing, item availability and the enemy’s follow-up determine whether the purchase is a usable answer.

Indomitable is worth investigating against an opening control effect, but a single-effect answer is not a blanket solution to repeated control. The supplied guides specifically flag Abrams and Dynamo as matchups where assuming it stops the whole sequence is a mistake.

Unstoppable fits a planned commitment that needs protection from control. Activate it before the dangerous sequence starts. It does not remove the need to survive incoming damage, and using it too early can let the enemy wait out your protection.
Survival and avoidance still have a role

Reactive Barrier can help absorb follow-up when it triggers, but a barrier does not mean the disable disappeared. Ethereal Shift and Counterspell offer different timing-based defensive options; compare their item pages and the matchup before deciding which event you are trying to avoid.

Against several sources of control, preserve spacing and communicate who is holding an interrupt or rescue. A teammate outside the engage may be able to help when the trapped player cannot. After the enemy buys immunity, stop relying on a control cast that no longer creates the same opening.
How to use these counters in real matchups
Seven’s delayed stun is setting up a burst
Compare a removable-debuff answer and its timing. A cleanse needs to change the sequence before follow-up damage forces you out; review the specific interaction on Seven’s guide.
Do not assume an opening-control block stops an entire ultimate. Preserve spacing, consider prevention before commitment and keep someone outside the engage able to help.
Using prevention only after the control has started.
Assuming a triggered barrier frees you to move.
What is the difference between Dispel Magic and Unstoppable?
Dispel Magic is an option for effects it can remove. Unstoppable protects a planned window from control when activated in time. They solve different parts of a fight.
Does Indomitable counter all crowd control?
No. Check the exact matchup and sequence. The supplied guides flag repeated control and specific Abrams and Dynamo interactions as reasons not to treat it as universal protection.

guide-spirit-damage.title: How to Counter Spirit Damage in Deadlock
guide-spirit-damage.meta: Counter spirit damage in Deadlock with shielding, resistance, cleanses and timed defense. Compare Spirit Shielding, Spirit Resilience, Spellbreaker and Counterspell.
blocks: How to Counter Spirit Damage in Deadlock
By Deadlock Item Builder · Practical matchup guide

Spirit damage can arrive as one burst, repeated abilities or a damage-over-time effect. Choose the answer to that pattern rather than treating every caster as the same matchup—or assuming every shot deals only weapon damage.

Compare Spirit Shielding for a useful barrier after a spirit burst, Spirit Resilience for recurring pressure, and Spellbreaker for dangerous spirit hits. Use a cleanse for removable effects or timed defense to avoid a specific commitment.
Choose for the problem you are facing; these are alternatives to compare, not a full shopping list.
An opening spirit burst leaves you unable to survive the follow-up.
The spirit-damage trigger reliably gives you a barrier and time to improve your position.
It responds to the trigger rather than stopping the opening ability. Follow-up control may still catch you.
Repeated spirit damage forces you out of fights.
You need consistent passive defense against the opponent’s actual spirit-damage build.
It does not remove damage-over-time effects or prevent the disable that starts the combo.
A large spirit hit is deciding fights despite your existing defense.
Its spirit defense and periodic burst protection address the hit you need to survive.
An earlier qualifying hit can spend the burst-protection effect. Check its availability before committing.
A predictable ability-damage moment is deciding the exchange.
You can recognize the threat and time your defensive response for the actual hit.
A mistimed response can leave the important hit unanswered. The enemy may bait your timing.
A removable burn or other debuff keeps damaging you.
The effect is removable and you can cast before its damage decides the fight.
It is not a universal answer to instant burst, every ultimate or a disable that prevents item use.
Identify the spirit damage that is killing you

Separate the initial hit from what follows. An enemy may start with control, add spirit burst and finish with gunfire. Look at the build and the recurring exchange before choosing a purchase. A spirit-defense item should answer a meaningful part of the damage rather than the fact that the hero has abilities.

Gunfire can also carry spirit pressure. Baba’s Thread Sap is described in the supplied guide as adding spirit damage to shots. Buying only weapon defense because the enemy is shooting can therefore miss the source that is winning the trade.
Counter spirit burst with a useful survival window

Spirit Shielding is an option when a spirit burst reliably triggers a barrier before the follow-up kills you. Take cover or improve your position while the protection lasts. Spellbreaker is another option to compare when a large spirit hit remains decisive, with attention to its periodic protection.

For a predictable committed hit, compare Counterspell or Ethereal Shift with passive defense. These depend on timing and a plan for the next position. If you are already caught and unable to activate an item, the setup may need its own answer.
Handle sustained damage and removable burns

When spirit pressure repeats across exchanges, consistent resistance may be more useful than relying on one brief defensive window. Spirit Resilience is a candidate to compare. Extra lane sustain may also help when the damage is recoverable and you can reduce exposure between trades.

A removable burn is a different problem from damage that has already landed. Dispel Magic is discussed in the supplied guides for Infernus’s Afterburn. Cleanse timing can change that exchange, but a cleanse does not undo every source of damage or replace safe positioning.
Prevent the combo instead of only absorbing it

If mobility lets a caster enter, deliver a combo and escape, movement control may create a better team response. If a defensive or damage ability must be prevented before it starts, compare cast denial. Be specific about what you want to stop; a silence is not automatically an interrupt for an existing channel.

Spirit Sap offers another situational comparison against Spirit-scaling damage. Its Spirit Power reduction is relevant to scaling damage, not a promise to shut off every ability. It also does not silence the target or remove the need for your own durability.
Reassess when the enemy changes their build

A spirit-heavy hero can invest in weapon pressure, and a gun-focused hero can add significant spirit damage. Revisit the death pattern after major purchases. If you now survive the ability hit but die while trapped in place, control defense or movement may become the next priority.

Preserve the parts of your build that let you punish the enemy’s commitment. Surviving with no useful follow-up is not always an improvement. Coordinate utility with your teammates and buy for the fight you expect to take next.
How to choose in real matchups
Holliday’s barrels are the damage problem
If you survive her displacement but the barrels kill you, compare spirit defense rather than spending every slot on lasso answers. Separate the damage problem from the control problem.
Baba’s shooting still carries spirit pressure
Thread Sap can add spirit damage to her shots. Check her build, compare the right defense and use the dedicated guide to distinguish gun pressure, melee pressure and her transformation threat.
Choosing weapon defense just because the enemy is firing a gun.
Using a cleanse as if it reverses instant burst damage.
Ignoring the control or positioning that lets the whole combo connect.
What is the best item to counter spirit damage in Deadlock?
Match the pattern. Compare Spirit Shielding for a barrier response, Spirit Resilience for recurring pressure, Spellbreaker for dangerous hits, and a cleanse or timed defense for specific effects.
Should I buy spirit resistance against every caster?
Check the opponent’s actual build and damage first. If weapon damage or a disable is deciding your deaths, spirit resistance may not solve the main problem.

role-spirit-carry.meta: Learn Deadlock spirit carry fundamentals: lane pressure, ability timing, rotations, enemy farm pressure, teamfight angles and choosing counter items.
blocks: How to Play Spirit Carry in Deadlock
Turn ability windows into an advantage. Pressure with purpose, reach targets from useful angles, and keep enough movement or defense to survive the response.
Find the window. Land the damage.
Reach a target your team can punish
Protect an escape for the response

A spirit carry invests in ability-driven damage and uses it to threaten important targets. “Spirit nuker” and “off carry” often overlap with this category, but not every spirit build plays the same way: some burst and leave, while others deliver repeated damage or control an area.

Your job is to make that damage matter at the right moment. A strong combo used into protection or beyond your team’s reach can accomplish less than a smaller spell sequence that helps secure a kill or objective.
Heroes that can play this role
Violet follows allied contact with empowered shots, brush damage and Still Life. Keep a useful view from behind the team instead of walking forward alone to finish a sketch.
These are common playstyles, not exclusive classes. Your build and team needs decide which job to emphasise.
