Which Deadlock role should you play?

Choose the job you enjoy doing repeatedly. Strong aim can suit a gun carry, but farming and safe positioning matter just as much. Frontline players need timing and awareness; supports need to recognise the teammate whose next action will decide the fight.
Turn souls into sustained weapon damage. Farm efficiently, reach a useful item spike, and fight from an angle where you can keep shooting.
Create damage windows with abilities. Use lane pressure, cooldown timing and safe approaches to land your combo without losing your escape.
Make dangerous space usable for your team. Threaten an engage, absorb pressure you can survive, and keep enemies away from your damage dealers.
Catch an exposed enemy and make the follow-up easy. Coordinate your control with nearby teammates instead of starting a fight no one can reach.
Keep teammates effective through saves, healing, control and utility. Use resources efficiently and position where your next spell can change the fight.
Roles versus positions: who gets the farm?

Roles describe how you contribute. **Positions describe resource priority.** Players sometimes use positions 1–6 to discuss who needs the most souls, with position 1 receiving the highest priority. The middle positions vary between coaching systems; they are not a universal hero ranking.

A damage build usually needs more investment to keep threatening enemies. A utility build may reach a useful save or control spike sooner. That does not mean a support should stop farming or that a carry should take every nearby camp. Allocate safe waves and camps so your team reaches its next useful items without leaving objectives undefended.

Discuss the next spike rather than arguing over a number: “I need one more wave for my damage item,” or “Take this lane; I can move with our pick hero.” A lower farm priority describes how you use resources, not how important you are.
Are Deadlock roles tied to lanes?

A lane assignment does not permanently decide your role. During lane, your partner and matchup shape how you trade, secure souls and manage pressure. After lane, the team should distribute safe farm, rotations and objective coverage around its current strengths.

Do not assume that a frontline must always occupy one lane or that a support must follow the same carry all game. Look at which area needs protection, which teammate needs safe farm and where a rotation can produce a real advantage.
What should you do after the laning phase?
**Gun carry:** collect an available wave, take nearby resources efficiently, and join fights that let you use your item spike without walking into a catch.
**Spirit carry:** use available damage cooldowns and lane pressure to threaten a rotation or invade with help. Keep a safe route out.
**Frontline:** contest an entrance or dangerous wave when your teammates can use the space. Avoid starting an engagement beyond their reach.
**Pick:** move with a teammate who can finish your catch. Check enemy visibility before spending your control.
**Support:** cover the teammate under pressure, help your team move through contested space, and take accessible resources between useful rotations.
Before moving, ask: **what changes if I go there?** If you cannot secure a kill, protect an objective, save a teammate or collect useful resources, another route may do more.
How your role changes counter item choices

Choose a counter you can apply while doing your job. A gun carry can maintain weapon-applied effects; a spirit build may apply Healbane more naturally. A support can sometimes handle a targeted utility purchase, letting a damage dealer keep their next damage spike. Personal survival items still need to be bought by the player taking the threat.

Use the [Counter Item Helper](/counter-item-helper) for enemy matchups, the [Counter Item Library](/counter-items) to compare effects, and the [counter itemization guide](/guides/counter-itemization) to decide whether a purchase is urgent. Coordinate a shared answer before several teammates buy the same active for the same job.
Can one Deadlock hero play multiple roles?
Yes. Items and team needs can shift a hero between damage, frontline, pick and support jobs. Use the chart as a starting point, then adapt to the build you are actually playing.
M1 means mouse one: your primary fire button. An M1 or gun carry invests in sustained weapon pressure and needs safe firing angles to turn that investment into damage.
What is the difference between a role and a position?

A role describes your combat job. A position describes your relative farm priority. Players use different systems for positions 1–6, so discuss resource needs rather than treating a number as a fixed hero class.
Does support mean you should never farm?
No. Supports still need useful items and should collect accessible resources. Avoid competing for the same safe farm as a teammate who needs it more when another productive route is available.
Should you choose a role based only on your hero?
No. Consider your build, teammates, enemy threats and the next objective. The same hero may need to deal damage in one lineup and protect or create space in another.

counter-comps: Deadlock Team Comp Counters: Items & Strategy
Recognise dive, poke, heavy CC, sustain, burst and split-push threats. Find practical counter items and a team game plan for the next fight.
Which threat is deciding your fights?

A team composition describes how several enemies combine their strengths. Most lineups have more than one threat: dive can arrive behind poke, while healing can make a burst window harder to finish. Start with the pattern that keeps costing your team the fight.
How to Counter Dive Comps in Deadlock
Enemies close distance to overwhelm a carry or support before the team can respond.
How to Counter Poke Comps in Deadlock
Enemies wear you down from range and control open approaches.
How to Counter CC-Heavy Teams in Deadlock
Enemies chain stuns, roots, silence or displacement to deny your response.
How to Counter Healing and Sustain Comps in Deadlock
Enemies extend fights through healing, recovery, barriers and saves.
How to Counter Burst Comps in Deadlock
Enemies concentrate damage into a short combo or catch-and-finish window.
How to Counter Split-Push Teams in Deadlock
Enemies pressure side lanes while your team is occupied elsewhere.
How to counter a mixed team composition
Is the first problem a catch, the damage after it, or recovery that prevents the finish?
Buy an effect your hero can apply and coordinate shared utility with teammates.
Use cover, a better angle or a cooldown gap so the same sequence does not repeat.

A team with healing and heavy control may require both a reliable anti-heal buyer and personal protection for the player being caught. Buying the same item on everyone can leave the other half of the problem untouched.
Your role changes the right purchase

A gun carry needs enough safety to keep firing. A frontline needs durability and a useful threat. A support or pick hero may be better positioned to supply targeted control or a save. Discuss who can deliver the effect before every teammate delays their next core item.
Can a team have more than one composition type?
Yes. Composition traits overlap. Choose the recurring threat that decides the exchange, then account for the protection or follow-up that makes it work.
Are these guides for playing as a role or against a team?
These guides explain how to play against enemy team threats. The Roles & Playstyles section explains your own job and how to choose a suitable playstyle.
Do the statistics measure exact team compositions?
No. The supplied data covers item performance against individual heroes. Grouping those matchups provides context, not a direct measurement of six-hero synergy.

Identify the threat, compare answers that fit your hero, and buy for the next fight.
Deadlock Anti-Heal Items: Healbane vs Toxic Bullets
Choose anti-heal you can apply reliably, then focus damage during the healing window.
Deadlock Gun Counters: Metal Skin vs Plated Armor
Compare a short defensive window, sustained protection and a disarm; use cover to limit follow-up.
Deadlock CC Counters: Cleanse, Block and Survive
Separate prevention from cleansing and survival; one item does not cover every disable.
Deadlock Mobility Counters: Slowing Hex vs Knockdown
Control the escape before committing damage, and plan around cleanses and immunity.
Deadlock Laning Guide: Counter Poke, Melee and Sustain
Use cover, sustain and cooldown windows first; buy a small answer to the recurring trade.
Deadlock Shielding vs Resistance: Which Should You Buy?
Choose between triggered barriers and ongoing damage reduction.
How to Counter Spirit Damage in Deadlock
Match your defense to burst, repeated abilities or removable damage-over-time effects.
Should I buy shielding or resistance in Deadlock?

Shielding provides a temporary barrier when its trigger occurs; resistance reduces incoming damage of the relevant type. Choose for the damage pattern, your health pool and the next fight. [Read the shielding vs resistance guide →](/guides/shielding-vs-resistance)
How do I stop getting chain CC’d or locked down in Deadlock?

Use the counter that matches the control pattern. Indomitable automatically removes one sudden hard-control event and grants a barrier, while Unstoppable is usually better when you expect several control effects during a planned engage. Reactive Barrier is the cheaper early-lane option when you mainly need to survive the first stun.
What is the best way to counter healing in Deadlock?

The best way to counter healing is to buy anti-heal items like Healbane, Toxic Bullets, Decay, or Spirit Burn. These items reduce health recovery by up to 70%, which is vital against sustain-heavy heroes.
How do you counter airborne heroes like Vindicta or Grey Talon?

Counter flyers using Knockdown. Its stun is significantly longer against airborne targets and it increases their gravity, making heroes like Vindicta and Grey Talon much easier to bring back to the ground and focus.
What item should I buy to counter high fire-rate gun heroes?

Metal Skin provides a temporary bullet-immunity window against committed gun damage. Rusted Barrel is a targeted active that reduces fire rate. Suppressor applies fire-rate reduction through spirit damage, so choose it on a hero that can maintain that effect.
What is the difference between Shred and Resistance Shredder items?
Shred items like Spirit Strike or Bullet Resist Shredder reduce an enemy's existing armor. This acts as a damage multiplier for your whole team, making them extremely effective against tanks.
How do I escape Warden's Binding Word or Paradox's wall?
Items that grant Extra Stamina or Stamina Mastery are essential for dashing out of ground-based zones. For Paradox specifically, Warp Stone allows you to teleport instantly after being swapped.
What is the best item for countering channeled ultimates like Seven's?

Knockdown is the standard answer because its delayed stun interrupts channeled abilities. Cursed Relic can also interrupt and silence a target before or during a vulnerable channel, but remember that a Silence by itself does not cancel a channel that has already started unless the source also interrupts.
How does Rebuttal help win lane in Deadlock?
Rebuttal is a melee counter item that cuts your parry cooldown from 4 seconds to 2 seconds. It also heals you and returns damage, making it much harder for melee heroes to bait your parry safely.
How do you remove debuffs like Bebop's sticky bomb or Infernus's burn?

Use Dispel Magic for removable non-ultimate effects such as Bebop's Sticky Bomb or Infernus's Afterburn. Divine Barrier can cleanse non-stun debuffs from an ally as well, making it the better team-save option when you need to protect someone else.
When should I buy defensive counter items over damage items?

A pro-level rule of thumb is to build defensive items when ahead to maintain your lead, and damage items when behind to punish mistakes. However, if one specific hero is preventing you from playing, buy the counter immediately.
How do you counter burst spirit damage from casters?

Compare Spirit Shielding for a triggered barrier, Spirit Resilience for recurring pressure, and Spellbreaker for dangerous spirit hits. A cleanse or timed defensive item may be better for a specific effect. [Read the spirit damage counter guide →](/guides/spirit-damage)
How can I save a teammate from a kidnap or grab?

Use Rescue Beam. This active item heals a teammate and pulls them to your current location, helping move threatened allies toward safety. Against Mo & Krill, do not assume the pull instantly cancels Combo; the team still needs to focus or interrupt the captor.
item-builder: h2
How to Use the Deadlock Item Builder
builder-guide-title
p
Follow these seven steps to create your item, check the live preview, and export a PNG.
builder-guide-intro
ol

Step 1Choose your item’s lookSelect Weapon, Vitality, or Spirit for the card’s colours. Pick an existing item icon or upload a PNG, JPG, or WebP under 5 MB. Set your item name and Soul Cost in Identity.The starting examples change with the category until you start editing. After that, changing category keeps your edits.

Step 2Write base statsUse one stat per row, such as +50 Bonus Health. To show a before-and-after value beside it, type +50 Bonus Health | 750 > 800.The | separates the stat from its comparison values. Base stats appear at the top of the card without automatic icons.

Step 3Add ability stat boxesChoose Passive or Active, then add your description and stat boxes. In each box, put the value first and the label after |:+26% | Fire Rate35m | Radius7s | DurationThe value appears above the label. Use **+ Add Box** for another stat or **+ Add Ability Section** for another effect.

Step 4Get automatic stat iconsAbility boxes recognise keywords in the label after |. For example, +26% | Fire Rate adds the Fire Rate icon beside the value. Capitalisation does not matter.Use these labels in your ability stat boxes. The examples below are formatting examples for custom items. Recognised labels and their automatic iconsIcon & labelWhat to use it forExample to copyDamageA general damage label; currently uses the bullet-damage icon.+15% | Weapon DamageBullet ResistResistance to incoming bullet damage.+17% | Bullet ResistSpirit ResistResistance to incoming spirit damage.+15% | Spirit ResistFire RateHow quickly the weapon fires.+26% | Fire RateStamina RecoveryHow quickly stamina recovers.+12% | Stamina RecoveryStaminaAn increase to the available stamina pool.+1 | StaminaSprintA sprint-speed bonus; Sprint Speed also matches.+1.5m | Sprint SpeedMove SpeedA movement-speed bonus.+2.5m | Move SpeedRegenHealth restored over time; Health Regen also matches.+3 | Health RegenHealthA health bonus; Bonus Health also matches.+50 | Bonus HealthDurationHow long an effect lasts.7s | DurationRangeHow far an attack or ability can reach.+10% | Ability RangeRadiusThe distance an area effect extends from its centre.35m | RadiusSpirit PowerA bonus to the Spirit Power stat.+10 | Spirit PowerSpirit DamageDamage described as spirit damage.40 | Spirit DamageAmmoA magazine-size or ammo-capacity bonus.+20% | Ammo Unrecognised labels still display, without an icon.

Step 5Format descriptions and effectsWrap words in two asterisks to make them bold: Gain **move speed** for 7 seconds. Press Enter in the description to start a new line.Enter a cooldown such as 22s in the CD field to show it with a cooldown icon. Tick **COND** on a stat box to add a “Conditional” label. Explain the condition in your description.

Step 6Add item upgradesChoose Upgrades From or Upgrades To in the dropdown to show an item connection. Search or select an item in the upgrade field to show its current artwork from the item library. You can also type a custom name, which displays as text. Leave the item name blank to hide this section.

Step 7Preview and export your itemCheck your finished card in the preview, then select **Export Template as PNG**. On mobile, use the Preview tab to review your card. The exported image includes the site watermark.
h2
Create and Share Custom Deadlock Items
p

The Deadlock Item Builder is a free web app that lets players create, customize, and share custom Deadlock item ideas using editable templates. Instead of writing item concepts in notes or screenshots, you can build structured item templates that are easy to edit, download, and share with the community.
p

With this Deadlock item creator, you can experiment with new item concepts, balance ideas, and theorycraft different designs for the community. Whether you're brainstorming new mechanics, creating fun item ideas, or exploring gameplay concepts, the builder gives you a clean format to present your ideas clearly.
p

The Deadlock Item Builder works as a flexible template system that allows you to customize stats, abilities, descriptions, and item effects. Once your item is complete, you can export the template and share it with friends, communities, or discussions about Deadlock gameplay.
h3
This tool is perfect for:
ul
Designing custom Deadlock items
Sharing item ideas with the community
Creating structured item templates
Exploring theorycraft and gameplay concepts
Saving and exporting your item designs
p

If you're creating custom deadlock items, you can also design full deadlock character abilities using the [Deadlock Hero Ability Maker](/hero-ability-maker) to build complete deadlock character ability concepts.
h2
Deadlock Item Builder FAQ
details
What is the Deadlock Item Builder?
The Deadlock Item Builder is a web-based tool that allows players to create and design their own custom Deadlock items using editable templates.
details
Is the Deadlock Item Builder free to use?
Yes. The Deadlock Item Builder is completely free to use. Anyone can create custom Deadlock items, edit templates, and download their item ideas without needing an account.
details
Do I need to create an account to use the item builder?
No. You can use the Deadlock Item Builder without creating an account. Simply open the builder and start designing.
details
Can I download the custom items I make?
Yes. After creating your custom Deadlock item, you can export and download the finished template as an image file.
details
How does the Deadlock Item Builder work?
The builder provides a customizable template where you can enter item stats, descriptions, and abilities. Once complete, you can download the image to share.
details
Can I share the items I create?
Yes. Download the PNG template and share it in Discord, Reddit, or with friends.
details
Why use an item builder?
It structures your ideas clearly in a format that looks professional and feels like the actual game UI.
details
Can I create different types of items?
Yes. The builder supports Weapon, Vitality, and Spirit categories.
details
Is this official?
No. This is a fan project created for the community and is not affiliated with Valve.
details
Who is this for?
For any Deadlock player who enjoys theorycrafting, balance discussions, and creative design.
hero-ability-maker: h2
Design and Explore Deadlock Hero Abilities
p

Abilities play a major role in how heroes function in Deadlock. Each ability shapes how a character moves, engages in combat, and interacts with enemies during a match. From mobility tools and spirit-powered attacks to defensive mechanics and crowd control effects, abilities define a hero’s overall playstyle.
p

The Deadlock Hero Ability Maker helps players organize and visualize these concepts. Instead of rough notes or scattered ideas, abilities can be structured into a clear format that highlights mechanics, cooldowns, effects, and intended gameplay interactions.
h3
Example Custom Deadlock Ability Concepts
ul
**Arc Relay** – Fire a spirit beam that chains between nearby enemies.
**Momentum Dash** – Dash forward and gain damage based on distance.
**Spirit Overload** – Convert energy into a temporary ability boost.
p
If you're experimenting with full hero designs, you can also create complementary items using the [Deadlock Item Builder Tool](/item-builder).
h2
Deadlock Hero Ability Maker FAQ
details
What is the Deadlock Hero Ability Maker?

The Deadlock Hero Ability Maker is a web tool that allows players to design custom hero abilities for Deadlock using a structured template. You can define ability names, effects, cooldowns, and descriptions to create complete ability concepts.
details
How do you create custom abilities in Deadlock?

While the game itself may not allow players to add new abilities, many players enjoy designing ability ideas using concept tools. The Deadlock Hero Ability Maker lets you create and organize custom ability concepts that can be shared with the community.
details
Can I design my own Deadlock hero abilities?

Yes. Using the ability creator, players can design their own hero abilities by defining mechanics, effects, and interactions. This is commonly used for theorycrafting or sharing creative hero concepts.
details
Is there a Deadlock ability template I can use?

Yes. The ability maker provides a structured template that mimics the format used in many game ability descriptions. This helps players organize ability stats, effects, and cooldowns in a clean format.
details
Can I create full hero ability kits?
Many players use the tool to design complete hero kits that include multiple abilities such as primary abilities, secondary abilities, passives, and ultimate skills.
details
Where do people share custom Deadlock abilities?
Custom ability concepts are commonly shared on Reddit, Discord servers, forums, and community discussion pages where players discuss balance ideas and hero design concepts.
details
What are good Deadlock ability ideas?

Popular ability concepts often include mobility skills like dashes or teleports, crowd control effects, spirit-powered attacks, defensive shields, and abilities that interact with movement or positioning.
details
Can I export or share the abilities I create?
Yes. Once an ability concept is finished, it can be exported as a high-resolution PNG image so it can be shared with other players online.
details
Is the Deadlock Ability Maker free?
Yes. The ability creator is completely free and does not require creating an account to design or export custom abilities.
details
Is this tool affiliated with Valve or Deadlock developers?
No. This tool is a fan-made project created for the Deadlock community and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve Corporation.
counter-items: Find the best Deadlock counter items for the threat in front of you—from anti-heal against sustain to bullet defense, spirit protection, cleanses, and tools that stop an escape.

Compare what each counter item solves, which hero matchups it fits, and when to buy it. Use the early-, mid-, and late-game tags as a starting point, then choose for the enemy build and the next fight your team needs to win.

Alchemical Fire helps dismantle the space an enemy team wants to fight from. Its area damage is especially useful against clustered summons: clear the setup first, then take the fight on ground that favors you.

Armor Piercer gives weapon carries a way to pressure enemies protected by bullet resistance or barriers. Its bullet procs bypass those defenses, making sustained shooting more useful against a target that ordinary weapon damage struggles to finish.

Bullet Resist Shredder makes a focused target more vulnerable to weapon damage. It shines when your own gun pressure and your teammates' bullets land together, turning a resistance reduction into a practical opening to finish the fight.

Capacitor combines weapon-build value with a targeted catch. Its projectile slows an enemy, prevents stamina usage, and restricts movement abilities and items, giving your team a window to punish a target that normally escapes.

Counterspell rewards reading an enemy's commitment. By upgrading your parry to block ability damage and effects during its protection window, it lets you turn a predictable burst or control attempt into a missed opportunity for the opponent.

Cultist Sacrifice turns enemy setup into an opportunity. Building on Monster Rounds, it improves NPC pressure and can consume eligible summons for souls and a lasting buff, making it particularly useful when McGinnis keeps building turret positions.

Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.

Debuff Reducer helps you spend less of each fight under status effects. It is a passive answer to repeated disruption, useful when shorter debuffs give you room to move or trade without relying on another active button.

Decay gives you a direct way to put healing reduction on a sustain target, alongside current-health damage over time. It suits fights where you need anti-heal applied deliberately before the enemy starts winning the health trade.

Disarming Hex stops a target from firing their weapon, creating breathing room against gun-focused carries. It is particularly useful when your team wants to keep fighting through the enemy's damage window rather than only protect one player.

Dispel Magic resets a fight weighed down by removable non-ultimate debuffs. Use it to clear effects such as Bebop's Sticky Bomb before detonation, then reposition or recommit with the debuff gone. Its activation restrictions are part of the decision.

Divine Barrier turns a defensive purchase into a teammate save. Its shield and debuff purge can protect an ally during a dangerous sequence, including removable bomb pressure, when you keep a clear view and a usable save angle.

Enduring Speed helps you reclaim distance against slows and persistent chases. The speed and slow resistance matter most when they let you leave an enemy's preferred range, break an exposed angle, or arrive at cover before another trade.

Escalating Resilience rewards weapon users who can keep shooting through a longer exchange. Its bullet resistance builds as you attack, helping you hold your ground against sustained gun pressure while continuing to contribute damage.

Ethereal Shift lets you sit out a dangerous moment through brief invulnerability and untargetability. Against a committed burst or a short ultimate window, the goal is to waste the enemy's investment and return with a plan for your next position.

Extra Regen is a lane-stabilizing purchase for health lost between trades. The value comes from staying available to last-hit and contest souls: recover behind cover, adjust your angle, and avoid giving back the same health to free poke.

Extra Stamina gives you more movement decisions in a fight. An additional dash or air movement option can be the difference between dodging a readable threat and having nothing left after spending stamina to farm or trade.

Fleetfoot helps you manage fighting distance with an active speed boost. It suits heroes who want to keep pressure on a target while kiting away from close-range threats, or quickly change position before the next damaging exchange.

Healbane turns your spirit damage into healing reduction, making it a natural counter-buy for ability users facing sustain. Apply it before the enemy gets full value from healing, then use the reduced recovery to help your team secure the kill.

Healing Rite helps you recover between fights and return to lane with enough health to contest farm. It works best when you can step out of the enemy's pressure, complete the recovery safely, and avoid returning to the same exposed angle.

Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.

Juggernaut slows enemy fire rate when you take hits, helping frontline players manage sustained weapon pressure. It is most useful when you can survive the exchange and keep holding space, rather than absorbing damage from an unwinnable position.

Knockdown gives your team a delayed stun to punish airborne targets and interrupt vulnerable channels. The delay is the key detail: cast while there is still time for the stun to land, and have damage ready when the target is controlled.

Metal Skin gives you a temporary bullet-immunity window against decisive weapon pressure. Against a gun carry, activate it for the dangerous commitment and use that time to reach cover or let allies respond; it does not remove debuffs already on you.

Monster Rounds helps you clear minions and summons before they take control of your lane or a fight. Against enemy setup, removing the extra targets first can be more effective than trying to damage the hero while every summon is still active.

Mystic Slow adds movement pressure to ability damage, helping spirit builds keep enemies within reach or create distance from a pursuer. It works through the damage you can actually land, so reliable ability contact matters more than simply owning the item.

Phantom Strike lets you commit directly to an enemy, ground them, and create a slowed, disarmed window. It can help punish an aerial carry, but the arrival point matters: your hero must survive where the target is standing.

Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.

Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.

Rebuttal strengthens your response to melee pressure through a successful parry. Healing, returned damage, and a shorter parry cooldown help disrupt repeated melee trades, making it a useful lane counter when you can recognize the actual melee attack.

Rescue Beam combines healing with a positional teammate save. The pull can remove an ally from the enemy's ongoing damage angle, so a good rescue depends as much on where you bring them as on how much health they recover.

Restorative Locket turns accumulated stacks into a self-heal, helping you stay present through repeated exchanges. The reset is most useful when it gives you enough health to keep farming or rejoin a fight from a better angle.

Return Fire punishes enemies for damaging you during an exchange you can survive. It suits durable brawlers facing sustained pressure: combine the reflection with appropriate defense so the opponent pays for continuing to shoot instead of simply winning the damage race.

Ricochet spreads weapon pressure to nearby targets, helping gun builds handle clustered enemies and summons. Its counter value grows when an enemy setup gives you several useful targets to hit from one safe angle, rather than a single isolated opponent.

Rusted Barrel reduces an enemy's fire rate, making sustained gun trades easier to manage. Apply it during the exchange you want to change, then use the reduced weapon pressure to contest the wave, reposition, or return damage.

Scourge pairs defensive resistance with a close-range aura that damages enemies based on maximum health. It suits heroes who can stay near a large-health target without losing the fight simply to maintain aura uptime.

Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.

Silencer turns sustained weapon hits into pressure against ability-reliant enemies, reducing outgoing spirit damage and building toward silence. It fits gun users who can stay on a target long enough to restrict the cast that would otherwise turn the fight.

Siphon Bullets creates a temporary health swing through repeated weapon hits, stealing a percentage of the enemy's maximum health. Against a large-health target, sustained contact and a coordinated finish help convert that temporary advantage before the stolen health returns.

Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.

Spellbreaker helps against spirit-heavy burst through spirit and debuff resistance plus periodic mitigation of a large spirit hit. Its protection is most valuable when available for the ability that matters, rather than spent on an earlier qualifying hit.

Spirit Burn rewards builds that can reach its spirit-damage trigger, adding an explosion, damage over time, and healing reduction. It combines damage scaling with anti-sustain pressure, but you must trigger the effect before the enemy's recovery decides the fight.

Spirit Resilience provides consistent passive protection against spirit damage. It helps when abilities keep wearing you down across multiple exchanges, giving you a baseline defense while you focus on positioning, cooldowns, and your own contribution to the fight.
Spirit Sap reduces a target’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist. Use it before a spell trade to weaken their Spirit-scaling damage and help your team’s spirit damage land harder.

Spirit Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of spirit damage, helping absorb what follows. It is useful when the opening ability hit starts a dangerous trade and a shield gives you time to reach cover or return manageable damage.

Stamina Mastery supports matchups that demand repeated movement, including successive dodges and vertical escapes. The extra flexibility helps only if you keep a reserve for the next threat instead of spending every movement option on the first exchange.

Suppressor lets spirit-damage users reduce an enemy's fire rate through their damage pressure. It is useful when your spirit damage can reach a gun carry consistently, helping your team trade with less sustained weapon pressure.

Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.

Toxic Bullets gives weapon users anti-heal and percentage-health bleed after repeated shooting. It fits carries who can keep landing shots on a sustain target, with the application built before the enemy's important healing window.

Unstoppable protects a planned commitment from crowd control. Activate it before the dangerous control sequence begins, especially when repeated disables would stop you from completing an engage or dealing damage. You still need a position that survives the incoming damage.

Veil Walker uses veil routes to give you speed and stealth for a safer approach or rotation. Its counter value comes from changing the angle an enemy can pressure, rather than expecting movement benefits while staying exposed in a direct duel.

Warp Stone gives you an immediate position change and bullet resistance, helping escape a close threat or committed damage angle. Pick a destination that removes follow-up pressure; teleporting within the same danger wastes much of the opportunity.

Weapon Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of weapon damage, helping absorb follow-up pressure. Use that shield window to reach cover or return a manageable trade instead of staying exposed until the next burst overwhelms you.

abrams.name: Abrams
abrams.title: How to Play Abrams in Deadlock | DIB
abrams.meta: Learn how to play Abrams in Deadlock: close-range fights, safe approaches, and avoiding predictable melee. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
abrams.ogTitle: Abrams Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
abrams.goal: Get close to a reachable enemy and hold their attention while your teammates attack. Your job can also be stopping someone who is chasing your team’s damage dealers.
abrams.positioning: Play towards the front of your team, with a wall or corner you can use to approach. Keep allies close enough to shoot whoever you catch. Against enemies on rooftops or across open ground, change your route instead of running straight through their fire.
fight: Look for an enemy near a wall, stepping forward to collect souls, or already occupied by a teammate. Shoulder Charge can pin them for a close exchange. Use Siphon Life while enemies remain nearby, and keep firing your shotgun between safe melee attacks.

You do not need to keep punching until someone dies. If enemies back away or prepare a parry, shoot or break off the exchange. Seismic Impact can start a fight your allies can join, but it can also stop an enemy threatening a teammate.
phases: Early game
Collect trooper souls near cover. Look for a wall pin when your partner can help, and break off the exchange if the enemy backs away.
Mid game
Move with a damage-dealing teammate and catch someone they can shoot. Turn a kill or retreat into lane pressure instead of chasing the next enemy.
Late game
Stay close enough to protect your team. Use Seismic Impact for a supported catch or stop someone diving your damage dealer.
abrams.threat: Move back around cover towards your team. Give your recovery time to work instead of absorbing more free shots; being durable does not make a solo fight against several enemies safe.
strengths: Shotgun and melee attacks reward reaching enemies safely.
Cover gives his healing time to restore lost health.
Wall pins and group control create allied shooting opportunities.
weaknesses: Long approaches
Distant enemies can damage him before he reaches useful range.
Predictable punches
Repeated heavy melee gives enemies opportunities to parry.
Reduced healing
Healing reduction makes extended close fights harder to sustain.
matchups: Flight and ranged gunfire can deny your close contact.
Cross through cover and pressure her landing position with help; avoid chasing directly beneath exposed flight.
Binding Word punishes a close commitment after your movement is spent.
Keep a retreat route and avoid spending every movement option to start the exchange while his catch is ready.
Haze wants uninterrupted shooting into your damage dealers.
Stay close enough to disrupt her commitment instead of chasing a different enemy while she shoots your teammate.
abrams.struggling: Protect a teammate and collect nearby souls instead of forcing a charge you cannot survive.
abrams.tip: A wall pin helps, but do not assume every heavy punch afterwards is safe from a parry.
mistakes: Being shot while trying to reach distant enemies.
Repeated heavy punches into someone waiting to parry; items reducing your healing.
proTips: Siphon Life keeps working while you move, dash, shoot, and cast — you never need to stand still for it.
Shoulder Charge pulls enemies along with you and travels farther when you collide with a hero, so aim to hit someone first.
Seismic Impact can collide with flying enemies mid-crash and drag them down into the slam.

apollo.name: Apollo
apollo.title: How to Play Apollo in Deadlock | DIB
apollo.meta: Learn how to play Apollo in Deadlock: dueling, choosing an approach, and keeping an escape route. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
apollo.ogTitle: Apollo Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
apollo.goal: Win short close-range exchanges against an exposed enemy, then finish them when it is safe. You want a controlled duel rather than everyone on the enemy team attacking you.
apollo.positioning: Play around the side of a fight with cover and a route back to allies. Stay close enough to threaten your lunges, but avoid spending every movement option just to reach someone. Tight or crowded routes can make both your attack and escape harder to manage.
fight: Practise the timing of Flawless Advance so your lunges are deliberate. Attack when an enemy is occupied, has missed an important ability, or cannot easily retreat. Use Riposte in response to an attack they have actually committed, rather than guessing repeatedly while exposed.

Mix your attacks with gunfire and movement instead of pressing everything at once. Look for a wounded target for Itani Lo Sahn, but check where the attack will leave you. A finish that strands you inside the enemy team can throw away the advantage.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise lunge timing in controlled exchanges. Preserve a movement option instead of spending everything to reach the enemy laner.
Mid game
Look for separated enemies near a useful team fight. Check their backup before committing, and return to collecting souls when no safe duel exists.
Late game
Attack a reachable target after dangerous enemy control is spent. Finish safely, then leave before the rest of the team turns on you.
apollo.threat: Use your remaining movement to return towards allies. If Riposte misses or your target gains backup, stop forcing the duel and wait until your important tools are ready again.
strengths: Timed attacks reward picking a manageable isolated fight.
Riposte can punish an enemy committing an attack.
Movement helps maintain contact with an exposed enemy.
weaknesses: Timing dependence
Missed lunges or a failed counter waste important opportunities.
Spent movement
Using every approach tool can leave no safe exit.
Grouped protection
Several enemies can punish a duel before he finishes.
matchups: Repeated close attacks create timing opportunities, but wall pins remain dangerous.
Fight away from a useful wall angle and use Riposte for a committed attack instead of guessing while already pinned.
She can damage you before your close attacks connect.
Use cover and a side approach; keep movement for leaving if you cannot reach a useful fight.
A close single-target hold can deny your duelling movement.
Track their approach and wait until they are occupied before committing onto someone beside them.
apollo.struggling: Take short exchanges near allies; avoid betting your remaining health on a missed counter.
apollo.tip: Practise the lunge timing against bots before trying to chain several attacks in a real fight.
mistakes: Missing Riposte while already committed close to enemies.
Spending every movement option before their teammates arrive.
proTips: Perfect Hold on Flawless Advance heals 35 HP per hero hit — timing is sustain, not just damage.
Riposte upgrades grant 75% lifesteal against your chosen target for 13 seconds, so always pick the duelist you'll keep fighting.
Apollo gains +60% bullet resist during Flawless Advance lunges, letting him tank return fire while charging the perfect hit.

baba.name: Baba
baba.title: How to Play Baba in Deadlock | DIB
baba.meta: Learn how to play Baba in Deadlock: disrupting enemies and supporting your team from useful positions. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
baba.ogTitle: Baba Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
baba.goal: Weaken enemies and help your team win the next exchange. Use Threadsap to strengthen your shooting, and choose whether your team needs protection, silence, or extra damage from your brew.
baba.positioning: Play near your team’s close-range fighters, using cover to get a useful Threadsap angle. You need enemies within reach, but should not be the easiest target for several ranged guns. Keep a nearby ally and a route out when preparing a longer attack.
fight: Open a shooting exchange with Threadsap when you can land it safely, then use the empowered bullets rather than treating it as a separate poke. Aim at reachable enemies instead of chasing a particular caster through their whole team.

Watch Baba’s Brew and pause on the effect you want before the important moment. Use Granny Long Legs to reach or leave a useful position. Commit Feed The Birds when teammates can exploit it and nearby enemies cannot freely interrupt you.
phases: Early game
Collect souls from cover and land Threadsap before a shooting exchange. Practise choosing a useful brew instead of casting without checking its effect.
Mid game
Travel near allies and prepare the brew your next fight needs. Use empowered shooting without walking beyond the team’s protection.
Late game
Look for a supported Feed The Birds opportunity. Keep nearby interrupters in view and change position if enemies can freely shoot you.
baba.threat: Reposition towards allies with your movement and use a helpful brew effect. Avoid repeating bench melee attacks into a waiting parry, or trying to finish a long channel while everyone shoots you.
strengths: Stolen spirit makes follow-up gunfire more threatening.
Brew choices provide protection, silence or additional damage.
Her ultimate creates a window teammates can exploit.
weaknesses: Setup dependence
Poor thread hits or brew choices weaken the next exchange.
Interruptible commitment
Nearby control can spoil a longer attack.
Exposed approaches
Ranged gunfire punishes reaching forward without cover or support.
matchups: Pocket needs a close spell-damage opening and defensive tools to leave.
Look for a safe Threadsap hit before trading; prepare silence for the approach rather than following the escape alone.
Nearby group control threatens a long Feed The Birds commitment.
Keep track of Dynamo and channel only from a position where he cannot freely approach you.
Long firing angles punish stepping forward for your setup.
Use cover to land Threadsap, then take a short shooting exchange instead of standing exposed beneath her angle.
baba.struggling: Stay near allies and provide useful brew effects instead of diving to force damage.
baba.tip: Granny Long Legs changes your melee attacks; those attacks can be parried, so avoid repeating them blindly.
mistakes: Starting a long attack while enemies can interrupt you.
Taking ranged gunfire or repeating parryable bench attacks.
proTips: Later bread ticks deal the most damage — the first tick is only about 4% of the maximum, so channel patience pays off.
Brewing continues through crowd control, so the pot keeps cycling even while you're stunned.
Being stunned during Feed The Birds triggers the bird bombardment early instead of canceling it.

bebop.name: Bebop
bebop.title: How to Play Bebop in Deadlock | DIB
bebop.meta: Learn how to play Bebop in Deadlock: finding hooks and turning catches into fights your team can follow. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
bebop.ogTitle: Bebop Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
bebop.goal: Pull an exposed enemy towards your team so allies can attack them together. Between catches, keep using your weapon and look for damage opportunities without delivering a dangerous enemy into your teammates.
bebop.positioning: Use corners or the side of the lane to find a clear Hook path around troopers. Stand where a pulled enemy will arrive in allied damage. Keep a retreat nearby, especially after missing Hook; you lose much of your immediate catching threat while it is unavailable.
fight: Look for someone stepping out from cover, concentrating on your teammate, or standing apart from their team. Land Hook, attach Sticky Bomb, and add gunfire. Check what the target can do at close range before pulling them directly beside vulnerable allies.

Uppercut changes the target’s position, so use it when the direction helps the catch rather than automatically punching them away from your team. Hyper Beam needs a protected firing angle with enemies remaining in view; it is not a reason to stand exposed.
phases: Early game
Collect souls while threatening Hook from an angle around troopers. After a miss, return to cover instead of staying close to a ready enemy.
Mid game
Look for catches with a teammate who can supply damage. A successful catch should help you push a lane or contest an objective.
Late game
Pull an exposed target into allied damage, or use Hyper Beam from protection. Avoid handing a dangerous close fighter access to your vulnerable teammates.
bebop.threat: Back towards cover and allies after a missed catch or an enemy rush. Keep shooting from a safer position instead of walking forward just because your close abilities are available.
strengths: Hook can bring an exposed enemy into allied damage.
Attaching bombs adds damage during a controlled close exchange.
A protected beam angle can pressure a committed fight.
weaknesses: Missed catches
Losing Hook reduces immediate threat and invites enemy aggression.
Bad pull choices
Bringing a close fighter into allies can help the enemy.
Open commitments
Exposed positioning makes catches and long attacks easier to punish.
matchups: An exposed ranged position can become a supported catch.
Look for a clear Hook path when she shows in a reachable angle, and pull towards teammates ready to shoot.
Pulling a durable close fighter can give him access to vulnerable allies.
Choose a more exposed target or make sure your team can control and damage Abrams before delivering him.
A pulled initiator may gain an ideal position for group control.
Avoid pulling him into tightly grouped allies unless you have immediate coordinated damage and control ready.
bebop.struggling: Catch near teammates and let their damage finish the target instead of hunting alone.
bebop.tip: Hook being ready is a threat even before you cast it. After a miss, give enemies less opportunity to rush you.
mistakes: Missing Hook and staying exposed afterwards.
Pulling a dangerous close fighter into your own teammates.
proTips: Bomb damage snapshots your spirit power at cast time — buffs must be active when you attach, not when it detonates.
Landing Exploding Uppercut on a hero refreshes Grapple Arm instantly, so hook-into-uppercut chains into a second grab.
Uppercut grants doubled gun range, faster spin-up, and +30% weapon damage for 9 seconds — your beam gun becomes a real finisher.

billy.name: Billy
billy.title: How to Play Billy in Deadlock | DIB
billy.meta: Learn how to play Billy in Deadlock: reaching melee range and choosing fights you can keep attacking in. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
billy.ogTitle: Billy Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
billy.goal: Stay close to a useful target, interrupt their movement, and combine gunfire with melee while teammates help. You are trying to keep a favourable fight going, not simply land the most punches.
billy.positioning: Approach from a corner or the side with allies within shooting distance. Fight where enemies cannot easily keep retreating in a straight line. Do not spend Rising Ram crossing open ground if it leaves you alone beyond your team’s reach.
fight: Once Blasted is unlocked, melee hits help restore ammunition. Activate it for a close fight you can maintain, then weave gunfire with safe melee attacks. Use Rising Ram and Bashdown to create openings rather than throwing both out while still too far away.

Watch enemy parries and use shooting when another punch is predictable. Chain Gang is useful when nearby enemies can be pulled into a fight your team wants; check that allies are ready and keep targets in a useful position rather than chasing every escape.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise shooting between safe melee hits once Blasted is unlocked. Do not assume every enemy will allow repeated punches.
Mid game
Approach from cover with allied damage nearby. Use your knock-ups to keep a reachable enemy in a fight your team can win.
Late game
Use Chain Gang when allies can attack the pulled enemies. Maintain a useful close exchange without following one target far beyond your team.
billy.threat: Move back towards nearby allies and use your disruption to stop pursuit. If you are silenced or your approach tools are spent, do not assume more health means you can keep walking through gunfire.
strengths: Melee ammunition recovery helps combine shooting with close attacks.
Knock-ups create openings to maintain a close fight.
His tools reward maintaining a supported exchange.
weaknesses: Distant targets
Enemies can keep shooting while he struggles to reach them.
Predictable melee
Repeated punches can be anticipated and parried.
Disabled tools
Silence or spent approach abilities can leave him exposed.
matchups: She needs space and uninterrupted shooting to build useful damage.
Approach with allied help and use disruption to deny her shooting window, without chasing away from your team.
Aerial ranged pressure can waste your approach without giving close contact.
Use cover and wait for a reachable position instead of spending Rising Ram on an unsupported open chase.
Pocket relies on movement and evasion during a close attack.
Threaten Chain Gang with allies ready, but keep shooting and avoid assuming every defensive option is already unavailable.
billy.struggling: Use control to stop enemies reaching your damage dealer rather than chasing past your team.
billy.tip: Light melee can help maintain your gunfire without repeatedly risking an obvious heavy punch.
mistakes: Enemies keeping their distance after Rising Ram is used.
Being silenced or repeating predictable melee attacks.
proTips: Meleeing McGinnis's wall breaks segments faster since your light attacks don't interrupt reload.
Rising Ram's cooldown halves on impact, so land it on the first target to chain into a second.
Re-entering the tether radius before it ends re-tethers runners — cutting corners keeps them chained.

calico.name: Calico
calico.title: How to Play Calico in Deadlock | DIB
calico.meta: Learn how to play Calico in Deadlock: setting up ambushes and choosing when to commit or escape. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
calico.ogTitle: Calico Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
calico.goal: Approach an exposed enemy unnoticed, deal a short burst at close range, and survive their response. You are looking for a distracted or separated target rather than starting a fight against the whole team.
calico.positioning: Use side routes and cover before entering combat. Ava helps you travel and hide your movement on the minimap, but enemies can still see you. Choose an approach that brings you back towards allies if the attack fails instead of trapping you behind several opponents.
fight: Look for someone busy shooting your teammate, collecting souls alone, or using an important escape. Use Leaping Slash and Gloom Bombs when you can connect at close range, then add your weapon damage rather than immediately using every defensive tool for more burst.

Keep Return to Shadows available to avoid a dangerous reply or change position. If the target survives and gains protection, leave and look for another opening. Do not assume Ava will instantly get you out after enemies have already begun damaging you.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and take short close exchanges only when safe. Avoid losing your health while walking through gunfire to force Leaping Slash.
Mid game
Clear a nearby wave, then use a side route to threaten a separated enemy. Do not abandon income for a long search without a target.
Late game
Wait for teammates to occupy the enemy’s attention. Burst an exposed target, then use your defensive option before the entire team focuses you.
calico.threat: Use your defensive window to move towards safety, not remain surrounded hoping the next burst wins. If you cannot reach a safe exit, stay with allies before attempting another side attack.
strengths: Ava helps reach a side angle before combat.
Her short attack sequence threatens exposed enemies.
Return to Shadows can protect a well-timed disengagement.
weaknesses: Protected targets
Nearby enemy help can outlast or punish the first burst.
Exposed entry
Taking damage before reaching a target weakens the attempt.
Blocked escape
Control or a poor route can ruin her exit.
matchups: A ranged hero focused on shooting may expose a side approach.
Approach before being noticed, check trap routes, and burst only when his nearby protection is occupied.
A close hold can stop you leaving after your first attack.
Keep their position in view and preserve an exit; avoid entering beside them while they are waiting to protect someone.
A delayed catch threatens a close attack when your escape is spent.
Take a short exchange with a route out; leave before a catch forces you to remain in his preferred fight.
calico.struggling: Clear safe waves and wait for a distracted target; avoid trying to burst a healthy protected enemy.
calico.tip: Being hidden on the minimap is not the same as being invisible to enemies looking at you.
mistakes: Committing onto enemies protected by several teammates.
Assuming Ava is invisibility or an instant escape after taking fire.
proTips: Aim Gloom Bombs at a hero's center of mass to land all bombs within 8m.
Leaping Slash's dash stops on the first hero hit — angle around tanks to reach the carry.
Ava can slip through map vents, but don't let her timer expire inside one or you'll bleed HP.

celeste.name: Celeste
celeste.title: How to Play Celeste in Deadlock | DIB
celeste.meta: Learn how to play Celeste in Deadlock: ranged spirit pressure and dealing damage while staying near cover. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
celeste.ogTitle: Celeste Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
celeste.goal: Use movement and spell combinations to pressure enemies while making their return attacks awkward. You want useful spell angles and repeated damage opportunities, rather than hovering still above everyone’s gunfire.
celeste.positioning: Play behind or beside your team’s close fighters, near cover you can return to. Use your air movement to change angles, not to remain permanently exposed. Get close enough for your spell setup without drifting so far ahead that nobody can protect you.
fight: Use Light Eater to prepare a damage exchange, then aim Radiant Daggers where enemies are likely to move. A target retreating through a narrow route or occupied by an ally is easier to hit than someone freely dodging in open ground.

Dazzling Trick helps protect a committed exchange, but do not spend it casually before an enemy rush. Look for grouped enemies for Shining Wonder and keep adding useful attacks from a safe angle. If enemies hide, change position rather than following them blindly around a corner.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise Light Eater into useful spell damage from cover. Use movement to change your angle rather than remaining exposed overhead.
Mid game
Move with allies towards useful fights and find a side angle for spell pressure. Keep Dazzling Trick available if enemies can rush you.
Late game
Pressure committed enemies and look for grouped targets for Shining Wonder. Keep moving between useful angles without separating from allied protection.
celeste.threat: Move towards cover and allied protection while using your defensive tools. Being mobile does not prevent an enemy from landing a burst when you pause in an exposed position.
strengths: Air movement helps choose useful attack positions.
Prepared spell sequences reward landing the setup.
Her barrier threatens enemies who commit close.
weaknesses: Missed setup
Mobile targets can avoid spells placed without a clear opening.
Exposed movement
Floating in view still allows several enemies to shoot her.
Spent protection
A rush is more dangerous after her barrier is used.
matchups: He needs close contact and a useful wall angle.
Use movement and cover to keep spell pressure while avoiding a grounded approach beside a wall he can use.
Floating in the open gives her a clear ranged firing line.
Use cover and change angles instead of treating air movement as protection from her gun.
A direct approach and hold can punish committing beyond your allies.
Keep your protection and distance available; attack from beside your team rather than hovering alone over their position.
celeste.struggling: Use spell pressure near allies and preserve your barrier rather than forcing a close duel.
celeste.tip: Your mobility helps you choose an angle; floating in full view still lets enemies shoot you.
mistakes: Floating where several enemies can shoot you.
Spending your protection before an enemy rushes you.
proTips: Carny Life homes at a ~45° angle and even tracks soul orbs — fire near corpses to secure them.
Cast Radiant Daggers inside buildings: the beam hits every vertical layer in its radius.
T3 Dazzling Trick lets Shining Wonder bounce off your own barrier and resets its timer.

deadman-danny.name: Deadman Danny
deadman-danny.title: How to Play Deadman Danny in Deadlock | DIB
deadman-danny.meta: Learn how to play Deadman Danny in Deadlock: choosing aerial approaches and committing alongside your team. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
deadman-danny.ogTitle: Deadman Danny Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
deadman-danny.goal: Set up enemies for charged shots, then use flight to create a useful attack or catch. Your goal is a controlled aerial approach with a planned landing, rather than diving whenever the jetpack is available.
deadman-danny.positioning: Begin from cover beside or behind teammates. Before flying over a wall, check where enemies are and where you can land without being surrounded. Height creates a new attack angle, but also exposes you to guns and control from several directions.
fight: Place Strix Salvo along a target’s likely movement and follow a mark with a charged shot. Start by practising this ground-based exchange. You can contribute useful damage without combining every attack with an aggressive dive into the enemy team.

Watch your jetpack heat before extending flight. Jettison Fuel can help manage heat while damaging an enemy, but it does not replace a safe landing plan. Use Close the Deal on a reachable target when allies can benefit from the resulting position.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise Strix Salvo marks into charged shots from cover. Learn the flight heat and landing controls before combining them with aggression.
Mid game
Find an aerial angle near a fight your teammates can join. Choose a safe landing before flying over a wall or starting a catch.
Late game
Attack exposed enemies with allied help and watch your health. Leave yourself a controlled landing rather than extending flight into a forced overheat dive.
deadman-danny.threat: Land somewhere defensible before heat makes the choice for you. A missed overheat dive can stun you, and health spent on your own attacks still leaves you vulnerable to enemy damage.
strengths: Salvo marks strengthen a following charged-shot opportunity.
Flight reaches attack angles blocked at street level.
A supported catch can move an enemy into a useful fight.
weaknesses: Landing commitment
Heat can force a dive before a safe opening appears.
Health spending
Self-damage makes an enemy response more dangerous.
Airborne exposure
Enemies can shoot or control him while he approaches.
matchups: A prepared firing position may be less protected from an unusual approach.
Choose an aerial side angle with a safe landing and allied follow-up; do not dive into the whole setup alone.
Landing near ready group control can remove your chance to leave.
Track Dynamo before choosing the landing; use marked shots from cover if he is protecting the destination.
Your flight can expose you to a ranged gunner already watching above the fight.
Use structures to break the sightline and plan a controlled landing instead of hovering through her firing angle.
deadman-danny.struggling: Use marked shots from cover and skip risky dives while you rebuild health and income.
deadman-danny.tip: An overheat dive that hits no hero can stun you. Do not learn the heat limit by diving into a full team.
mistakes: Overheating into an empty or heavily defended landing.
Losing health through self-damage before enemies attack back.
proTips: Firing a charged shot at your feet with an enemy in the blast removes self-damage but keeps the rocket-jump knockback.
Jettison Fuel's backblast can apply a mark with the right upgrade, feeding your whole combo.
The ult moves to the target regardless of distance — but walls and Frozen Shelter stop it cold.

the-doorman.name: The Doorman
the-doorman.title: How to Play The Doorman in Deadlock | DIB
the-doorman.meta: Learn how to play The Doorman in Deadlock: using rotations and displacement to create opportunities for allies. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
the-doorman.ogTitle: The Doorman Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
the-doorman.goal: Help your team reach useful fights, move enemies out of safe positions, and create a temporary numbers advantage. Think about where everyone will end up, not only whether you can land a catch.
the-doorman.positioning: Play close enough to help a teammate without standing alone in front of the enemy team. Place Doorway exits in positions your team can safely use. Before taking a route yourself, check the other end and whether nearby allies can follow you.
fight: Use Call Bell when your teammate is ready for a shooting exchange. Luggage Cart can move an enemy towards allied damage or disrupt an approach. Check the direction first: moving someone out of your team’s shots can waste the opening you created.

Use Doorway before a rotation is urgent, and tell teammates where it leads. Hotel Guest temporarily removes an enemy from the current fight; use that time to help your team attack whoever remains instead of simply waiting for the removed target to return.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and help your partner’s shooting exchanges with Call Bell. Practise placing usable doors outside combat before relying on them to escape.
Mid game
Prepare routes to the next objective and communicate the destination. Use a catch when nearby allies can exploit where the enemy lands.
Late game
Remove an important enemy temporarily and help attack the remaining team. Keep thinking about the returning target and whether your exits are still safe.
the-doorman.threat: Move towards a prepared safe route or nearby allies. Avoid attempting another close catch while already surrounded; a clever door placement does not guarantee its exit is still safe.
strengths: Prepared doors help teammates reach useful positions.
Moving a target can improve allied access to them.
Removing one enemy changes who can contribute immediately.
weaknesses: Route planning
An unsafe exit can turn a shortcut into danger.
Close exposure
Attempting a catch alone leaves little protection.
Team coordination
Clever movement is wasted when allies cannot use it.
matchups: A sustained shooter benefits from remaining in the current fight.
Consider Hotel Guest when removing her creates an immediate advantage, then help teammates attack the remaining enemies.
An unsupported close catch gives him the range he wants.
Use Call Bell and gunfire beside your partner; choose a cart direction that does not strand you next to him.
An approach from height can bypass the route you are watching.
Check above and beside the fight, and keep a safe door route rather than assuming one front-facing setup covers everything.
the-doorman.struggling: Create safe routes and disrupt nearby enemies rather than walking alone into a close catch.
the-doorman.tip: Hotel Guest removes a target temporarily. Help your team use that time instead of waiting for the target to return.
mistakes: Placing a route without checking both exits.
Being caught alone while trying to move an enemy.
proTips: Bells can be shot or melee-detonated early; ring them behind cover.
Unstoppable effects drop cart targets — check before you drag.
At T3, doorways connect spawn to guardians for instant defense.

drifter.name: Drifter
drifter.title: How to Play Drifter in Deadlock | DIB
drifter.meta: Learn how to play Drifter in Deadlock: isolating targets and choosing safe opportunities to commit. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
drifter.ogTitle: Drifter Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
drifter.goal: Find an enemy too far from teammates to get help, then use your isolation damage to win the close fight. Keep checking for backup rather than assuming a target remains alone.
drifter.positioning: Move through covered side routes and approach within manageable range before relying on Stalker’s Mark. Stay aware of your own route back. Being behind an enemy is useful only if you can finish or leave before the rest of their team arrives.
fight: Bloodscent helps identify isolated targets and rewards fighting them. Look for lone farmers or late arrivals, but check the map before committing. Stalker’s Mark is easier to connect when you are already close or the enemy has spent movement trying to escape.

Use the mark’s reactivation to maintain contact, then Rend and shoot at close range. If an ally arrives to protect your target, reassess instead of continuing the same duel. Around teamfights, wait at an edge for separation rather than charging through the full enemy group.
phases: Early game
Collect souls from cover and practise reliable close marks. Avoid taking free ranged damage just to walk up to a healthy enemy.
Mid game
Look for isolated farmers or late arrivals while maintaining your own income. Recheck nearby enemy movement before taking the mark’s teleport.
Late game
Work around the edge while allies occupy the main group. Attack an enemy who separates, rather than starting inside everyone’s protection.
drifter.threat: Return towards cover and allies instead of teleporting farther into danger. If you are behind in souls, help finish an already weakened enemy rather than betting on a full-health isolated duel.
strengths: Lone enemies provide a more favourable fighting condition.
A landed mark can maintain contact through an escape.
weaknesses: Enemy backup
A duel changes quickly when the target gains nearby help.
Missed mark
Unreliable entry can leave him unable to maintain contact.
Poor recovery fights
Falling behind makes unsupported healthy-target duels riskier.
matchups: A lone ranged farmer may have limited nearby help.
Approach through cover after checking his team’s positions and trap route; do not teleport if protection has arrived.
Their close hold can stop a finishing attempt and protect your target.
Look for an isolated enemy elsewhere or wait until they commit before entering near them.
Her defensive timing and nearby partner can spoil a quick solo finish.
Confirm isolation and avoid spending every tool before Stone Form or allied help has been accounted for.
drifter.struggling: Collect safe souls and help finish an already weakened target instead of forcing a full-health duel.
drifter.tip: Recheck the map before teleporting: a previously lone target may now have teammates nearby.
mistakes: Teleporting onto a target whose teammates are now nearby.
Trying to force a full-health duel while behind in souls.
proTips: The mark can tag the Rejuvenator, letting you teleport to it after an objective fight
Landing Rend within close range silences enemies with the right upgrade, cutting off their escape
Mark's bleed scales off current health, so opening on wounded targets melts them fastest

dynamo.name: Dynamo
dynamo.title: How to Play Dynamo in Deadlock | DIB
dynamo.meta: Learn how to play Dynamo in Deadlock: supporting allies and setting up fights your team can follow. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
dynamo.ogTitle: Dynamo Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
dynamo.goal: Help teammates keep fighting and hold enemies where allies can damage them. A good save or a small reliable catch can matter as much as a large Singularity.
dynamo.positioning: Play near teammates who can use your control, usually just behind or beside the person taking the first contact. Stay close enough to protect an ally without being the easiest enemy target. Before committing forward, check whether teammates can actually reach the area.
fight: In lane, use Kinetic Pulse to create a shooting opening for you and your partner. Keep firing while the target is disrupted instead of treating the knock-up as your entire contribution. Use healing to sustain a useful position when your team can remain nearby.

Quantum Entanglement can avoid a dangerous attack, so do not spend it only to get closer. For Singularity, look for enemies committed to an objective or already occupied by teammates. Check nearby interrupters and whether your allies are ready before beginning the channel.
phases: Early game
Collect souls alongside your partner. Use Kinetic Pulse and gunfire together, preserving a defensive option for an enemy rush.
Mid game
Collect nearby income between useful team fights. Stay near the next contested objective rather than wandering alone while your team needs control.
Late game
Use Singularity when allies can deal damage during it, or control a smaller threat to save a teammate. Do not wait endlessly for a perfect catch.
dynamo.threat: Use your defensive movement and control to return towards allied protection. If someone attacks your damage dealer, turning back to stop them may be more useful than continuing towards the enemy team.
strengths: Kinetic Pulse creates a clearer shooting opportunity.
Healing helps allies continue using a position.
Singularity can hold enemies for coordinated damage.
weaknesses: Missing follow-up
Control has less value when allies cannot attack.
Interruptions
Enemy control can stop a long commitment.
Overcommitted entry
Spending defence to enter can leave no useful escape.
matchups: His delayed explosion creates a recognisable incoming danger.
Keep Quantum Entanglement for a timed defensive response when possible; do not spend it casually before his approach.
Static Charge and sustained area pressure punish an exposed channel position.
Track the delayed stun and his firing area before committing Singularity; use cover and allied pressure to create a safer opening.
A committed shooter can threaten an ally while focused on damage.
Stay within protective reach and use control to stop her attack when your team can follow up.
dynamo.struggling: Help teammates with control and healing; do not wait alone for a perfect multi-enemy ultimate.
dynamo.tip: A smaller Singularity that saves an ally can be better than waiting for the entire enemy team to group.
mistakes: Holding enemies where no teammate can shoot them.
Being interrupted during a long commitment.
proTips: Kinetic Pulse has a 0.42s cast delay and travels along the ground, so enemies can jump over it
Quantum Entanglement resets your air dashes and jumps, and can teleport allies through walls with clever targeting
Meleeing during Rejuvenating Aurora's channel does not break the heal, so farm objectives while sustaining

graves.name: Graves
graves.title: How to Play Graves in Deadlock | DIB
graves.meta: Learn how to play Graves in Deadlock: using summons and prepared positions to pressure objectives. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
graves.ogTitle: Graves Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
graves.goal: Build summon pressure around a lane or objective so enemies must spend time clearing it or fight through it. Help your team gain ground while keeping yourself and the valuable setup alive.
graves.positioning: Take a covered position near the area your team wants to control. Keep Grasping Hands between likely enemy approaches and your setup when useful. Avoid standing well ahead of your summons or following a retreating enemy into open space where your preparation no longer helps.
fight: Collect the nearby deaths that feed Jar of Dead, then send Deadheads towards a useful target. Your weapon helps direct their attention, so keep actively participating instead of throwing summons and waiting. Use their pressure to clear space or make an enemy spend time responding.

Before an objective fight, place Borrowed Decree where enemies cannot immediately walk up and destroy it. Protect the approach rather than chasing a distant finish. When enemies move elsewhere, move your attention with the team instead of defending an area that no longer matters.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and build Jar of Dead pressure while staying near cover. Avoid exposing yourself ahead of the summons just to force a gun exchange.
Mid game
Move your prepared pressure towards objectives your team can contest. Set up before enemies arrive and make them spend time responding.
Late game
Protect Borrowed Decree and the routes around it. Move with your team when the important fight shifts instead of defending an irrelevant setup.
graves.threat: Use your prepared ground and teammates to slow the approach while retreating to cover. If someone gets past the setup, prioritise survival instead of trying to out-duel them in the open.
strengths: Enemies must spend time responding to repeated threats.
Setup makes important objective approaches more costly.
Weapon targeting helps guide summoned pressure onto a priority.
weaknesses: Rushed setup
Fast attackers can reach her before preparation matters.
Cleared summons
Exposed valuable summons lose their impact quickly.
Limited retreat
Leaving prepared ground can expose a weak open-field fight.
matchups: A wall catch can take him past your summons into a close fight.
Keep Grasping Hands on a useful approach and avoid positioning beside a wall pin while far from your partner.
Long-range gunfire punishes open positions outside your effective beam range.
Collect souls from cover and use summons for pressure instead of walking into her firing line to shoot back.
Summons make a focused gunner split attention between you and additional threats.
Direct Deadheads towards her while staying protected; do not walk close just because she is clearing your summons.
graves.struggling: Use summons to clear safe lanes and defend an objective; avoid walking into open ranged exchanges.
graves.tip: Protect Borrowed Decree’s position instead of dropping it where enemies can immediately destroy it.
mistakes: Letting enemies rush through your setup directly onto you.
Leaving valuable summons where enemies can clear them freely.
proTips: Your weapon deals double damage every 13 consecutive hits on the same target, so commit to one enemy
Air-dashing while firing pauses ammo consumption, letting you chase longer without reloading
Ghouls explode on death dealing percentage-based damage, so let them suicide onto tanks

grey-talon.name: Grey Talon
grey-talon.title: How to Play Grey Talon in Deadlock | DIB
grey-talon.meta: Learn how to play Grey Talon in Deadlock: backline positioning and landing long-range Charged Shots safely. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
grey-talon.ogTitle: Grey Talon Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
grey-talon.goal: Play behind your teammates and use Charged Shot to damage enemies from long range. Let close-range allies draw attention while you take clear shots and help finish the fight.
grey-talon.positioning: Choose a position behind your teammates with a clear view of the enemy and nearby cover. High ground can improve your angle, but keep a route back towards allied protection. Move when enemies begin approaching your position, rather than waiting until they are beside you.
fight: Look for targets distracted by teammates, moving through a narrow route, or held still by an ally. These are easier Charged Shot opportunities than someone freely dodging. Keep using your bow between abilities when you can safely land useful shots.
