Place Spirit Snare on a route an enemy could use to reach you or escape the fight. Flight can open a firing angle, but enemies can still shoot you. Move into cover before steering Guided Owl, then aim to help an ongoing fight or finish a wounded escape.
phases: Early game
Collect trooper souls from cover and aim Charged Shot when enemies step forward or pause to fire. Avoid walking closer just to force a hit.
Mid game
Support nearby fights from behind allies while collecting waves and safe camps between opportunities. Set traps on likely approaches to your firing position.
Late game
Choose a protected sightline on the main fight. Use Guided Owl from cover for a useful follow-up, and reposition early when enemies approach.
grey-talon.threat: Retreat towards teammates and use your trap to make pursuit harder. Avoid standing your ground alone against a close attacker, or continuing to steer an owl while your own hero is in danger.
strengths: Charged Shot contributes from behind close-range teammates.
Allied control or distraction creates clearer shot opportunities.
Guided Owl can influence a fight away from his position.
weaknesses: Close attackers
An enemy reaching him disrupts his preferred fighting distance.
Blocked sightlines
Cover can deny shots and force him to reposition.
Aiming exposure
Shot or owl focus can distract from nearby threats.
matchups: He needs close range and useful wall angles to pressure you.
Keep ranged shots from cover, trap an approach and move early when he begins closing; avoid fighting beside an easy pin.
He can approach from height, so a rooftop is not automatic safety.
Watch above the fight and preserve a route towards allies; relocate before his landing reaches your firing position.
An isolated shooting position gives her a catch-and-gun opportunity.
Avoid remaining alone on a predictable angle; move towards allied protection when she disappears from your view.
grey-talon.struggling: Use ranged damage and trap protection near allies rather than hunting distant finishes alone.
grey-talon.tip: Take cover before steering Guided Owl; your own hero still needs protection while you control it.
mistakes: An enemy reaching your firing position.
Steering Guided Owl while your own hero is exposed.
proTips: You can mantle and slide while holding a charged arrow — keep repositioning instead of standing still.
Shoot your own Spirit Snare with Charged Shot to trigger the curse early instead of waiting for it to arm.
Owl kills grant bonus spirit power, so save the ultimate for guaranteed finishes rather than opening with it.

haze.name: Haze
haze.title: How to Play Haze in Deadlock | DIB
haze.meta: Learn how to play Haze in Deadlock: building damage on a target and choosing safe flanking opportunities. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
haze.ogTitle: Haze Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
haze.goal: Build enough income to deal useful gun damage, then attack an exposed enemy while teammates occupy their attention. You want time to keep hitting a target rather than being everyone’s first target.
haze.positioning: Play beside or behind your team before taking a side angle into a fight. Use cover and Smoke Bomb to approach without crossing open enemy gunfire. Keep an escape route in mind: invisibility is not a reliable rescue once enemies are close and already tracking you.
fight: Fixation rewards repeated hits on the same enemy. Choose a target you can safely keep shooting instead of scattering a few bullets across everyone. Sleep Dagger gives you time to improve your position before firing; do not rush to wake the target from a poor angle.

Look for an enemy separated from protection, or enter after allies draw attention. Bullet Dance can punish a useful commitment, but check enemy control and defensive tools first. You can still contribute through ordinary shooting instead of waiting for a perfect ultimate opportunity.
phases: Early game
Prioritise trooper souls and safe shooting. Build Fixation on one target during a useful exchange instead of scattering damage across everyone.
Mid game
Collect waves and nearby camps, then join useful nearby fights. Use Smoke Bomb for a side approach without assuming it hides you at close range.
Late game
Let teammates draw attention before committing sustained fire or Bullet Dance. Check enemy control and defensive tools before entering a group.
haze.threat: Move back through cover towards allies and use Sleep Dagger if it creates a retreat opportunity. Do not assume Smoke Bomb immediately makes you safe: nearby enemies can see and continue tracking you.
strengths: Repeated hits build pressure on the same target.
Smoke Bomb helps find an unnoticed entry angle.
Sustained damage rewards entering after allies draw attention.
weaknesses: Weak entry timing
Starting first invites concentrated damage and control.
Close detection
Invisibility does not hide her from nearby enemies.
Interrupted damage
Defensive tools or control can spoil a committed attack.
matchups: Ready group control can stop your committed damage window.
Keep his location in view and approach from another angle or wait until he is occupied before entering.
A close hold can stop sustained shooting before you produce enough damage.
Do not enter directly beside them while they are waiting; keep distance and let teammates draw the commitment first.
An isolated ranged attacker may be occupied aiming away from your approach.
Use a covered side route, check traps and nearby allies, then take a supported dagger-and-shooting opening.
haze.struggling: Collect safe income and join nearby fights after allies draw attention; avoid gambling on solo kills.
haze.tip: Invisibility does not make you untouchable. Do not enter first and expect Smoke Bomb to rescue you.
mistakes: Being seen at close range despite Smoke Bomb.
Starting first into enemy control or splitting shots without building useful pressure.
proTips: Sleep Dagger doesn't break invisibility, so cast it while still hidden for a guaranteed setup.
Headshots stack Fixation three times faster — aim high to ramp damage quickly.
Bullet Dance fires with perfect accuracy, so use it while jumping to dodge return fire.

holliday.name: Holliday
holliday.title: How to Play Holliday in Deadlock | DIB
holliday.meta: Learn how to play Holliday in Deadlock: finding shooting angles and turning catches into team opportunities. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
holliday.ogTitle: Holliday Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
holliday.goal: Use accurate shots and a supported catch to make one enemy easy for your team to attack. Your goal is useful damage and positioning, not carrying someone somewhere allies cannot reach.
holliday.positioning: Play at a useful shooting distance with cover nearby, then use side angles or height to look for a catch. Before using Spirit Lasso, choose where you want the enemy to end up. Keep your route connected to teammates instead of landing behind the whole enemy team.
fight: Take patient Crackshot headshots when enemies pause to shoot, move predictably, or are disrupted by an ally. Powder Keg can threaten their space and add burst, but keep using your gun instead of waiting for every barrel setup to be perfect.

Use Bounce Pad to gain an angle or change position, and Spirit Lasso when teammates can exploit the catch. Moving during the lasso is optional: a stationary target near your team may be easier to finish than one you bounce away with.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and take patient Crackshot opportunities. Use barrels without walking into unnecessary close danger just to force the combination.
Mid game
Look for side approaches near allies and plan a lasso destination. Keep up income instead of travelling constantly for unsupported catches.
Late game
Catch an enemy where allies can keep attacking. Use movement during the lasso only if it improves the position rather than spoiling allied aim.
holliday.threat: Use movement to return towards cover and allies. Avoid spending Bounce Pad solely to continue a low-value chase if it leaves you unable to escape a closer enemy.
strengths: Patient headshots create strong individual damage opportunities.
Barrels and movement help prepare an attack.
Lasso can deliver a target into allied damage.
weaknesses: Aim dependence
Missed shots reduce the value of short openings.
Bad destinations
Moving a catch away can waste allied follow-up.
Spent movement
A close attacker is harder to escape after committing forward.
matchups: A direct close approach and wall pin can punish a spent movement tool.
Keep a covered retreat and avoid using Bounce Pad purely for damage while his approach remains ready.
An exposed ranged position can become a valuable displacement target.
Approach from a safe side and choose a lasso destination your team can shoot, rather than chasing into her protection.
Defensive evasion can make your intended catch window unreliable.
Watch which escape tool has been used and avoid spending all movement to chase a target still holding a safe exit.
holliday.struggling: Use ranged shots and a supported catch rather than spending every movement tool on a risky solo play.
holliday.tip: A Bounce Pad during a lasso is an option, not a requirement; moving the target can make allied shots harder.
mistakes: Dragging a target away from your team’s shots.
Using movement carelessly when an enemy can rush you.
proTips: Melee your own Powder Keg to knock it airborne into enemies for impact damage plus stacking burns.
Bounce pads extend Spirit Lasso's range — cast it mid-launch to grab targets you couldn't reach.
Activating Warp Stone during Spirit Lasso flings the victim much farther than the pull alone.

infernus.name: Infernus
infernus.title: How to Play Infernus in Deadlock | DIB
infernus.meta: Learn how to play Infernus in Deadlock: maintaining damage and choosing close fights you can survive. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
infernus.ogTitle: Infernus Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
infernus.goal: Keep enemies burning while staying alive long enough to attack again. You want a sustained close-to-mid-range fight your teammates can join, rather than a single unsupported dash through everyone.
infernus.positioning: Play near the front or side of your team with cover between shooting opportunities. Stay close enough to land repeated shots, but avoid being the first exposed target for the whole enemy team. Plan where Flame Dash can take you if the exchange becomes dangerous.
fight: Afterburn needs repeated hits to ignite an enemy. Look for a target distracted by your teammate or unable to immediately hide; isolated single bullets may not create the burn you need. Use Napalm within its useful range to help maintain a favourable exchange.

Once the enemy is burning, keep useful pressure without following them through several opponents. For Concussive Combustion, approach with timing and allied support so enemies cannot simply focus you before the explosion. Your ordinary gunfire and burns still matter when the ultimate is unavailable.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and find a covered angle for several hits that trigger Afterburn. Keep Flame Dash available if the enemy commits onto you.
Mid game
Clear useful waves and camps, then join fights where you can maintain contact. Avoid spending your approach to chase into an unsupported position.
Late game
Approach with allies and time Concussive Combustion for the fight. Continue useful burns and gunfire without outrunning your team’s ability to help.
infernus.threat: Use Flame Dash to leave when needed rather than saving it only for chasing. Head towards cover and teammates; do not keep running after an elevated target you cannot maintain contact with.
strengths: Damage continues after a successful ignition.
Useful wave and camp damage helps maintain income.
A supported commitment can keep enemies under repeated damage.
weaknesses: Interrupted contact
Enemies hiding quickly can prevent useful burn buildup.
Vertical separation
Elevated escapes can break a ground-based chase.
Unsafe durability assumptions
Burst or reduced healing can defeat an overcommitted approach.
matchups: Maintained beam pressure makes a sustained shooting exchange harder to keep favourable.
Use cover to break the exchange and keep Flame Dash available instead of trading openly until he controls the pace.
A close health reversal can punish chasing a wounded-looking target.
Maintain useful shooting distance and check her reversal threat before dashing directly onto her to finish.
A prepared position can force predictable movement around walls and entrances.
Apply burns from cover while your team contests; avoid dashing past the wall into an unsupported enclosed fight.
infernus.struggling: Collect safe waves and join after a teammate starts the fight; avoid leading a dive you cannot sustain.
infernus.tip: One occasional bullet is not the same as igniting an enemy. Seek a safe sustained shooting window.
mistakes: Leaving cover without enough time to ignite an enemy.
Chasing through several enemies after spending Flame Dash.
proTips: Concussive Combustion can't be interrupted, so cast it before diving in — it detonates after the delay regardless.
Gun hits refresh and extend Afterburn, so keep spraying to keep the burn stacking instead of bursting and stopping.
Napalm's debuff makes the target take more damage from your whole team, not just you — mark the focus target.

ivy.name: Ivy
ivy.title: How to Play Ivy in Deadlock | DIB
ivy.meta: Learn how to play Ivy in Deadlock: playing alongside an ally and supporting coordinated fights. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
ivy.ogTitle: Ivy Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
ivy.goal: Help a useful teammate keep fighting while contributing your own damage. Your exact balance of shooting, spell damage and protection depends on your build, but you should remain an active participant.
ivy.positioning: Play beside or just behind the ally you are helping, close enough for Kudzu Connection and with a clear line between you. Use cover and movement to change angles. Avoid standing so far behind that your gun and area pressure never affect the fight.
fight: Place Entangling Thorns where enemies must approach, retreat or stand to fight your teammate. Shoot a reachable target while your partner attacks. Keep Stone Form for a meaningful enemy commitment rather than using it for a little extra damage before an attacker rushes you.

Kudzu Connection helps a coordinated exchange; do not drift out of useful range while expecting it to keep working. Air Drop can start a fight or move an ally, but agree on the destination and timing first. Transporting someone away from a useful attack can hurt your team.
phases: Early game
Collect souls beside your partner and use Thorns for useful pressure. Preserve Stone Form for a serious enemy commitment rather than minor extra damage.
Mid game
Keep collecting income for your build while supporting a useful ally. Coordinate Air Drop before trying to move someone into or away from a fight.
Late game
Add your build’s damage and protect nearby allies. Choose transport and control that improve the current fight instead of moving teammates unexpectedly.
ivy.threat: Use Stone Form and movement to survive the dangerous moment, then return towards allied help. If your build is damage-focused, keep collecting income instead of assuming a support label means you should stop farming.
strengths: Gun, spell and utility builds support different team needs.
Connection helps a coordinated allied exchange.
Stone Form can deny a dangerous close commitment.
weaknesses: Team separation
Partners moving apart can reduce shared benefits.
Spent defence
A rush is harder to answer after Stone Form.
Transport mistakes
Moving an ally at the wrong time can harm their attack.
matchups: A close wall catch can force you to spend defence before a second threat arrives.
Preserve Stone Form for the dangerous commitment and fight beside your partner with an exit from his wall angle.
Her focused damage can become dangerous when your teammate is left alone.
Stay close enough to protect the targeted ally and add disruption rather than leaving to chase a different enemy.
Long sightlines punish stepping away from cover to maintain a partner exchange.
Choose cover your partner can also use and change the shared angle instead of both standing in her open firing line.
ivy.struggling: Clear safe waves and contribute protection; keep collecting souls if your chosen build needs gun damage.
ivy.tip: Do not pick up a teammate for Air Drop without agreeing on the destination and timing.
mistakes: Using Stone Form for minor damage before a dangerous attack.
Transporting an ally without agreeing where they should go.
proTips: Stone Form can be cast while you're busy with other actions — fire it mid-fight without pausing.
Kudzu healing is shared both ways, so tether a tanky ally to keep yourself sustained.
Self-cast Air Drop turns you into the explosion — land directly on grouped enemies for maximum impact.

kelvin.name: Kelvin
kelvin.title: How to Play Kelvin in Deadlock | DIB
kelvin.meta: Learn how to play Kelvin in Deadlock: protecting allies and using movement to support fights and rotations. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
kelvin.ogTitle: Kelvin Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
kelvin.goal: Keep teammates healthy and make enemies struggle to approach or keep shooting. Use your mobility to arrive at useful fights, then control who gets to keep attacking inside them.
kelvin.positioning: Play close enough to help an ally with grenades and beam pressure, usually beside or behind the teammate taking first contact. Keep cover nearby against distant guns. Before using Frozen Shelter, check which allies and enemies will be inside and whose shots it will block.
fight: Aim Frost Grenade where it can help an ally while threatening an enemy. Arctic Beam becomes more disruptive when you can maintain contact, so choose a reachable threat rather than sweeping it randomly across distant targets. Use your gun when a safe shooting opportunity is available.

Ice Path helps your team reach an angle or leave a bad fight; do not travel so far ahead that nobody can benefit. Frozen Shelter can create recovery time or isolate a fight, but trapping a vulnerable teammate beside a stronger close fighter is a poor save.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and aim Frost Grenade to help your partner while threatening an enemy. Use cover when maintaining Arctic Beam would expose you.
Mid game
Help teammates reach the next contest with Ice Path. Keep collecting nearby income and avoid arriving so far ahead that you must fight alone.
Late game
Slow immediate threats and use shelter with a deliberate plan. Check who is inside and whether the dome blocks your damage dealers from helping.
kelvin.threat: Slow the pursuer and move back towards cover or allies. Use shelter with a plan for the fight inside it, rather than treating it as a button that automatically makes every dangerous situation safe.
strengths: Grenades can help allies while threatening nearby enemies.
Maintained beam contact reduces enemy movement and shooting.
Path and shelter change access to a fight.
weaknesses: Long-range pressure
Distant guns punish an exposed close-to-mid-range approach.
Dome mistakes
Shelter can trap allies or block their damage.
Reduced healing
Enemy healing reduction limits recovery-based protection.
matchups: Her gun damage needs a sustained shooting window.
Use beam disruption and protection on the immediate threat, but avoid a dome that blocks your own allies from helping.
Shelter can leave a vulnerable ally inside a close fight Abrams wants.
Check who is inside before casting; use distance and slows instead of automatically enclosing the whole attack.
Her distant firing angles can sit outside a useful beam exchange.
Collect souls from cover and use protected movement to change the angle rather than chasing straight through her shots.
kelvin.struggling: Protect allies with slows and shelter rather than assuming you can win every close fight.
kelvin.tip: Frozen Shelter can block your own team’s shots or trap an ally with a stronger close fighter. Check who is inside.
mistakes: Trapping an ally inside Frozen Shelter with a stronger enemy.
Blocking allied shooting or relying on healing against heavy healing reduction.
proTips: Frozen Shelter's dome is impenetrable — cast it between your team and theirs to divide the fight.
Dash or crouch on your own Ice Path to climb to vertical spots other heroes can't reach.
At max rank the dome purges debuffs from allies inside, so time it against enemy crowd control.

lady-geist.name: Lady Geist
lady-geist.title: How to Play Lady Geist in Deadlock | DIB
lady-geist.meta: Learn how to play Lady Geist in Deadlock: managing your health while applying pressure from useful positions. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
lady-geist.ogTitle: Lady Geist Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
lady-geist.goal: Wear enemies down with spells while managing the health those spells cost you. Threaten a close health reversal when appropriate, but do not make becoming dangerously low your normal plan.
lady-geist.positioning: Use corners and nearby cover at a useful spell distance. Stand where you can retreat after casting and where an approaching enemy must expose themselves. Avoid crossing open gunfire simply because you hope to reach someone for Soul Exchange.
fight: Use Malice to prepare a damage exchange, then look for an Essence Bomb that hits an enemy or useful shared space around the wave. Keep shooting when safe. Spend health on attacks likely to connect instead of repeatedly throwing spells at someone who can easily avoid them.

Recover between exchanges and use Life Drain when you can maintain its useful contact without being focused. Soul Exchange threatens an enemy who comes close while you are hurt, but it is not guaranteed protection against sudden damage, control or an enemy staying out of reach.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and use attacks likely to connect. Recover between exchanges instead of spending health on every available cast.
Mid game
Use covered spell pressure near useful lane or objective fights. Keep a close reversal as a threat without deliberately becoming dangerously low.
Late game
Pressure committed enemies and preserve a safe route. Use Soul Exchange only when a viable target is reachable, not as an excuse to cross enemy fire.
lady-geist.threat: Return around cover towards your team and preserve enough health to survive the next hit. Do not chase a healthy target through damage just to try to reverse health at the last moment.
strengths: Spell placement threatens enemies around useful shared space.
Malice supports a stronger following exchange.
A nearby target can enable a meaningful turnaround.
weaknesses: Health costs
Missed or careless casts still spend her resources.
Burst while low
Sudden damage can arrive before a reversal.
Distant enemies
Targets outside close reversal range deny that defensive threat.
matchups: His close commitment can bring a target into your health-reversal range.
Take covered spell exchanges and retain a reversal option; do not deliberately lose health or assume a swap beats every burst.
She can pressure your health while staying away from a close reversal.
Use cover and reliable spell placement; avoid spending more health on missed casts while crossing her firing line.
An unexpected focused-gun attack can finish you after health-costing spells.
Preserve a covered retreat and stay near allies instead of repeatedly casting low while her approach is unaccounted for.
lady-geist.struggling: Clear from cover and preserve health; avoid spending it on attacks unlikely to connect.
lady-geist.tip: A low health bar is not an invitation to rush through enemy damage hoping to land Soul Exchange.
mistakes: Spending health on attacks that miss.
Running through damage while low to force Soul Exchange.
proTips: Soul Exchange sets both of you to the lower health percentage — use it when you're nearly dead and the target is healthy.
Life Drain keeps tracking through walls once the tether connects, so break line of sight after attaching.
Malice shards amplify damage the target takes from your whole team, so mark the focus target first.

lash.name: Lash
lash.title: How to Play Lash in Deadlock | DIB
lash.meta: Learn how to play Lash in Deadlock: using height and choosing an initiation your team can follow. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
lash.ogTitle: Lash Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
lash.goal: Use height and movement to attack an enemy from an unexpected angle, then put them where your teammates can help finish the fight. A useful landing matters more than a spectacular approach.
lash.positioning: Look for nearby height beside the fight rather than far behind the enemy team. Keep your teammates’ positions in view and a route available after landing. You want enough height for a useful Ground Strike without spending so long setting up that the opportunity disappears.
fight: Use Grapple and available terrain to reach an angle, then Ground Strike onto a reachable target. Add Flog and gunfire while allies can help. Look for enemies already occupied, approaching through a predictable route, or caught by another teammate instead of diving at every moving target.

Death Slam can separate enemies from their support or bring them into allied damage. Choose the destination before starting and check that the enemy stays in a useful line of sight. After landing, reassess your health and exit rather than immediately committing deeper.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and use nearby height for reliable Ground Strike opportunities. Keep a route back after landing rather than spending every movement option.
Mid game
Clear a useful wave, then look for a timely side or elevated approach. Join fights your teammates can follow instead of searching endlessly for height.
Late game
Choose a Death Slam destination that gives allies a useful attack. Reassess after landing and turn back if your own damage dealer needs protection.
lash.threat: Move back towards cover and allied protection using whatever movement remains. If you missed the attack or an enemy stops your approach, leave rather than trying to improvise a solo brawl in the middle of everyone.
strengths: Movement creates unusual attack angles around a fight.
A useful throw can separate enemies from protection.
Flog helps recover after connecting useful damage.
weaknesses: Missed landing
A failed attack can leave him exposed beside enemies.
Control on entry
Interrupted movement can spoil the intended approach.
Poor destinations
A throw is wasted if allies cannot reach the target.
matchups: A ranged firing position may be reachable from an overlooked vertical angle.
Approach with allied help, check his trap route and choose a landing that does not leave you alone behind the team.
They can hold you after you land and prevent a clean exit.
Track their position before diving and preserve movement; attack elsewhere if they are waiting beside your intended target.
Landing among grouped allies can put you near a ready enemy control threat.
Avoid committing to a destination Dynamo is protecting while your teammates cannot immediately follow.
lash.struggling: Use disruption to help a teammate and take nearby souls rather than repeatedly forcing missed dives.
lash.tip: A lower, reliable approach can be better than taking so long to find height that the fight ends.
mistakes: Missing an attack and landing without a way out.
Moving enemies somewhere your teammates cannot reach.
proTips: Ground Strike damage scales with fall height — always dive from as high as possible.
Grapple resets your air jumps and dashes mid-flight, so chain them to stay airborne.
Death Slam throws enemies into each other, adding bonus collision damage on top of the slam.

mcginnis.name: McGinnis
mcginnis.title: How to Play McGinnis in Deadlock | DIB
mcginnis.meta: Learn how to play McGinnis in Deadlock: preparing fighting positions and turning pressure into objectives. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
mcginnis.ogTitle: McGinnis Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
mcginnis.goal: Use your gun, wall and prepared position to help your team hold ground or take an objective. Turrets add pressure, but they do not replace shooting, collecting souls or choosing a safe position.
mcginnis.positioning: Play behind your team’s close fighters with cover nearby and a retreat route. Set up around ground your team actually wants to use. Spread turrets enough that one area attack does not remove everything, and avoid placing them where enemies can destroy them for free.
fight: Keep your machine gun working on a useful target. Spectral Wall can separate one enemy from help, block an approach or protect your retreat; check that it does not block your own teammates from attacking. Medicinal Specter helps allies keep using the position you are defending.

Prepare before an objective fight instead of dropping everything while already surrounded. Use Heavy Barrage from a protected angle when enemies must cross or remain in its area, but keep your build in mind: a gun-focused plan should not wait passively for a turret or ultimate setup.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and keep shooting alongside a defensible setup. Use wall placement carefully so your partner can still attack or retreat.
Mid game
Move with useful lane pressure and prepare objective ground. Keep using your machine gun and heal instead of waiting passively behind turrets.
Late game
Help the team hold a firing position with walls, shooting and spread-out turrets. Retreat with allies if the prepared ground is no longer defensible.
mcginnis.threat: Use wall placement, cover and your teammates to create distance. Avoid trying to rebuild a whole setup while a close attacker is already on you; survival comes before defending a turret position alone.
strengths: Her gun contributes alongside setup and abilities.
Wall placement can isolate a reachable enemy.
Healing and turrets support holding useful ground.
weaknesses: Sudden rushes
Direct attackers can bypass an unfinished setup.
Immobile pressure
Committing to a firing position makes route planning important.
Setup loss
Grouped or exposed turrets are easier to clear.
matchups: A side attack can bypass the prepared front and threaten you directly.
Keep a defensive wall angle and spread the setup; watch the sides instead of focusing only on the turret firing line.
Long-range shooting can pressure an exposed setup without approaching it.
Use cover for yourself and useful turret placement; do not walk into open fire to defend every turret.
He must approach close to threaten your team.
Use wall placement to make that approach awkward and keep shooting with allies, without trapping your own teammate beside him.
mcginnis.struggling: Defend useful ground and clear safe waves; avoid setting up alone far past allied help.
mcginnis.tip: Do not stop collecting souls or shooting because you placed turrets. Gun and turret builds have different priorities.
mistakes: Setting up alone beyond your team’s help.
Blocking allies with a wall or letting enemies clear every turret together.
proTips: Pre-spin your minigun before rounding corners — it takes two seconds to reach full fire rate.
Spectral Wall's eruption can be triggered early by firing or recasting, so don't wait for the full duration.
Wall upgrades can deploy two extra Mini Turrets — fortify the position before the fight, not during.

mina.name: Mina
mina.title: How to Play Mina in Deadlock | DIB
mina.meta: Learn how to play Mina in Deadlock: harassing enemies and choosing when to pursue a weakened target. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
mina.ogTitle: Mina Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
mina.goal: Build repeated damage opportunities, then finish a wounded target without getting caught by the reply. Your mobility helps you survive, but your low health makes one careless exposed exchange costly.
mina.positioning: Play around covered side angles near your teammates rather than standing at the very front. Stay close enough to land useful attacks while preserving a route back. Before following a wounded enemy, check whether their teammates can turn and burst you.
fight: Use attacks to build Love Bites pressure, then look for Rake when a target is wounded enough for it to matter. Do not assume your gun alone is the whole plan. Take short opportunities while the enemy is distracted instead of remaining visible until they can unload everything.

Rake can restore health when it finishes a target, including troopers or camps, so use farming to recover between fights. Keep Sanguine Retreat for avoiding a dangerous response or changing position. Use your larger damage commitment when allies can occupy enemies rather than forcing it alone.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and use Rake to finish troopers when you need recovery. Take short covered attacks and preserve Sanguine Retreat for danger.
Mid game
Keep income moving while looking for repeated Love Bites opportunities. Avoid a long exposed fight against someone ready to burst you.
Late game
Attack from the side after enemies commit elsewhere. Help finish wounded targets without following them beyond your team’s ability to protect you.
mina.threat: Use your evasive movement towards cover and teammates before you are too low to survive. If the enemy can stop that movement, wait near allied protection instead of relying on it to rescue every risky attack.
strengths: Love Bites rewards finding safe attack opportunities.
Retreat tools help avoid a dangerous response.
Rake can restore health from finishing appropriate targets.
weaknesses: Low tolerance for burst
A brief exposed mistake can be costly.
Disabled escape
Control makes relying on movement much riskier.
Overlong exchanges
Staying visible gives enemies time to answer fully.
matchups: A connected ranged spell sequence can punish your low tolerance for burst.
Use cover and preserve Sanguine Retreat when his setup is ready; do not remain exposed to complete one more attack.
A close control commitment can deny the movement you were relying on.
Keep his approach in view and enter after he is occupied rather than following a wounded target directly beside him.
An isolated ranged target can be distracted aiming at your teammates.
Use a covered side angle and keep an exit; do not extend the chase through his trap or incoming protection.
mina.struggling: Recover through safe farming and short attacks instead of trying to survive a long exposed exchange.
mina.tip: Rake can help recover health by finishing troopers or camps; you do not need a hero kill to use its recovery.
mistakes: Taking one large burst while your escape is unavailable.
Staying exposed just to finish one more Love Bites sequence.
proTips: Love Bites has a separate proc cooldown per target, so rotate targets in teamfights to trigger more bites.
Every Love Bite on a hero permanently adds bats to your ultimate, so harass heroes all game to scale it.
Rake kills don't drop soul orbs from troopers — last-hit troopers with your gun, not the slash.

mirage.name: Mirage
mirage.title: How to Play Mirage in Deadlock | DIB
mirage.meta: Learn how to play Mirage in Deadlock: maintaining pressure and choosing when to respond across the map. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
mirage.ogTitle: Mirage Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
mirage.goal: Build damage through repeated shots while keeping the option to reinforce another useful fight. Your map presence is valuable when you arrive safely and change the numbers, not whenever someone starts fighting.
mirage.positioning: Use cover in a position where you can repeatedly shoot a reachable target. Stay near enough to teammates to avoid being isolated if you spend Dust Devil. Before Traveler, inspect the destination and the positions enemies could reach by the time you arrive.
fight: Djinn’s Mark rewards maintaining pressure on a target rather than occasional random shots. Fire Scarabs helps prepare an exchange, and Dust Devil can disrupt an enemy or defend your position. Do not spend every tool aggressively before you know where the next threat will come from.

Between fights, keep collecting waves and watch the map. Traveler can turn a small fight into a numbers advantage or help defend an objective, but joining a fight already lost may simply add another death. Arrive near allied protection rather than aiming for the centre of the enemy group.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and build marks through safe repeated shots. Preserve Dust Devil when the enemy can force a close exchange.
Mid game
Watch for a Traveler arrival that creates a useful numbers advantage. Collect your wave first when a distant fight is already lost.
Late game
Arrive near allied cover, then maintain damage on a reachable target. Avoid committing every defensive option just to join the centre of a fight.
mirage.threat: Use your defensive movement and nearby cover to return to allies. Do not assume you can start a long-distance departure safely while enemies are already able to keep attacking you.
strengths: Maintaining hits makes marks more meaningful.
Traveler can change the numbers in a distant fight.
Dust Devil helps a close exchange or retreat.
weaknesses: Unsafe arrivals
A poor destination can turn reinforcement into another death.
Broken contact
Frequent cover can limit repeated-shot opportunities.
Overused defence
Spending movement to attack leaves fewer responses to a rush.
matchups: Long open shooting exchanges also build her focused-target damage.
Use cover and your defensive option deliberately; do not assume maintaining marks means you must stand still and trade everything.
Arriving near a ready close hold can turn Traveler into an unsafe commitment.
Inspect the arrival point and choose allied cover instead of teleporting into the centre of their protection.
A teammate pressured by her setup may benefit from a selective reinforcement.
Arrive only where you and the ally can fight together safely; avoid teleporting beyond a wall into an isolated position.
mirage.struggling: Use safe farm and selective reinforcements rather than teleporting into every losing fight.
mirage.tip: A global response is optional: staying to collect a wave can be better than joining a lost fight.
mistakes: Arriving at an unsafe Traveler destination.
Taking sudden damage before your repeated shots can matter.
proTips: Each Djinn's Mark doubles the total damage — four marks hit far harder than the sum of two.
Dust Devil makes you invincible during the cast, so use it to dodge incoming ultimates.
Any damage interrupts Traveler's channel, so cast it from fog of war or behind cover.

mo-krill.name: Mo & Krill
mo-krill.title: How to Play Mo & Krill in Deadlock | DIB
mo-krill.meta: Learn how to play Mo & Krill in Deadlock: catching priority targets where your teammates can follow up. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
mo-krill.ogTitle: Mo & Krill Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
mo-krill.goal: Reach a dangerous enemy and stop them while your teammates attack. You can also protect your own damage dealer by disabling whoever is chasing them instead of always diving the enemy’s strongest shooter.
mo-krill.positioning: Approach near the front or from a covered side, keeping a damage-dealing teammate close enough to use your catch. Avoid chasing across a long open sightline alone. A target beside your team is often more useful than an important enemy far beyond everyone’s reach.
fight: Burrow helps you reach a close opening. Use Scorn during the exchange to support your recovery, and Sand Blast to disrupt a gun threat when its shooting matters. Keep watching the rest of the enemy team instead of looking only at the person directly ahead.

Use Combo on someone your allies can immediately damage, particularly a dangerous enemy who has committed into reach. The control is valuable even if you do not get the final hit. If teammates retreat or cannot follow, avoid committing just because the target is technically in range.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and use useful close exchanges to recover. Avoid crossing long open gunfire without a realistic route onto the enemy.
Mid game
Travel with a damage-dealing ally and approach through cover. A nearby catch that allies can finish is worth more than chasing a distant target.
Late game
Stop a dangerous enemy with Combo where teammates can attack, or disable the diver chasing your own damage dealer. Keep your team’s position in view.
mo-krill.threat: Use disruption and your approach tools to return towards allies. If the enemy keeps distance or can interrupt your commitment, change the angle or protect a teammate rather than repeatedly forcing the same chase.
strengths: Combo can stop a dangerous enemy for allied damage.
Sand Blast limits an immediate shooting threat.
Scorn and durable approaches support useful close exchanges.
weaknesses: Distant targets
Long open approaches allow enemies to keep shooting.
Interrupted commitment
Control can prevent a catch from becoming useful damage.
Missing allied reach
A distant held target may receive no follow-up.
matchups: A committed gunner benefits from being left free to shoot.
Use Sand Blast or a supported Combo on the immediate threat rather than chasing someone less dangerous across the fight.
Distant or airborne shooting can deny your close-range tools.
Approach through cover with help and wait for a reachable position instead of repeatedly burrowing across open fire alone.
A protected priority target may have nearby group control ready to stop your commitment.
Track Dynamo before taking a hold and choose an angle where your team can immediately pressure his response.
mo-krill.struggling: Stop threats near your team; avoid chasing a distant enemy you cannot reach safely.
mo-krill.tip: You can use Combo defensively on an enemy chasing your damage dealer instead of always diving theirs.
mistakes: Catching a distant target without allied damage nearby.
Enemies keeping their distance or interrupting your commitment.
proTips: Scorn can be cast while busy — weave it in mid-Combo, mid-melee, even on the zipline.
Slowing Hex cannot disable Burrow, so walk straight through it.
Combo's permanent HP procs if the target dies during the channel or within 3s after — your team can secure it for you.

paige.name: Paige
paige.title: How to Play Paige in Deadlock | DIB
paige.meta: Learn how to play Paige in Deadlock: protecting allies and staying close enough to support their fights. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
paige.ogTitle: Paige Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
paige.goal: Protect the teammate taking an important exchange and help them keep dealing damage. Your shields and control should enable a useful action, not simply go on whoever happens to be closest.
paige.positioning: Play behind or beside the ally you are supporting, with cover and another teammate within reach. Avoid standing alone at the front: you have limited ways to escape a direct rush. Keep a view of both your damage dealer and the enemies approaching them.
fight: Use Plot Armor as an ally begins shooting or is about to take meaningful damage. While its barrier remains, it also strengthens their gunfire, so timing and recipient matter. Captivating Read helps restrict an enemy’s movement so your team can land shots and spells.

Use Bookwyrm to pressure an enemy route or clear a useful wave rather than walking dangerously close to add damage. Watch the wider fight for Rallying Charge opportunities, aiming where your teammates can benefit and enemies are likely to remain, rather than treating it as an automatic distant save.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and time Plot Armor for your partner’s meaningful exchanges. Stay near cover because you have limited ways to escape a direct rush.
Mid game
Support a productive teammate while using safe wave clear to maintain income. Watch other fights for opportunities your longer-distance help can reach.
Late game
Protect the ally taking the important attack and use control for allied damage. Aim Rallying Charge where teammates and enemies are actually moving.
paige.threat: Move towards allies and use control to make the approach harder. Spend protection on the immediate danger, but avoid leaving yourself isolated while trying to reach a teammate who is already far beyond help.
strengths: Protection helps an ally take a meaningful exchange.
An intact Plot Armor strengthens the recipient’s gunfire.
Control and longer-distance help support coordinated fights.
weaknesses: Direct rushes
Limited escape makes isolated positioning dangerous.
Poor recipient choice
Protection is wasted on an uninvolved ally.
Unavailable tools
Several threats can arrive after her important spells are spent.
matchups: A focused gun attack can quickly overwhelm an unprotected teammate.
Time Plot Armor for the ally actually taking the exchange and use control to help them attack or leave.
An approach from above can reach you despite a protected front.
Stay close to allied help, watch height and preserve control for the landing rather than standing alone far behind everyone.
A clear hook can pull you out of the position supporting your partner.
Use troopers and cover to deny the path, and avoid lining up in the same predictable exposed gap.
paige.struggling: Support your strongest available teammate and use long-range wave clear without walking into danger.
paige.tip: Shielding an ally who is already shooting can turn protection into damage; choose the recipient deliberately.
mistakes: Being rushed while alone with no movement escape.
Using protection on an ally who is not taking a useful exchange.
proTips: Her shots can't crit on headshots but still trigger headshot items like Headshot Booster — build those, not crit.
A Rallying Charge that hits nothing refunds half its cooldown, so throw speculative charges freely.
Captivating Read's T3 strips 18% spirit resist for 6s, amplifying your whole team's spirit damage.

paradox.name: Paradox
paradox.title: How to Play Paradox in Deadlock | DIB
paradox.meta: Learn how to play Paradox in Deadlock: finding a pick and choosing swaps your team can follow. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
paradox.ogTitle: Paradox Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
paradox.goal: Catch an exposed enemy and swap them into a position your team can attack. Before making the play, account for where you will land as carefully as where the enemy will arrive.
paradox.positioning: Play near allies with a useful view of the target. Your current position becomes the enemy’s destination during a swap, so do not begin from somewhere your team cannot reach. Keep cover or allied protection available at the far end whenever possible.
fight: Use Pulse Grenade to pressure a route or an enemy occupied by your teammate. Charge Kinetic Carbine for a controlled shot rather than firing it without a clear target. Landing that setup makes a following Paradoxical Swap easier than trying to hit an enemy freely dodging.

Time Wall can interrupt a useful enemy firing line or help control a route. Once a target is caught, help teammates damage them instead of looking immediately for a second elaborate play. Do not swap a durable enemy into vulnerable allies while placing yourself somewhere you cannot survive.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise controlled Carbine shots from cover. Use grenade pressure without stepping into unnecessary danger to force a swap.
Mid game
Move near allies who can attack a catch. Check where you will land and where the enemy will arrive before committing.
Late game
Catch a valuable exposed target only when the exchange helps your team. Keep using safer damage and disruption if the swap destination is defended.
paradox.threat: Use cover and your remaining disruption to get back towards allies. If enemies are waiting at your swap destination, keep using safer damage and setup until the position changes instead of forcing the exchange.
strengths: Carbine helps prepare a more reliable catch.
An exposed enemy can be delivered into allied damage.
Wall placement can interfere with a useful firing line.
weaknesses: Unsafe exchange
A swap can leave her in the enemy’s protection.
Missed setup
Freely moving targets are harder to catch reliably.
Team dependence
A good catch still needs allies ready to attack.
matchups: An exposed firing position can become a useful swap target.
Set up Carbine from allied cover and check your destination; a caught sniper is not worth landing alone inside his team.
Swapping a close fighter towards vulnerable allies may improve his access.
Choose a different target unless allies can control and damage him immediately, and check the position you will inherit.
Evasive tools can spoil a committed catch and leave you overextended.
Watch which defensive option is used before forcing the swap; keep using covered damage when no reliable catch exists.
paradox.struggling: Use controlled catches from allied protection instead of swapping into the middle of the enemy team.
paradox.tip: Your starting position matters as much as your aim: it becomes the enemy’s destination.
mistakes: Swapping yourself into a position you cannot survive.
Catching a target when teammates cannot attack it.
proTips: Kinetic Carbine scales only off weapon damage — spirit power does nothing for it. But spirit resist shred still boosts its damage, while bullet resist shred does not.
Time Wall stops ability and item projectiles too, and ally weapon-damage abilities gain the +30% bonus.
Swap triggers Indomitable and Cloak of Opportunity, cleansing it so nobody moves — check enemy items before committing.

pocket.name: Pocket
pocket.title: How to Play Pocket in Deadlock | DIB
pocket.meta: Learn how to play Pocket in Deadlock: finding a burst opportunity and planning an escape before committing. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
pocket.ogTitle: Pocket Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
pocket.goal: Enter from a side, apply close damage, and escape before enemies can focus you together. You want repeated useful attacks, not one burst that spends every defensive tool and ends in a death.
pocket.positioning: Use cover around the edge of a fight with a route back towards allies. Your shotgun wants closer range, but you should not walk through the whole enemy team to use it. Check both your current position and the destination of Flying Cloak before choosing to teleport.
fight: Use Barrage to prepare damage while an enemy is occupied or moving predictably, then add shotgun shots when safe. Avoid remaining an easy stationary target during the cast. Keep Cloak or Enchanter’s Satchel available for the response instead of treating both as extra entry damage.

Affliction can weaken several nearby enemies when you get a useful opening. Its damage does not finish enemies by itself, so your team still needs a final hit from another source. After applying pressure, leave or change position before everyone turns their attacks onto you.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise Barrage from a safe moving angle. Keep a defensive option for the enemy reply instead of using everything for damage.
Mid game
Clear a useful wave, then approach nearby fights from the side. Check your Cloak destination and preserve a way out after entry.
Late game
Apply useful damage to committed enemies, then leave before being focused. Affliction weakens targets but needs another damage source to finish them.
pocket.threat: Use your defensive option to avoid the dangerous moment and return towards safety. If silence or movement restriction could stop your escape, wait near allies and choose a later opening rather than diving into the threat.
strengths: Tools help reach a useful shotgun exchange.
Cloak and Satchel can avoid dangerous replies.
Affliction applies pressure across nearby committed enemies.
weaknesses: Spent escape
Using every tool to enter makes the reply dangerous.
Silence and restriction
Disabled tools undermine the planned exit.
Non-lethal pressure
Affliction alone does not supply the final hit.
matchups: His delayed catch punishes committing close after spending your escape options.
Keep Cloak or Satchel available and leave before the catch forces you into his preferred extended fight.
A prepared silence threatens a spell-based entry and exit.
Watch her brew and stay near allied help; avoid using every movement option to enter while she is waiting close.
A distracted ranged shooter can expose a side opening.
Approach through cover, check traps and preserve a defensive option instead of spending both Cloak and Satchel just to reach him.
pocket.struggling: Clear safe waves and join distracted enemies from a side; avoid using every escape to reach someone.
pocket.tip: Affliction weakens enemies but cannot finish them by itself. You or your teammates must supply the final damage.
mistakes: Spending both Cloak and Satchel just to enter.
Being silenced or expecting Affliction to deal the finishing hit.
proTips: Enchanter's Satchel disarms you but instantly finishes your reload — Satchel mid-reload, then re-engage with a full clip.
Barrage's damage amp applies to Pocket herself, boosting all your damage — even against targets you never hit with Barrage.
Affliction is non-lethal and procs no items — use it to set up kills, never to finish them.

rat-king.name: Rat King
rat-king.title: How to Play Rat King in Deadlock | DIB
rat-king.meta: Learn how to play Rat King in Deadlock: creating space and staying close enough to enable your teammates. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
rat-king.ogTitle: Rat King Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
rat-king.goal: Help your team move into a close fight together, then keep pressure on enemies your allies can reach. Your barrier and banner support a coordinated advance rather than a long solo chase.
rat-king.positioning: Play near the front with teammates close behind or beside you. Use corners and covered routes to approach gun range instead of crossing long open sightlines. Before a committed advance, check that allies are ready to move rather than still collecting a distant wave.
fight: Use Rat Swarm on a reachable target, then follow with gunfire while its effect helps your damage. Scrap Grenade can pressure grouped enemies or a route they need to cross. Keep Royal Pestments available for a meaningful exchange instead of wasting protection before you are threatened.

Rule, Ratannia! is most useful when nearby allies can move and fight with you. Use it to help the team reach an objective fight or maintain pressure, then put the disruptive part where enemies are committed. Reassess if they scatter instead of following each one separately.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and take close exchanges with protection ready. Use Swarm into shooting instead of crossing open gunfire to force a chase.
Mid game
Move with allies towards the next useful contest. Check that teammates are ready before beginning a committed advance.
Late game
Use your banner and disruption to help the group move and fight together. Avoid separating from them to chase a distant or elevated enemy.
rat-king.threat: Move back with your team and preserve useful protection. Avoid chasing a flying or distant target away from allied damage; the enemy may be trying to separate you from the group your tools help.
strengths: Swarm improves a useful shooting exchange.
Barrier helps take a meaningful close commitment.
Banner rewards teammates moving and fighting together.
weaknesses: Team spread
Distant allies cannot exploit a group-focused advance.
Ranged separation
Distant or elevated enemies can deny close contact.
Open exposure
Being durable does not make crossing several guns free.
matchups: Unsupported time in her firing line lets focused gun damage build.
Advance with protection and teammates ready rather than walking alone through sustained fire to chase her.
Elevated ranged pressure can deny your close gun and group-advance plan.
Use covered approaches and pressure a reachable fight instead of chasing her alone beneath an exposed flight angle.
A grounded close fight can let nearby allies use your group advance.
Move together and keep Swarm pressure on a reachable target, while avoiding easy wall pins and predictable punches.
rat-king.struggling: Help a coordinated team push and protect nearby allies instead of chasing a distant gunner alone.
rat-king.tip: Your banner helps a group advance; using it far from teammates wastes much of its purpose.
mistakes: Advancing while teammates are too far away.
Chasing elevated or distant enemies across open gunfire.
proTips: Enemies shake rats off with any ground or air dash — reapply Swarm after they dash, not before.
Your grenade homes toward enemies within 50.8m, and one pellet of your gun is always perfectly accurate — trust the throw.
You double-jump higher than other heroes and can use tunnel vents — take vertical angles nobody expects.

rem.name: Rem
rem.title: How to Play Rem in Deadlock | DIB
rem.meta: Learn how to play Rem in Deadlock: supporting a partner and disrupting enemies during team fights. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
rem.ogTitle: Rem Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
rem.goal: Keep a useful teammate active while disrupting enemies who try to reach them. Use your helpers between fights so contributing is more than staying attached to one ally for the entire match.
rem.positioning: Stay close to an ally who can protect you, usually behind or beside the first person taking contact. Keep a view of approaching enemies so you can respond before they are already on top of you. Avoid travelling alone into routes the enemy team controls.
fight: Pillow Toss can push back a dangerous approach and create space for an ally to keep shooting or leave. Use Tag Along when a teammate needs recovery, and consider moving support to another ally when the situation changes rather than following the same person regardless of the fight.

Send Lil Helpers to collect safe boxes between fights while staying near your team. For Naptime, tell teammates before the sleep opening so they can prepare their damage. Do not assume its control will remain undisturbed while everyone attacks independently; coordinated timing gets more value from the opportunity.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and support your lane partner. Use Pillow Toss to stop a serious approach rather than exposing yourself for small damage.
Mid game
Send helpers on safe tasks while travelling near allies. Use Tag Along to help recovery, changing support as the team’s needs change.
Late game
Coordinate Naptime before the damage begins, and protect a useful teammate. Avoid remaining passive on one ally while the important fight moves elsewhere.
rem.threat: Move towards an ally and use knockback to make pursuit harder. If you cannot safely reach your intended partner, stay near another teammate rather than crossing exposed ground to attach to one particular player.
strengths: Tag Along helps keep a useful ally active.
Pillow Toss creates distance from an approaching enemy.
Helpers contribute while Rem stays near allied protection.
weaknesses: Isolation
Being caught away from allies undermines his escape plan.
Missed protection
A wasted defensive toss leaves a larger opening.
Uncoordinated sleep
Independent damage can spoil the intended follow-up timing.
matchups: A close wall catch can separate you from protective teammates.
Stay near an ally and keep Pillow Toss for a serious approach instead of spending it on minor damage.
Her catch can move the ally you rely on into an unsafe position.
Track the approach and stay near additional allied help; do not assume one partner remains a safe place throughout the fight.
A teammate under focused shooting needs timely recovery and space.
Help the attacked ally and use knockback when useful, rather than remaining with an uninvolved partner far from the threat.
rem.struggling: Keep a useful ally active and use helpers safely; avoid wandering alone for extra damage.
rem.tip: Coordinate Naptime with your team’s attack rather than assuming sleeping enemies will stay asleep under damage.
mistakes: Being caught away from an ally who can protect you.
Preparing sleep without coordinating the team’s damage.
proTips: While napping, your self-casts target your ally instead — items and abilities redirect to them.
Helpers assigned to Sinner's Sacrifice always secure the full jackpot as if you'd heavy-meleed it, unless a player interrupts them.
Naptime's cooldown is halved if the channel gets interrupted — don't be afraid to throw it.

seven.name: Seven
seven.title: How to Play Seven in Deadlock | DIB
seven.meta: Learn how to play Seven in Deadlock: collecting income and choosing positions for sustained area pressure. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
seven.ogTitle: Seven Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
seven.goal: Turn efficient soul collection into sustained damage around important fights. Your job is to make enemy approaches dangerous and help your team keep attacking, rather than waiting only for a large ultimate.
seven.positioning: Play behind or beside your team’s close fighters with a clear route to cover. Choose a view of the paths enemies need to cross for an objective. Avoid standing alone at the front or taking a distant camp when your team is already preparing a nearby fight.
fight: Send Lightning Ball through a useful wave or enemy approach, ideally creating pressure on both. Static Charge is delayed, so give yourself and teammates time to prepare damage where the target will be when it lands. Keep shooting and use Power Surge when it supports the exchange.

Storm Cloud is useful when enemies are committed to an area or held by teammates, not simply whenever several appear on screen. They can leave your sightline or interrupt you, so choose a protected position and an opening that makes escaping your damage inconvenient.
phases: Early game
Clear troopers efficiently with useful Ball placement and secure souls. Prepare damage for Static Charge rather than only casting it and waiting.
Mid game
Collect waves and nearby safe camps, then arrive for important fights. Do not spend the whole stage farming while teammates repeatedly contest objectives.
Late game
Control enemy approaches with ordinary damage and spells. Use Storm Cloud from protection when the fight makes leaving your sightline difficult.
seven.threat: Move back behind cover and use your control to discourage pursuit. If a close attacker reaches you, seek help instead of beginning a long exposed ultimate and hoping it wins before they finish you.
strengths: Area tools help collect waves and nearby camps.
Static Charge gives allies time to prepare damage.
Repeated damage makes objective approaches costly.
weaknesses: Direct rushes
An attacker reaching him threatens his firing position.
Long-attack exposure
A channel invites interrupts or concentrated fire.
Avoided sightlines
Enemies can leave an ultimate’s useful damage area.
matchups: His close approach must cross space you can pressure.
Use Ball and delayed stun where he needs to move, then retreat before he reaches a useful wall angle.
An aerial approach can reach your channel position from outside the front line.
Watch above and preserve cover; do not begin Storm Cloud while his landing can reach you freely.
Ranged pressure can punish you without remaining in your preferred area.
Use structures to limit his sightline and choose objective ground instead of channeling in an open street duel.
seven.struggling: Clear safe waves and help with stuns; do not force a long ultimate while exposed.
seven.tip: Enemies can leave Storm Cloud’s sightline. Use it where an objective or allied control makes staying costly.
mistakes: Standing exposed during a long ultimate.
Collecting camps so long that you miss your team’s important fight.
proTips: Lightning Ball's slow is reapplied every 0.1s tick, which effectively ignores debuff resist — don't rely on cleanse to walk through it.
Storm Cloud was nerfed to 71.25 DPS — it's zone control first, damage second; the targeted lightning strike is the real burst.
Power Surge's shock bounces to 4 nearby enemies, and its T3 shreds 15% spirit resist for 10s for your whole team.

shiv.name: Shiv
shiv.title: How to Play Shiv in Deadlock | DIB
shiv.meta: Learn how to play Shiv in Deadlock: building momentum and choosing when to commit to a weakened enemy. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
shiv.ogTitle: Shiv Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
shiv.goal: Build pressure before a close fight, then help finish wounded enemies. Your damage management gives you opportunities to keep fighting, but it does not remove the need to watch health and incoming threats.
shiv.positioning: Play around the front edge or side of your team where you can reach a target without being surrounded. Use cover while building pressure. Keep a route back to allied help instead of dashing so far ahead that a finishing opportunity becomes a solo fight.
fight: Use Serrated Knives to build pressure, then look for a close Slice and Dice exchange while your resources are favourable. Mix shotgun damage with your abilities. An enemy already fighting your teammate is a better commitment than someone waiting with every defensive tool ready.

Bloodletting delays some damage, so account for what is still waiting to arrive instead of reading only your visible health. Killing Blow can finish a sufficiently wounded enemy, but do not chase the next target automatically if allies are falling back or your resources are exhausted.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and build pressure with controlled knife attacks. Watch delayed damage rather than treating every apparently favourable health bar as safe.
Mid game
Approach with your fighting resources ready and allies in reach. Choose a target you can maintain contact with without becoming surrounded.
Late game
Look for a safe Killing Blow finish after allies and your pressure weaken someone. Reassess health and backup before following another target.
shiv.threat: Break off towards cover and teammates before the delayed damage becomes fatal. When behind, keep knife pressure and help finish an already weakened target instead of trying to prove you can survive a full-health duel.
strengths: Knives help prepare a stronger close exchange.
Deferred damage creates choices about when to continue or leave.
Killing Blow punishes sufficiently wounded targets.
weaknesses: Hidden danger
Deferred damage can make visible health misleading.
Distant fights
Enemies keeping space can deny a useful close commitment.
Unsafe pursuit
Following every finish can separate him from help.
matchups: Chasing her low health into close range can enable a reversal.
Keep pressure from a useful angle and account for Soul Exchange before spending your approach on a finish.
Distance and elevation can deny your close damage sequence.
Collect souls from cover and wait for a reachable fight instead of chasing through repeated ranged shots.
A committed firing position can create a predictable close target.
Approach with allies through a safe route; do not dash past her wall into an isolated fight among the setup.
shiv.struggling: Maintain knife pressure and finish weakened targets near teammates instead of initiating a full-health duel.
shiv.tip: Your health bar does not tell the whole story when damage is still waiting to arrive.
mistakes: Ignoring damage still waiting to arrive through Bloodletting.
Chasing a finishing opportunity beyond your team’s help.
proTips: Headshots build rage 1.65x faster than bodyshots — aim high while farming rage.
Bloodletting is affected by healing modifiers, so enemy anti-heal guts it — and Pocket's Affliction at 1 HP can kill you straight through it.
Executing with Killing Blow fully refills your rage meter and lets you recast for 16s — chain executes to win fights.

silver.name: Silver
silver.title: How to Play Silver in Deadlock | DIB
silver.meta: Learn how to play Silver in Deadlock: preparing close-range fights and making your transformation count. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
silver.ogTitle: Silver Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
silver.goal: Use human-form gun damage to prepare a useful close-range fight, then make your transformation window count. You want enemies you can keep attacking, rather than spending the entire window travelling after them.
silver.positioning: Start near cover beside your team, close enough for your gun burst without standing inside every enemy attack. Watch your bloodlust while approaching. Before the form changes, choose a target and route where you can stay in contact and still return towards allies.
fight: Entangling Bola can limit an enemy’s escape, while Boot Kick and Slam Fire create a close gun-damage opportunity. Aim carefully rather than spraying from too far away. Keep track of the upcoming transformation instead of treating your human and werewolf actions as unrelated plans.

In werewolf form, focus on a reachable enemy and use your close attacks while teammates occupy other threats. A target escaping vertically or along a distant route may waste your window. Do not assume a full bloodlust bar can be held indefinitely while you wait for the perfect moment.
phases: Early game
Collect souls through controlled human-form exchanges. Watch bloodlust while choosing a position instead of being surprised by the coming transformation.
Mid game
Plan a covered route onto a reachable enemy before the close-range window. Keep collecting income rather than chasing someone you cannot catch.
Late game
Fight with allies during your strong form and choose targets you can stay near. Leave if enemy control prevents useful contact.
silver.threat: Return towards allies and use your available form’s tools to survive. If enemies can stop your movement, avoid rushing into their whole team just because your transformation makes you feel temporarily stronger.
strengths: Prepared close shots create an early damage opportunity.
Transformation changes the available attack and recovery tools.
Bola helps keep a reachable target in contact.
weaknesses: Form timing
Transformation can occur before a useful approach is ready.
Lost contact
Chasing wastes the limited close-range opportunity.
Movement control
Being stopped makes maintaining close damage much harder.
matchups: A distant or airborne target can waste your werewolf fighting window.
Choose a grounded reachable enemy or wait for a better approach instead of transforming into a long exposed chase.
A close hold can spend your strongest window without letting you attack.
Track their commitment and fight near allies rather than leaping directly beside them while they wait to protect someone.
Restricting an isolated target’s escape can create a close gun opportunity.
Use Bola from a covered approach and keep allied reach in mind; do not assume the target’s teammates are absent.
silver.struggling: Use controlled human-form exchanges near allies instead of chasing through the whole transformation.
silver.tip: Transformation can happen as bloodlust fills; do not assume you can hold a full resource indefinitely.
mistakes: Losing your close-range window while travelling or chasing.
Being stopped by enemy control before you can keep attacking.
proTips: You can steer Boot Kick's throw direction with your aim after landing it — kick carries into walls or straight to your team.
Hero kills as a wolf refresh your abilities and extend the transformation — commit to the cleanup.
Slam Fire's +100% weapon damage vs NPCs also buffs your melees — you clear neutral camps insanely fast.

sinclair.name: Sinclair
sinclair.title: How to Play Sinclair in Deadlock | DIB
sinclair.meta: Learn how to play Sinclair in Deadlock: finding ranged angles and adapting to the utility you copy. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
sinclair.ogTitle: Sinclair Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
sinclair.goal: Pressure enemies with controlled ranged attacks and use a copied ultimate that fits the fight. A reliable spell setup is more useful than a complicated imitation you cannot safely position for.
sinclair.positioning: Play behind or beside teammates with cover and a safe Spectral Assistant location. Keep track of where swapping with the Assistant will take you. Avoid placing it somewhere dangerous and then treating the swap as a guaranteed escape when enemies approach.
fight: Use Vexing Bolt’s redirection to threaten an exposed target rather than repeatedly firing straight at someone who can easily dodge. The Assistant adds another attack angle, so think about where both attacks can matter while keeping your own position protected.

Use Rabbit Hex when allies can take advantage of the control. For Audience Participation, choose an enemy ultimate you understand and can use from a realistic position. Consider the upcoming objective, who will protect you and what teammates can do during the copied effect.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise Bolt redirection with a safe Assistant position. Avoid treating a swap as safety if its destination is exposed.
Mid game
Choose copied tools you understand for the next objective fight. Keep pressure from a covered angle without abandoning your escape setup.
Late game
Use control and a useful copied ultimate while allies can benefit. Prefer reliable positioning over attempting an unfamiliar combination inside the enemy group.
sinclair.threat: Swap only if the Assistant’s position is safer than your current one, then return towards cover or allies. If both positions are threatened, stop forcing damage and preserve distance while waiting for a better setup.
strengths: Bolt control creates less obvious ranged threats.
A prepared swap changes his attack or escape angle.
A familiar copied ultimate can fit the upcoming fight.
weaknesses: Position tracking
A threatened Assistant location can ruin an escape.
Execution demands
Missed redirection wastes the intended damage opening.
Unfamiliar tools
A copied ability fails without suitable positioning and timing.
matchups: A close fighter needs to cross space your ranged attacks can pressure.
Use Bolt from cover and keep a genuinely safe Assistant position; avoid standing beside an easy wall pin.
An unexpected close burst can punish attention spent aiming or choosing a copied tool.
Keep nearby allies and a protected swap destination, and watch the side route before committing a long setup.
His ultimate is a potential copied group-control tool, but requires the right position.

sinclair.struggling: Provide ranged damage and a simple useful copied tool rather than forcing an unfamiliar big play.
sinclair.tip: A copied ultimate is only useful if you know its range, timing and position requirements.

Copying a complex ability without knowing how to use it safely.

Slowing Hex blocks the assistant swap but not the summon — and the Vexing Bolt redirect doesn't break stealth.
