solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.title: How to Play Solomon in Deadlock | DIB
solomon.meta: Learn how to play Solomon in Deadlock: preparing zones and fighting where your pieces can influence enemies. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
solomon.ogTitle: Solomon Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
solomon.goal: Prepare dangerous ground around routes enemies need to use, then move your pieces as the fight changes. Your goal is to make enemies cross useful threatened areas, not simply place a board and wait.
solomon.positioning: Play behind or beside teammates near cover, overlooking a doorway, lane approach or objective route. Avoid moving so far forward that an attacker reaches you before your pieces matter. Keep protection available for yourself or an ally when enemies push past the prepared ground.
fight: Place Setup Bishop where its threatened diagonals affect a real approach, then move it through a target or onto their likely next route. Use ordinary shots when useful, but do not chase a gun duel far beyond the area your spells are controlling.

Rook Battery can help stop an approaching enemy or prepare allied damage. Kingside Knight can protect a teammate or help reposition. Use Develop Queen on a committed group or a route they must cross, then update the threat as enemies move instead of leaving every piece behind.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise threatening an actual approach with Bishop. Keep protection ready for someone rushing past your pieces.
Mid game
Set up the next contested route before enemies arrive. Move pieces when targets change direction instead of defending an old empty area.
Late game
Control routes around the objective with moving pieces and Queen placement. Keep yourself near cover and help an ally if enemies push through.
solomon.threat: Move towards cover and allies while using your available control or protection. If your setup is elsewhere, prioritise reaching safety rather than standing still trying to rebuild the whole board under direct attack.
strengths: Pieces make relevant enemy approaches dangerous.
Repositioning pieces follows a changing fight.
Defensive tools can help when enemies push through.
weaknesses: Setup time
A sudden rush can arrive before pieces matter.
Location dependence
An old board may no longer affect the fight.
Direct pressure
Close attackers punish exposed attention on remote pieces.
matchups: A fast close catch can reach you before the prepared ground matters.
Stay away from easy wall angles and preserve a defensive tool while moving Bishop onto the real approach.
A distant firing angle can avoid the ground your pieces threaten.
Use cover and protect the relevant objective route rather than walking into her shots to move the fight towards her.
An established objective position creates predictable contested routes.
Place pieces on the approaches your team is contesting and keep updating them instead of standing exposed in her firing line.
solomon.struggling: Prepare defensive routes near allies rather than chasing enemies outside your pieces.
solomon.tip: A threatening piece in an irrelevant location does not control the current fight. Update the board as enemies move.
mistakes: Being rushed before your pieces are ready.
Leaving pieces in places that no longer affect the fight.
proTips: Right-click moves pieces instead of zooming — your gun has no scope.
The bishop is invulnerable while moving, so reposition it through danger.
Rook Battery's re-activate splits the rooks perpendicular for crossfire angles.

venator.name: Venator
venator.title: How to Play Venator in Deadlock | DIB
venator.meta: Learn how to play Venator in Deadlock: preparing traps and creating useful shooting opportunities. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
venator.ogTitle: Venator Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
venator.goal: Keep useful gunfire on enemies while traps and wall threats make approaching you risky. You want a protected firing position and a reachable target, not a solo close catch at any cost.
venator.positioning: Play beside or behind your team’s first contact with nearby cover. Trap a route enemies could use to reach you, and notice walls behind potential targets. Keep a second retreat route in mind because a visible trap can be destroyed, avoided or still arming.
fight: Use Hex-Lined Snap Trap to prepare a likely approach, then shoot enemies your team is already pressuring. Gutshot can punish someone close to a wall or create space when they reach you. Choose its direction deliberately instead of pushing a target out of allied damage.

Consecrating Grenade adds useful pressure against healing and can threaten a route around cover. Use Ira Domini when an enemy is caught, retreating predictably or already occupied, rather than expecting its slower attack to solve an exposed duel by itself.
phases: Early game
Collect souls from cover while preparing a trap on an approach. Watch nearby walls for a useful Gutshot rather than forcing a close duel.
Mid game
Keep collecting income and prepare routes before an objective fight. Replace lost protection when enemies destroy or bypass your traps.
Late game
Maintain useful gunfire from a protected position. Use catches and Ira Domini when enemies are held, retreating predictably or occupied by allies.
venator.threat: Use your close disruption and covered route to move back towards allies. Do not remain standing on a trap expecting it to protect you from every direction while several enemies attack.
strengths: Traps help manage approaches to a firing position.
Gutshot threatens enemies beside nearby terrain.
Grenade damage helps challenge recovery-based exchanges.
weaknesses: Lost protection
Traps can be destroyed, avoided or not yet armed.
Direct rushes
Several close threats can overwhelm one firing position.
Poor wall angles
Open-ground displacement may not hold a target usefully.
matchups: A direct close approach can cross a prepared trap and a useful wall angle.
Keep cover, trap the route and preserve Gutshot for the commitment instead of spending it on minor damage.
A vertical approach may bypass the ground route your trap protects.
Watch height and keep allied help nearby; one trapped doorway does not protect every angle.
His close recovery-based fight gives your grenade a useful target.
Apply grenade pressure during the supported exchange and maintain a safe firing angle rather than chasing inside his aura alone.
venator.struggling: Clear safe waves and protect a firing position rather than forcing an unsupported close catch.
venator.tip: A trap needs to arm and can be destroyed; it is not permission to ignore the route behind you.
mistakes: Assuming traps cannot be destroyed or bypassed.
Taking a close fight without a useful wall or retreat route.
proTips: Enemies must shoot traps to disarm them — hide traps behind corners and edges.
Gutshot's wall stun blesses your next heavy melee at higher tiers.
The final Ira Domini stake is the blessed one — save it for the lowest target.

victor.name: Victor
victor.title: How to Play Victor in Deadlock | DIB
victor.meta: Learn how to play Victor in Deadlock: taking sustained frontline fights while keeping allied support nearby. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
victor.ogTitle: Victor Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
victor.goal: Stay close to useful fights while managing the health you spend and recover. Draw enemy attention only when your team can benefit, rather than treating self-damage or a revival as permission to fight alone.
victor.positioning: Approach near the front with teammates close enough to attack alongside you. Use cover to avoid losing health before you can reach useful range. Think about the ground you would revive on: a second life is much less useful if enemies already control the whole area.
fight: Taking damage, including your own ability costs, charges Pain Battery. Use a charged attack on a reachable enemy rather than taking unnecessary shots just to fill it. Time Jumpstart around recovery you can actually use, and keep watching how much health the exchange costs.

Aura of Suffering rewards remaining close, but only while you can survive there. Keep attacking with your team and step back if they retreat. Shocking Reanimation can extend your contribution, but do not plan around the enemy politely leaving you alone afterwards.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and manage your recovery carefully. Avoid taking free damage simply to charge Pain Battery or forcing early fights you cannot sustain.
Mid game
Enter useful fights alongside teammates and keep a covered way back. Spend health only when the resulting pressure can actually help.
Late game
Stay near allies while applying close pressure, and retreat when they do. Think about the position you would revive into before accepting a death.
victor.threat: Return towards cover and allied help while managing recovery. If you cannot reach a target or healing is heavily reduced, avoid spending more health to continue a chase that the enemy controls.
strengths: Staying near a useful fight creates repeated threats.
Damage taken can prepare Pain Battery’s response.
His tools can extend a supported contribution.
weaknesses: Health spending
His own costs still make enemy damage dangerous.
Distant targets
Ranged enemies can damage him without entering his area.
Unsafe revival
Returning in enemy-controlled ground can lead to another death.
matchups: She can pressure you without entering the close area you threaten.
Collect souls from cover and keep health for a supported approach instead of paying it to cross her firing line.
Trap protection and healing pressure make a direct recovery-based rush harder.
Change the route with allies and account for grenade pressure before committing health to a long close fight.
A supported close exchange can keep an enemy within your pressure.
Use recovery deliberately while teammates attack, but avoid easy wall pins and do not assume a revival makes the duel safe.
victor.struggling: Collect safe income and contribute near allies; avoid spending health to force an early duel.
victor.tip: A revival is not an escape route. If the enemy controls the area, they can be waiting when you return.
mistakes: Spending health when you cannot recover safely.
Reviving in an area completely controlled by enemies.
proTips: T3 Jumpstart's debuff resistance also halves ultimate debuffs if active first.
While Shocking Reanimation is on cooldown you gain fire rate and spirit damage per bullet.
Reanimation purges your debuffs on trigger — dying cleansed is fine.

vindicta.name: Vindicta
vindicta.title: How to Play Vindicta in Deadlock | DIB
vindicta.meta: Learn how to play Vindicta in Deadlock: ranged positioning and finding safe opportunities to finish enemies. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
vindicta.ogTitle: Vindicta Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
vindicta.goal: Play behind your teammates, deal steady ranged gun damage, and use Assassinate to help finish wounded enemies. Stay involved in the fight without becoming an easy close-range target.
vindicta.positioning: Choose a clear firing angle with cover and a route back towards allied protection. Flight can let you shoot over an obstacle, but also exposes you to other sightlines. Reposition before a close attacker reaches your landing area instead of waiting until you are already trapped.
fight: Shoot reachable enemies occupied by your teammates. Stake helps restrict a target’s movement and can also slow an attacker’s approach to you. Keep dealing ordinary gun damage rather than spending the entire fight scoped in, searching for a low-health enemy somewhere else.

Use Crow Familiar as part of a useful damage exchange and look for an Assassinate finish once a target is wounded. Check nearby threats before aiming at a distant escape. A missed finish is less costly than losing your safe position and dying while ignoring someone next to you.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and shoot from cover behind your partner’s contact. Keep distance from close attackers instead of floating exposed for every exchange.
Mid game
Find useful firing angles near allied protection and maintain income. Help ongoing fights rather than travelling alone after every low-health enemy.
Late game
Keep ranged damage on reachable targets and look for Assassinate finishes. Watch side approaches while aiming, and move before someone reaches your landing area.
vindicta.threat: Move towards cover and allies, using Stake when it helps restrict pursuit. Do not assume being airborne makes a close attacker irrelevant or prevents other ranged enemies from shooting you.
strengths: Safe sightlines support repeated shooting behind allies.
Flight opens views blocked at ground level.
Assassinate rewards useful follow-up on damaged enemies.
weaknesses: Close attackers
Reaching her position disrupts safe aiming.
Airborne exposure
Flight opens enemy sightlines as well as her own.
Tunnel vision
Distant finishes can distract from an approaching threat.
matchups: He must reach close range and a useful wall angle to threaten you.
Keep ranged pressure from cover and reposition early; avoid allowing his approach to trap your landing beside a wall.
He can reach an aerial or elevated angle you assumed was protected.
Watch above the fight and keep a route towards allies before focusing on a distant Assassinate finish.
An isolated firing position gives her a control-and-gun opening.
Stay within allied help and move when she is missing nearby, rather than aiming from the same exposed location.
vindicta.struggling: Use safe gunfire and a supported Stake rather than crossing the map for a risky finish.
vindicta.tip: Flight exposes you to other sightlines. Move before a close attacker reaches your landing area.
mistakes: A close attacker reaching your position while you aim elsewhere.
Assuming Flight protects you from other enemies’ gunfire.

Assassinate ignores Disarm — scope right through it.
Targets under 50% HP show a popup — trust the marker.

viscous.name: Viscous
viscous.title: How to Play Viscous in Deadlock | DIB
viscous.meta: Learn how to play Viscous in Deadlock: protecting teammates and disrupting enemies without losing allied support. Positioning, matchups, and game plan.
viscous.ogTitle: Viscous Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
viscous.goal: Deny the enemy’s most dangerous attack and help teammates keep a useful position. Add damage and disruption, but make sure your saves and punches help the team rather than interrupting it.
viscous.positioning: Stay beside or slightly behind allies where you can see who is being attacked. Keep cover available so you are not the easiest first target. For Puddle Punch, think about both the surface you use and where the target will move afterwards.
fight: Use Splatter to threaten an approach or retreat route, then add gunfire when safe. The Cube can protect an ally during serious danger, but it temporarily stops them acting too. Save it for a meaningful commitment rather than cubing every teammate who takes a small hit.

Puddle Punch can create an opening, defend a retreat or move a threat away; careless placement can also save an enemy from allied shots. Goo Ball can disrupt enemies already committed nearby, but avoid rolling so far away that you abandon the teammate who needs protection.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and use safe Splatter pressure. Preserve protection for a serious attack rather than stopping your partner’s actions for minor damage.
Mid game
Stay near useful fights and check where your punches will move targets. Protect teammates without becoming an isolated easy target yourself.
Late game
Deny the enemy’s dangerous commitment, then help your ally survive the release. Use disruption that supports the fight rather than moving everyone unpredictably.
viscous.threat: Use your defensive option and nearby allies to survive, then plan what happens after protection ends. Temporarily avoiding damage is not enough if enemies remain around the same exit with every attack ready.
strengths: Cube can waste an enemy’s dangerous commitment.
Punch placement can create an opening or protect a retreat.
Slowing ground makes approaches and escapes less comfortable.
weaknesses: Save interference
Cube temporarily stops an ally acting too.
Bad displacement
A punch can move enemies out of allied damage.
Poor release position
A temporary save may end inside continuing danger.
matchups: A committed shooting window creates a clear dangerous moment for an ally.
Cube the seriously threatened teammate when it prevents meaningful damage, then help them reach safety after release.
Predictable close punches and a wall catch can force an awkward defensive save.
Keep a route away from the wall angle and use displacement deliberately; do not remain close after the safe exchange ends.
A wall and prepared shooting position can make an uncontrolled roll or punch harmful.
Choose disruption that preserves allied access, rather than moving a target away from teammates trying to damage it.
viscous.struggling: Protect a productive teammate and control routes rather than trying to start every fight alone.
viscous.tip: The Cube also stops an ally acting temporarily. Use it to prevent real danger, not every small hit.
mistakes: Stopping a teammate’s useful attack with an unnecessary Cube.
Punching a target somewhere that helps the enemy.

The Cube doesn't interrupt channels — save channeling allies freely.
Self-Cube during Goo Ball preserves momentum; canceling reverses it.

vyper.name: Vyper
vyper.title: How to Play Vyper in Deadlock | DIB
vyper.meta: Learn how to play Vyper in Deadlock: staying mobile and choosing close-range gun fights you can maintain. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
vyper.ogTitle: Vyper Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
vyper.goal: Keep close gun pressure on a reachable enemy while using movement to avoid becoming an easy target. Your speed should preserve a useful fight, not carry you blindly into several opponents.
vyper.positioning: Play around a side of the fight with nearby allies and a slide route you understand. Stay close enough for useful gun damage without cutting yourself off from a retreat. Practise the terrain first: moving quickly is not helpful if the destination is exposed or blocked.
fight: Use Slither-supported movement to maintain a favourable distance while shooting. Screwjab Dagger helps keep contact and adds pressure on the same target. Look for an enemy distracted by teammates rather than sliding directly into someone waiting with control that can stop your movement.

Lethal Venom is more threatening against wounded targets, so connect ordinary damage before expecting a finish. Petrifying Bola changes damage timing: ordinary shots cannot hurt the petrified target, while Lethal Venom can. Coordinate that window instead of making teammates waste their attacks.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and practise safe slide routes before forcing close fights. Use short gun exchanges without moving into several ready enemies.
Mid game
Maintain income, then approach a reachable target from the side with allies nearby. Avoid entering first into control that stops your movement.
Late game
Keep close shooting active while managing escape routes. Use venom and petrification deliberately so the team does not waste ordinary shots into protection.
vyper.threat: Move back towards allied help before enemy control lands. If slowed or knocked up, prioritise getting out of focus rather than assuming another slide will immediately restore a safe position.
strengths: Slides help sustain close damage while changing position.
Daggers help pressure the same reachable target.
Venom adds a finishing threat after ordinary damage.
weaknesses: Movement interruption
Slows and knock-ups undermine her intended rhythm.
Distant targets
Open ranged fights deny her preferred close gunfire.
Damage timing
Petrification can block the team’s ordinary attacks on the target.
matchups: Maintained beam contact interferes with movement and a sustained gun exchange.
Break the sightline with cover and re-enter from another angle rather than trying to slide through his pressure indefinitely.
A close hold denies the movement your fighting plan depends on.
Wait for their attention to turn elsewhere and keep allied help nearby before entering close gun range.
A distracted ranged position may offer a covered route into useful gun distance.
Check traps and backup first, then keep a retreat route instead of sliding straight through the firing line.
vyper.struggling: Collect safe souls and attack after enemy control is occupied instead of sliding in first.
vyper.tip: Ordinary shots cannot damage a petrified target; Lethal Venom is the important exception. Coordinate team damage around that protection.
mistakes: Being slowed or knocked up while relying on movement.
Shooting into petrification instead of coordinating your damage.
proTips: Lethal Venom ignores petrify's damage block — inject before you bola.
Her gun's recoil fires in an octagon; burst-fire to stay accurate.
Slither loses no speed sliding uphill — use slopes to escape.

warden.name: Warden
warden.title: How to Play Warden in Deadlock | DIB
warden.meta: Learn how to play Warden in Deadlock: catching enemies and choosing when to move into close range. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
warden.ogTitle: Warden Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
warden.goal: Weaken a shooting exchange, catch an enemy who cannot easily leave, and move into a close fight your team can join. Your catch and ultimate both need timing rather than blind forward movement.
warden.positioning: Play near your team’s front edge using corners to approach. Stay close enough to threaten an enemy, but prepare Last Stand from cover instead of in view of a ready interrupter. Keep teammates within reach so a caught target becomes useful allied damage.
fight: Alchemical Flask helps weaken the target and makes escaping Binding Word more difficult. Watch for an enemy who has already spent movement or is occupied by your teammate. Binding Word is delayed, so keep pressure on their route rather than assuming the cast instantly stops them.

Use Willpower to reach a useful distance or leave a poor exchange. Prepare Last Stand before committing into a close group, and keep your team’s position in mind. If enemies spread out or your allies retreat, do not keep walking deeper simply because your strongest fighting tool is active.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and watch enemies spend movement before trying Binding Word. Use Flask to support the exchange instead of assuming the catch is instant.
Mid game
Approach with an ally who can shoot your target. Prepare a close fight from cover rather than crossing a long exposed sightline.
Late game
Start Last Stand from a protected position and advance with support. Turn back if your damage dealer needs help or enemies leave useful range.
warden.threat: Use your remaining movement, protection and cover to return towards allies. Against a distant gunner, cut off a route or wait for support instead of chasing through open shots without reaching useful range.
strengths: Flask reduces the threat of a useful enemy response.
Binding Word punishes poor escape timing.
A prepared ultimate supports a committed nearby exchange.
weaknesses: Avoided catches
Ready movement can escape a delayed trap.
Interrupted preparation
A visible ultimate windup gives enemies an opening.
Long-range pressure
Distant enemies punish approaching through open ground.
matchups: A gun exchange can become more manageable after Flask connects.
Apply pressure when her escape movement is spent, but do not stand exposed long enough to feed unlimited focused fire.
Ranged aerial pressure can avoid your useful catch distance.
Use cover and maintain souls until a reachable opening appears rather than crossing open fire for a low-probability catch.
Ready nearby control threatens your visible Last Stand preparation.
Prepare from cover and track his position before advancing; do not rely on getting the windup for free.
warden.struggling: Use catches and weaker enemy gunfire to help your damage dealer instead of charging alone.
warden.tip: Binding Word is a delayed catch, not an instant stun. Do not assume the target is trapped when you cast it.

Preparing Last Stand in view of an enemy ready to interrupt it.

wraith.name: Wraith
wraith.title: How to Play Wraith in Deadlock | DIB
wraith.meta: Learn how to play Wraith in Deadlock: choosing duels and turning isolated targets into useful picks. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
wraith.ogTitle: Wraith Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
wraith.goal: Create a short favourable fight against an exposed enemy, using gunfire, cards and control together. Keep enough positioning freedom to survive after the enemy’s teammates notice you.
wraith.positioning: Play beside your team or along a covered side route where you can reach a target without a desperate teleport. Before using Project Mind aggressively, check the destination and nearby enemy backup. Keeping it available often makes a normal shooting position much safer.
fight: Gunfire builds Card Trick attacks, so keep shooting useful targets instead of waiting only for an ability combination. Add cards during a clear damage opportunity. Look for an enemy separated from help or already occupied, then use Telekinesis while allies can also contribute.

Once the target is controlled, use your gun and available cards to make the window count. If the enemy has a defensive tool that avoids the catch, choose another target or wait until they use it. Do not repeat an identical failed commitment while ignoring their items.
phases: Early game
Collect souls, build cards through gunfire and preserve a safe teleport. Avoid using movement just to force unnecessary early damage.
Mid game
Look for a reachable exposed enemy and check nearby backup. Use a successful catch to help push a lane instead of constantly searching for another duel.
Late game
Use Telekinesis with allied damage ready and keep shooting. Change targets or wait when enemy defensive tools repeatedly avoid your catch.
wraith.threat: Use Project Mind towards a genuinely safer position and return to allies. If it is unavailable, shorten your exposure and avoid wandering alone where an enemy can force a close fight from several directions.
strengths: A short controlled exchange supports concentrated shooting.
Control plus a reserved teleport helps manage a duel.
weaknesses: Defensive answers
Enemy tools can avoid the planned control window.
Spent teleport
Aggressive entry can remove the safest exit.
Protected targets
Backup can punish a duel before she finishes it.
matchups: An isolated aiming position can expose a short catch-and-gun window.
Approach through cover, check the trap route and use Telekinesis with a safe exit still available.
A protective hold can stop your shooting commitment after aggressive movement.
Avoid teleporting directly beside them while they wait; choose another angle or target with allied help.
Cube can protect the target during your intended damage window.
Track whether the save is available and avoid spending every tool before Viscous commits it or becomes unable to help.
wraith.struggling: Collect safe income and help a teammate attack a controlled target instead of gambling on a solo teleport.
wraith.tip: Before repeating the same catch, check whether the enemy has bought or used a tool that avoids it.

Repeating a catch into enemy defensive tools that already stopped it.

Activating T3 Full Auto mid-reload finishes the reload instantly.

yamato.name: Yamato
yamato.title: How to Play Yamato in Deadlock | DIB
yamato.meta: Learn how to play Yamato in Deadlock: choosing a target and planning your commitment before diving in. Get positioning tips and an early, mid, and late game plan.
yamato.ogTitle: Yamato Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
yamato.goal: Use deliberate spell damage to prepare a target, then commit at close range during a strong fighting window. You want a reachable enemy and an exit, not an endless dive through the whole team.
yamato.positioning: Play around a covered side or front edge of your team. Power Slash can pressure before you commit, while Flying Slash brings you closer and changes your escape options. Check where the enemy’s teammates are before following a target into their protection.
fight: Take Power Slash opportunities while the enemy is distracted or moving predictably. Follow with close attacks and Crimson Slash when the exchange is safe. Use Flying Slash to reach a target your team can help attack rather than simply whichever enemy is farthest away.

Shadow Transformation refreshes your fighting tools and gives you a stronger commitment window, but does not make you impossible to kill. Plan your attacks and return route before activating it. Watch its remaining duration instead of continuing deeper because a wounded enemy is still visible.
phases: Early game
Collect souls and take covered Power Slash opportunities. Preserve health and avoid grappling into a protected target just because they are in range.
Mid game
Look for a reachable enemy whose escape or attention is occupied. Commit near allies with a plan for when your protection ends.
Late game
Use your strong window for a useful close attack, then leave before it expires. Do not assume transformation prevents death or guarantees a safe chase.
yamato.threat: Move back towards allies and cover before your strong window ends. If your protection is unavailable or enemies are waiting to stop your approach, keep using safer damage until another player creates an opening.
strengths: Power Slash threatens before a full commitment.
Grapple reaches a useful close-range opportunity.
Transformation refreshes tools and strengthens a deliberate attack.
weaknesses: Unsafe entry
Grappling into protection can leave her surrounded.
Expired protection
Staying after the strong window makes retreat harder.
Distant control
Enemies denying contact can waste her commitment.
matchups: A distracted ranged shooter can be vulnerable to a timely close approach.
Use cover and grapple only when the destination is reachable by allies; preserve your strong window for the actual fight.
A close finishing attempt can give her the reversal range she wants.
Account for Soul Exchange before following her low health, and keep a route back instead of committing every tool.
Their close control threatens an entry before your strong defensive window is established.
Track their position and avoid a blind grapple beside them; wait for allied pressure to create an opening.
yamato.struggling: Use safe spell damage and join an existing fight rather than forcing a dive without protection.
yamato.tip: Shadow Transformation is a strong fighting window, not death prevention. Have a way to leave when it ends.
mistakes: Staying surrounded after your strong defensive window ends.
Assuming transformation makes you impossible to kill.
proTips: Power Slash deals 30%/50%/100% at blue, red, and max charge stages.
Dash before charging Power Slash to offset the 1.3 m/s crawl.
Alt-fire works even without enough ammo in the clip.

violet.name: Violet
violet.title: How to Play Violet in Deadlock | DIB
violet.meta: Learn how to play Violet in Deadlock: positioning behind allies, using ink to control space, and following up with Still Life. A beginner game plan and matchup tips.
violet.ogTitle: Violet Guide: How to Play in Deadlock
violet.goal: Play behind an ally who can take the first contact. Land empowered Living Ink shots and brush damage on distracted enemies, then use Still Life when you can keep the target in view. Use ink to help your team hold a useful area.
violet.positioning: Stay behind or beside your first-contact teammate, close enough to follow their attack. Keep a clear view of the target and nearby cover for yourself. Avoid drawing a wall across your team’s firing line or only retreat route.
fight: Follow your teammate’s pressure. Aim Living Ink shots and Flow State through the enemy’s route; successful empowered hero hits help bring your cooldowns back sooner.
Use Still Life on a visible target already occupied by your team. Keep aiming at them, but give up an unsafe angle rather than walking alone into the enemy team to finish a sketch.

Place Abstract Landscape where allies can use its Spirit Power and enemies must contest the area. Watch its edge: an enemy leaving takes damage, silence and slow. It is an area commitment, not a guaranteed trap.

Work with an ally who can start fights or hold a target in view. Violet provides ranged pressure, control and team buffs; she does not replace a durable first-contact hero or every kind of teammate save.
phases: Early game
Secure trooper souls from a covered angle. Trade with empowered shots when enemies pause to farm; look for Still Life while your lane partner distracts them. Keep movement for the return attack.
Mid game
Move with a teammate and fight around useful routes. Follow their opening with damage and control, then collect safe waves between fights instead of chasing every sketch.
Late game
Set up behind your team before an objective fight. Place the ultimate where allies can actually fight, keep walls clear of friendly routes, and reposition if an enemy reaches your angle.
violet.threat: Retreat toward teammates and cover. A drawn stroke can restrict a route, but also blocks projectiles and can be broken with heavy melee. Do not rely on a wall as an invulnerable escape or keep chasing a sketch while isolated.
strengths: Drawn strokes and the ultimate change available routes.
Flow State improves allied sliding; the ultimate grants Spirit Power.
weaknesses: Broken sight
Cover makes sustained Still Life pressure harder.
Close pressure
An enemy reaching your angle can force you to retreat.
Poor placement
Walls can obstruct friendly movement and fire.
matchups: He needs close access to pressure you.
Use ranged pressure behind your partner and move before he closes. Avoid standing beside an easy charge pin.
A clean Hook can pull you out of your protected angle.
Use existing solid cover against the hook angle and keep your partner in help range; do not count on a freshly drawn stroke to block Hook.
He can reach you from above the front line.
Watch his approach from height and move toward allies before he lands; do not focus on finishing Still Life while ignoring the dive.
violet.struggling: Farm safe waves near allies and contribute damage and control to their fights. Stop forcing isolated sketches or starting fights from the front.
violet.tip: A safe follow-up that helps your team is better than finishing a sketch from a position where you die.
mistakes: Walking past teammates to maintain Still Life.
Drawing a stroke across your own team’s route or firing line.
Using the ultimate where allies cannot help contest the area.
proTips: Use drawn strokes deliberately: they block projectiles as well as movement.
Collect a completed sketch when safe; finishing Still Life alone does not grant its collectible reward.
Track your ultimate upgrade: its final upgrade lets the ink persist after an enemy leaves.

Expect different defensive responses: enemies may reduce status duration, gain protection after control or prepare control immunity. Watch which response has been used before committing more resources.
